name: Psalms
sourceNote: Written freshly, thought for thought, from the oldest Hebrew, Greek, and Aramaic witnesses (the Masoretic Text with the Dead Sea Scrolls, the Septuagint, and the Samaritan Pentateuch). © 2026 Jose Santiago. All rights reserved.

verses.text:
Happy is the person{a}
who ignores the advice of wicked people,
never lingers on the path of sinners,
and never takes a seat among scoffers.

Instead, he loves the teaching{b} of Yahweh,
and he thinks about it{c} day and night.

He is like a tree set beside running water.
It bears fruit when its time comes,
and its leaves never dry up.
Whatever he does turns out well.

Not so the wicked!
They are like husks blown off by the wind.

So the wicked will not hold up when God judges,
and sinners will have no place among the good.

Yahweh watches over the way of the good,
but the way of the wicked will end in ruin.

notes.text: The Hebrew word, ashre, means “how happy is.” It begins Psalm 1 and ends Psalm 2 (2:12), so the two psalms work together as the doorway to the whole book. “The person” means anyone who lives this way.
Hebrew torah, meaning “teaching.” It is God’s whole message, not only his commands.
Hebrew hagah, which means to say quietly to oneself, reading aloud and thinking it over.

verses.text:
Why are the nations in an uproar?{a}
Why do the peoples make plans that come to nothing?

They say, “Let’s snap their chains
and throw off their ropes!”

The One who is seated in heaven laughs.
The Lord{c} pokes fun at them.

Then his anger bursts out and he speaks.
His fury fills them with terror:

“I have already put my own king
on Zion, my holy hill.”

Just ask, and I will hand you the nations.
The whole earth, to its far corners, will belong to you.

With an iron rod{e} you will crush them.
Like a clay pot, you will break them in pieces.”

So now, you kings, show some sense.
Take warning, you rulers of the earth.

Serve Yahweh with respect.
Celebrate, but with a shiver of awe.

Honor the son,{f} or he may become angry, and you will be lost on the road,
for his anger can flare up fast.
Happy are all who run to him for safety.

notes.text: Or “gather in noise.” Acts 4:25–26 quotes verses 1–2 from the Greek.

Original: “his anointed one” (Hebrew mashiach), a king poured with oil at his start. It is the word that “Messiah” comes from. The New Testament reads this psalm about Christ (Acts 13:33; Hebrews 1:5; 5:5).
Hebrew Adonai, “Lord,” a title for God that is different from the name Yahweh. It is written “Lord” throughout this book.
Original: “I have fathered you.” This is how a king’s crowning as God’s son was announced (compare 2 Samuel 7:14).
The Septuagint has “shepherd them with an iron rod” (the same Hebrew letters read with other vowels). Revelation 2:27, 12:5, and 19:15 use this form.

The Hebrew is hard. “Son” here is the Aramaic word bar (verse 7 has the Hebrew ben). Some read “Kiss purely” or “Worship in purity.” The Septuagint has “Take hold of instruction.” Kissing a king’s hand or feet showed that you obeyed him.

verses.text:
Yahweh, how many enemies I have!
Crowds are rising up against me.

But you, Yahweh, are a shield around me.
You are my pride, and you hold my head up.

I call out loud to Yahweh,
and from his holy hill he answers me.
Selah

I lay down to sleep, and I woke again,
because Yahweh holds me up.

I will not be afraid of tens of thousands
who have lined up around me against me.

Rise up, Yahweh! Save me, my God!
You have hit all my enemies across the face.
You have knocked out the teeth of the wicked.

Rescue comes from Yahweh.
May your blessing rest on your people!
Selah

notes.text: See 2 Samuel 15–18. In the Hebrew Bible, a psalm’s title counts as verse 1 or verses 1–2. So the Hebrew verse numbers of psalms with titles are usually one or two higher than the verse numbers here.
“Selah” appears 71 times in the Psalms. No one knows what it means for sure. It is probably a music direction, such as a pause or a louder part. The Septuagint renders it “interlude.”

chapters.title: A psalm of David, written when he ran away from his son Absalom.{a}

verses.text:
You people of rank,{c} how long will you drag my good name through the mud?
How long will you chase after empty things and lies?
Selah

Know this: Yahweh has set the faithful one{d} apart as his own.
When I call, Yahweh listens.

Shake with awe,{e} and do not sin.
Think it over on your beds, and be quiet.
Selah

Offer the right kind of sacrifices,
and trust in Yahweh.

Many are asking, “Who can show us what is good?”
Yahweh, make your face shine down on us.

You have filled my heart with more joy
than the joy of a full harvest of grain and wine.

I will lie down and fall asleep in peace,
for you alone, Yahweh, let me live without fear.

notes.text: Hebrew lamnatseach, “for the director” (it begins 55 psalms), and neginot, “stringed instruments.” The Septuagint takes the first word to mean “for the end.”
Original: “you made room for me.”
Hebrew bene ish, which may mean people of high standing. Or “you sons of men.”
Hebrew chasid, someone loyal to God in his faithful love (chesed).
Or “Be angry.” The Septuagint says “Be angry, and do not sin.” Paul quotes it in Ephesians 4:26.

chapters.title: For the choir director: with stringed instruments.{a} A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Yahweh, give my words a hearing.
Take note of my groaning.{b}

My King and my God, hear me calling for help,
for it is to you alone that I pray.

Yahweh, at sunrise you hear my voice.
At sunrise I lay out my case for you{c} and wait.

You are not a God who enjoys evil.
Wrong has no place to stay with you.

Proud people cannot stand before you.
You hate everyone who does harm.

You wipe out those who tell lies.
Yahweh is disgusted by killers and cheats.

But I, because your faithful love{d} is so great,
will enter your house.
With deep respect I will bow toward your holy temple.

Yahweh, I have enemies who watch me.
Lead me in your goodness,
and make the road straight ahead of me.

Nothing they say can be trusted.
Their insides are full of destruction.
Their throats are open graves.
Their tongues flatter and fool.{e}

Declare them guilty, God!
Let their own plots trip them up.
Push them away, for they have sinned so much
and rebelled against you.

But let everyone who runs to you for safety be glad.
Let them sing for joy forever. Protect them,
so that those who love your name may celebrate in you.

Yahweh, you bless those who do right.
You wrap them in your favor like a shield.

notes.text: Hebrew nechilot, probably “flutes.” This is uncertain.
Or “my murmuring” or “my thinking.”
Or “I get a sacrifice ready for you.” The verb is used for laying out an offering or lining up words.
Hebrew chesed, God’s loyal love that keeps his promises. It is a key word in the Psalms (about 130 times). This book says “faithful love.”
Paul quotes this line in Romans 3:13.

chapters.title: For the choir director: for flutes.{a} A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Yahweh, do not scold me in your anger,
or discipline me in your rage.

Be kind to me, Yahweh, for I am wasting away.
Heal me, Yahweh, for my bones shake.

My soul is trembling too.
But you, Yahweh, how long will it be?

Come back, Yahweh, and rescue my life.
Save me, because you are always loyal in love.

In death no one remembers you.
Down in the grave,{b} who can praise you?

I am worn out from groaning.
All night long I drench my bed.
My tears soak my mattress.

My eyes are weak from grief.
They have grown old because of my enemies.

Leave me, all you evildoers,
for Yahweh has heard me sobbing.

Yahweh has heard my cry for mercy.
Yahweh accepts my prayer.

All my enemies will be ashamed and badly shaken.
They will retreat, and in a moment they will be put to shame.

notes.text: Hebrew al-hasheminit, perhaps an eight-stringed instrument or a lower pitch. This is uncertain. This is the first of seven psalms long called the Penitential Psalms (6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, 143).
Original: Sheol, the Hebrew name for the place of the dead.

chapters.title: For the choir director: with stringed instruments, on the eighth.{a} A psalm of David.

subheads.1: A Prayer of the Sick and Sorry

verses.text:
Yahweh my God, I run to you for safety.
Save me from everyone who chases me, and set me free.

Otherwise, like a lion, they will rip me apart,
and carry me off with no one to save me.

Yahweh my God, if I have done what they say,
if my hands are guilty of any wrong,

if I have paid back evil to a friend,
or robbed my enemy for no reason,

then let my enemy hunt me down and catch me.
Let him stamp my life into the ground
and leave my honor lying in the dirt.
Selah

Get up, Yahweh, in your anger!
Rise against the fury of my enemies.
Wake up for me!{c} You have called for justice.

Let the nations gather around you,
and from above them take your seat.

Yahweh judges the peoples.
Judge me, Yahweh, by my goodness,
and by the innocence that is mine.

Bring the evil of the wicked to an end,
and make the good secure.
You search minds and hearts,{d} God of justice.

God is the shield over me.
He saves those with honest hearts.

God is a fair judge.
Every day he shows his anger at evil.

If a person will not turn around, God will sharpen his sword.
His bow is already bent and aimed.

He has gotten deadly weapons ready.
He has set his arrows on fire.

See how the wicked man is pregnant with evil,
full of trouble, and gives birth to lies.

He digs a hole and makes it deep,
then falls into the pit he made.

The trouble he caused lands back on his own head.
His violence drops onto his own skull.

I will thank Yahweh for being fair.
My song will honor the name of Yahweh Most High.{e}

notes.text: Hebrew shiggayon, a word of uncertain meaning. It may mean a sad song or a wild, emotional song (compare Habakkuk 3:1).
Nothing else is known of Cush. He may have been an ally of Saul from Saul’s tribe, Benjamin.
Or “Wake up, my God.” The Septuagint says “Wake up, Lord my God.”
Original: “hearts and kidneys,” the places of thought and deep feeling.
Hebrew Elyon, “Most High,” a title for God (compare Genesis 14:18–22).

chapters.title: A shiggaion{a} of David. He sang it to Yahweh about the words of Cush, a man of Benjamin.{b}

verses.text:
I look at your sky, made by your fingers,
at the moon and stars you put in place,

and I ask, what are humans, that you remember them?
What are mortals,{e} that you care for them?

You made them a little lower than the heavenly beings,{f}
and put glory and honor on their heads like a crown.

You made them rulers over what your hands made.
You set everything under their feet:

flocks and herds of every kind,
and the animals of the open country,

birds that fly and fish that swim,
whatever moves along the paths of the sea.

Yahweh, our Lord,
how glorious your name is over all the earth!

notes.text: Hebrew al-haggittit, perhaps an instrument or tune from Gath, or a song for the winepress. This is uncertain.
Here “Lord” is the Hebrew word adon, “master,” an everyday word for a lord, used here for God.
The Hebrew of this line is hard. It may be “you who set your splendor above the heavens.”
The Septuagint says “you have prepared praise.” Matthew 21:16 quotes it this way.
Hebrew enosh and ben adam are both words for human beings. Hebrews 2:6–8 applies verses 4–6 to Jesus.
Hebrew elohim can mean God or heavenly beings. The Septuagint says “angels,” as Hebrews 2:7 quotes it.

chapters.title: For the choir director: on the gittith.{a} A psalm of David.

verses.text:
I will praise Yahweh with every part of my heart.
I will tell about every wonder you have done.

I will rejoice and cheer because of you.
I will make music to your name, God Most High.

My enemies back away,
stumble, and are destroyed in your presence.

You took my side and defended my case.
You sit on your throne as a fair judge.

You scolded the nations and wiped out the wicked.
You erased their names for all time.

The enemy is finished, left in ruins for good.
You pulled up their cities by the roots,
and even their memory has faded.

But Yahweh sits as King forever.
He has built his throne for judging.

He will judge the world with fairness.
He will rule the peoples with honesty.

Yahweh is a high safe place for the beaten down,
a high safe place in times of trouble.

Those who know your name trust you,
for you, Yahweh, never leave those who look for you.

Make music for Yahweh, who lives on Zion!
Announce his deeds among the peoples!

He, who pays back for spilled blood, has not forgotten them.
He never ignores the cry of the poor.{b}

Show me mercy, Yahweh!
See how much my enemies make me suffer.
You lift me up from the gates of death,

The nations have dropped into the hole they dug.
Their own feet are tangled in the net they hid.

Yahweh has shown who he is by his justice.
The wicked are caught by what their own hands made.
Higgaion.{d} Selah

The wicked will go back to the grave,{e}
all the nations that forget God.

The needy will not be forgotten forever,
and the hope of the suffering{f} will not die for good.

Rise up, Yahweh! Do not let mere humans win.
Let the nations be judged in front of you.

Make them afraid, Yahweh.
Let the nations learn they are only men and women.
Selah

notes.text: Hebrew al-muth-labben, perhaps “on the death of the son.” It may be the name of a tune. This is uncertain. Psalms 9 and 10 together make one acrostic poem, each pair of verses starting with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet. The pattern is broken in places.
This follows the reading handed down by scribes. The written text says “the afflicted.” The two Hebrew words for “poor” and “humble” often swap places in the Psalms.
That is, Jerusalem, pictured as a young woman.
Hebrew higgayon, perhaps a musical pause or a quiet thinking time (compare 19:14; 92:3).
Original: Sheol, the place of the dead.
This follows the reading handed down by scribes. The written text says “the humble.”

chapters.title: For the choir director: on Muth-labben.{a} A psalm of David.

subheads.15: The Nations Fall in Their Own Pit

verses.text:
Why, Yahweh, are you standing far away?
Why do you hide when times are hard?

In their pride, the wicked chase after the poor.
May the poor be saved, and the wicked caught in their own plots.

The wicked man brags about what his heart craves.
He blesses{a} the greedy and insults Yahweh.

In his pride, the wicked man does not look for God.
His every plan says, “There is no God.”

His ventures always succeed.
Your judgments are far above him, out of sight.
He sneers at everyone who opposes him.

He tells himself, “Nothing will shake me.
No trouble will ever touch me or my children.”

His mouth is stuffed with curses, lies, and threats.{b}
Under his tongue lie trouble and harm.

He waits in ambush outside the villages.
In hidden spots he murders the innocent.
His eyes search for the helpless.

He hides like a lion in its den.
He waits to catch the poor.
He catches them and drags them off in his net.

He crouches low,
and the helpless fall under his weight.{c}

He tells himself, “God has forgotten.
He has covered his face. He will never look.”

Rise up, Yahweh! God, lift your hand!
Do not forget the weak.{d}

Why do the wicked turn away from God
and say to themselves, “You will not call me to account”?

But you do see. You watch trouble and grief
and take it into your hands.
The helpless leave themselves with you.
You have always been the helper of orphans.

Snap the arm of the evil wicked man.
Search out his wrongdoing until none remains.

Yahweh is King forever and ever.
The nations will vanish from his land.

Yahweh, you have heard the wish of the humble.
You will steady their hearts and listen closely to them,

to see that orphans and the beaten down get justice,
so that humans made of earth will never again spread terror.

notes.text: Or “he praises the greedy and insults Yahweh.” The Hebrew is uncertain. The word for “blesses” may be a polite way of writing “curses.”
Paul quotes this line in Romans 3:14.
The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain.
This follows the reading handed down by scribes. The written text says “the afflicted.”

verses.text:
Look, wicked men have bent their bows.
They aim arrows from the dark
at people whose hearts are honest.

If everything solid is knocked down,
what can good people do?

Yahweh is in his holy temple.
Yahweh sits on his throne in heaven.
His eyes watch, and he looks closely at every human being.

Yahweh tests the good.
He hates the wicked and everyone who loves violence.

He will pour down traps{c} on the wicked.
Fire, burning sulfur, and a scorching wind
will be what they get to drink.

Yahweh is fair, and he loves what is fair.
Honest people will see his face.

notes.text: The Hebrew word le- in psalm titles can mean “by,” “for,” or “belonging to.” It may point to the writer, a dedication, or a collection linked to David.
The standard Hebrew reading has “you” as singular. A note in the margin of the Hebrew copies says “you” is plural here.
Some read “hot coals” instead, with a small spelling change.

chapters.title: For the music director. By David.{a}

verses.text:
Help, Yahweh! Faithful people are gone.
Honest people have disappeared from the human family.

Everyone lies to the person next door.
They flatter with their lips and plan with a divided heart.

May Yahweh silence every flattering mouth
and the tongue that brags so loudly.

They say, “Our tongues will make us strong!
Our lips belong to us. Who can be our boss?”

Yahweh says, “The poor have been robbed, and the needy groan.
So now I will get up.
I will put them in the safety they long for.”

You, Yahweh, will keep us{c} safe.
You will guard us from these people always.

The wicked strut around on every side,
while lowlife behavior is praised among people.

notes.text: Hebrew “on the sheminith,” which means “the eighth.” It may be an eight-stringed instrument or a low pitch. No one is sure.
The meaning of these Hebrew words is uncertain.
Some Hebrew copies and the Septuagint say “us.” Other Hebrew copies say “them.”

chapters.title: For the music director, on the eight-stringed instrument.{a} A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Yahweh, are you going to forget me forever?
Until when will you hide your face?

How long must I wrestle with my thoughts,
with sadness in my heart every day?
How long will my enemy stand above me?

Look at me and answer, Yahweh my God.
Make my eyes bright again,
or I will fall asleep and never wake.

Then my enemy will boast, “I beat him!”
and my opponents will cheer when I fall.

But I have trusted your faithful love.
My heart will celebrate when you rescue me.

I will sing to Yahweh,
because he has been so good to me.

chapters.title: For the music director. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Fools{b} tell themselves, “There is no God.”
They are rotten and do disgusting things.
Not one of them does anything good.

Yahweh bends down to look from heaven at all of humanity.
He wants to see if anyone is wise,
if anyone is searching for God.

Don’t these evildoers know anything?
They swallow up my people as if they were bread,
and they never call on Yahweh.

They will shake with fear there,
because God is with the people who do right.

You laugh at the plans of the poor,
but Yahweh is their safe place.

If only Israel’s rescue would come from Zion!
When Yahweh brings his people back from their troubles,
Jacob will celebrate and Israel will be glad.

notes.text: Psalm 53 is almost the same as this one. It uses the word “God” (Elohim) where this psalm says “Yahweh.”
The Hebrew word nabal means someone with no moral sense, not just someone slow to learn. Compare Nabal in 1 Samuel 25:25.
Paul quotes verses 1–3 in Romans 3:10–12. Some copies of the Septuagint add the lines Paul quotes in Romans 3:13–18.

chapters.title: For the music director. By David.{a}

verses.text:
Yahweh, who gets to stay in your tent?
Who can settle on your holy mountain?

Whoever lives without blame and does what is right,
and tells the truth from the heart.

He never spreads lies about others.
He does his friend no harm
and does not pass on gossip about a neighbor.

He has no respect for people who are rotten,
but he honors those who fear Yahweh.
He keeps a promise even when it costs him.

notes.text: The law told Israelites not to charge interest to a poor fellow Israelite. See Exodus 22:25, Leviticus 25:35–37, and Deuteronomy 23:19–20.

chapters.title: A psalm of David.

verses.text: Keep me safe, God, because I run to you.

I{b} tell Yahweh, “You are my Lord.
Apart from you, I own nothing good.”

The holy ones who live in this land
are the noble people I take such delight in.{c}

People who rush after other gods will have more and more pain.
I will not pour out their blood offerings,
and I will not even say their names.

Yahweh, you are what I am given, my full cup.
My future is held in your hands.

My property lines fall in pleasant places.
What I inherited is lovely to me.

I thank Yahweh, who gives me advice.
Even at night my inner self teaches me.{d}

Yahweh is always before my eyes.
With him at my right side, nothing can knock me down.

That is why my heart is happy and my spirit{e} cheers.
Even my body will rest without worry.

You will not abandon my life to the grave.
You will not allow your devoted one to see the pit.{f}

You show me the road to life.
In your presence there is full joy.
At your right hand there is pleasure forever.

notes.text: The meaning of miktam is uncertain. It is in the titles of Psalms 16 and 56–60. It may mean “inscription.”
The Septuagint and some Hebrew copies say “I.” Most Hebrew copies say “you,” as if the writer is speaking to himself.
The Hebrew of verses 3–4 is hard to read, so the meaning is uncertain.
The Hebrew says “my kidneys,” which means the deepest part of a person.
Hebrew “my glory,” which may mean “my soul.” The Septuagint says “my tongue,” which Acts 2:26 quotes.
Some read “see decay.” The Septuagint says “decay.” Acts 2:27 and 13:35 use it for Jesus rising from the dead.

chapters.title: A miktam{a} of David.

verses.text:
Yahweh, listen to my honest plea.
Pay attention to my cry.
Hear my prayer, which comes from lips that do not lie.

Let my verdict come from you.
Your eyes can see what is fair.

You have searched my heart and looked into it at night.
You tested me and found nothing wrong.
I made up my mind not to speak badly.

When others do wrong, I follow what you have said.
I have stayed away from violent people.

My feet have stayed on your paths.
My steps have not slipped.

I am calling to you, God, since you give answers.
Bend down and listen to my words.

Show your amazing faithful love.
You save with your strong right hand
the people who run to you from their attackers.

Protect me as you would your own eyeball.{a}
Tuck me away in the shade of your wings,

away from the wicked who beat me down,
and from deadly enemies who circle me.

Their hearts have grown hard.{b}
Their mouths speak with pride.

They have followed our tracks and now surround us.
They watch for the chance to throw us down.

He is like a lion hungry to tear something apart,
like a young lion waiting in a hiding place.

Stand up, Yahweh! Meet him and knock him down!
Save my life from the wicked with your blade,

and by your hand from people of this world, Yahweh,
whose only reward is in this life.
You fill their stomachs with what you have saved up.{c}
Their children have plenty,
and they leave extra for their little ones.

But I, being innocent, will see your face.
When I wake up, seeing you will fill me with joy.

notes.text: Hebrew “the little man, the daughter of the eye.” It means the tiny picture of yourself you see in someone’s eye.
Hebrew “they have shut their fat.”
The meaning of this verse is uncertain. It may describe the punishment saved up for the wicked, or the good things God gives his own people.

chapters.title: A prayer of David.

verses.text: I love you, Yahweh. You make me strong.{b}

Yahweh is my rock, my fort, and my rescuer.
My God is the rock I hide behind.
He is my shield, my mighty horn,{c} and my high tower.

I called out to Yahweh, who deserves praise,
and he saved me from my enemies.

Ropes of death tied me up.
Floods of ruin{d} terrified me.

Cords of the grave wrapped around me.
Death set its traps in my path.

Trouble came, and I called on Yahweh.
I begged my God for help.
He heard me in his temple,
and my cry reached his ears.

The earth shook and rocked.
The bases of the mountains trembled,
because he was so angry.

Smoke came out of his nose.
Fire poured from his mouth,
and burning coals flew from it.

He pulled the sky down and stepped onto it.
Dark clouds lay under his feet.

He rode a winged creature and flew.
He swooped along on the wind.

He made darkness his hiding place.
Black storm clouds were a tent around him.

From the glow in front of him,
his thick clouds raced on,
with hail and burning coals.

He shot arrows and sent them scattering.{f}
He flung lightning and threw them into a panic.

Then the sea floor could be seen,
and the foundations of the world lay bare,
when you roared, Yahweh,
and blasted out your breath.

He stretched his hand down from the heights and took hold of me.
He lifted me out of the deep water.

He saved me from an enemy too strong for me,
from people who hated me and were stronger than I was.

They attacked me on my worst day,
but Yahweh held me up.

He led me out into a wide-open space.
He rescued me because he found joy in me.

Yahweh rewarded me for doing right.
He paid me back because my hands were clean.

I have followed the ways of Yahweh.
I never turned from my God to do evil.

I kept his rules in view at all times.
I never shoved his laws aside.

I was blameless in his eyes,
and I kept myself from doing wrong.

So Yahweh has repaid me for doing right,
because he saw that my hands were clean.

With the faithful, you are faithful.
With the blameless, you are fully good.

With the pure, you are pure.
With the crooked, you outsmart them.

You rescue people who are humble,
but you bring proud eyes down.

You are the one who keeps my lamp burning.
Yahweh my God makes my dark places bright.

With your help I can charge at an army.
With my God I can jump a wall.

This God’s way is perfect.
Yahweh’s word has proved true.
He is a shield for everyone who hides in him.

Who is God besides Yahweh?
Who is a rock besides our God?

God is the one who dresses me in strength
and makes my road safe.

He makes my feet quick like a deer’s.
He sets me firmly on the high places.

War skills come from him to my hands,
so even my arms can stretch a bronze bow.

You gave me your shield of victory.
Your right hand was under me,
and your gentleness{g} has made me great.

You gave my steps plenty of room,
so my ankles did not give way.

I ran after my enemies and caught them.
I did not come back until they were finished.

I hit them so hard they could not get up.
They fell down at my feet.

You dressed me in strength for battle.
You made my attackers bow down under me.

You made my enemies turn and run.
I destroyed the people who hated me.

They shouted for help, but no one came.
They even called to Yahweh, but he gave them no reply.

I crushed them as fine as dust in the wind.
I dumped them out like mud in the street.

You saved me when my own people fought me.
You put me at the head of nations.
Strangers I had never met have become my servants.

The moment they hear about me, they do what I say.
Foreigners cringe in front of me.

Foreigners lose heart.
They come trembling out of their forts.

Yahweh is alive! Praise be to my rock!
May God, my savior, be lifted high.

He is the God who pays back my enemies
and puts nations under me.

He sets me free from my enemies.
Yes, you raise me up above my attackers.
You rescue me from cruel men.

So I will thank you among the nations, Yahweh,
and I will sing songs about your name.{h}

He wins great victories for his king.
He is loyal and kind to the one he chose,
to David and all his descendants forever.

notes.text: This psalm is also in 2 Samuel 22, with many small differences.
This line is not in 2 Samuel 22.
A horn was the weapon and pride of a strong animal. Here it pictures strength and victory.
Hebrew beliyya’al, “worthlessness.” Here it may be a name for the world of the dead.
This line is missing in 2 Samuel 22:14, in some Hebrew copies, and in the Septuagint. It may be a repeat of verse 12.
The ones scattered are his enemies.
Or “your humility,” meaning your stooping down. In 2 Samuel 22:36 it reads “your answering.”
Paul quotes this verse in Romans 15:9.

chapters.title: For the music director. By David, Yahweh’s servant. He sang the words of this song to Yahweh on the day Yahweh saved him from all his enemies and from Saul.{a} He said:

verses.text:
The skies tell how glorious God is.
The wide dome{a} above shows off his handiwork.

One day pours out its message to the next.
One night passes its knowledge on to the following night.

They use no talking and no words.
Their voice cannot be heard.

Still, their message{b} reaches every corner of the earth,
and their news travels to the far end of the world.
God set up a home in the sky for the sun.

The sun comes out like a groom leaving his wedding room.
It runs its course with the joy of a champion.

It starts at one edge of the sky
and circles to the other edge.
Nothing hides from its heat.

Yahweh’s teaching is flawless. It brings the soul back to life.
Yahweh’s reminders can be trusted. They make simple people wise.

Yahweh’s orders are right. They fill the heart with joy.
Yahweh’s commands are clear. They give light to the eyes.

Respect for Yahweh is clean and never wears out.
Yahweh’s decisions are true. Every one of them is completely fair.

Gold cannot compare with them,
not even heaps of the purest gold.
Honey tastes less sweet,
even when it drips fresh from the comb.

Your servant is warned by them.
Following them brings a great reward.

Who can notice every one of his own mistakes?
Wipe away the faults I cannot see.

Hold your servant back from sins I choose to do.
Never let them be my masters.
Then I can stand blameless
and free of any great offense.

Let what I say and what I think inside
be pleasing to you,
Yahweh, my rock and the one who buys me back.

notes.text: Hebrew raqia’, the solid dome of the sky in Genesis 1:6–8.
Or “their sound.” The Septuagint has “their sound,” which Romans 10:18 quotes.

chapters.title: For the music director. A psalm of David.

subheads.12: A Prayer for a Clean Heart

verses.text:
May Yahweh answer you when trouble comes.
May the name of Jacob’s God keep you safe.

May he send help to you from his holy place,
and hold you up from Zion.

May he keep in mind every present you gave
and accept your burnt sacrifice.
Selah

May he give you what your heart wants,
and bring all your plans to pass.

When you win, we will shout for joy.
In our God’s name we will lift our banners.
May Yahweh give you every request.

Now I am sure that Yahweh rescues the king he chose.
He will answer from his holy heaven
with the winning power of his right hand.

Some count on chariots and some on horses,
but we count on the name of Yahweh our God.

They stumble and fall,
but we rise and stand strong.

Yahweh, give the king victory!{a}
Answer us on the day we call.

notes.text: Following the Septuagint, this may read, “Yahweh, give the king victory, and answer us on the day we call.”

chapters.title: For the music director. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Yahweh, the king is happy because you made him strong.
He is thrilled with the victories you give!{a}

You gave him the wish of his heart.
You did not refuse what his lips asked for.
Selah

You met him with good gifts,
and put a crown of fine gold on his head.

He requested life, and you handed it over,
a length of days with no end.

Your rescue made him famous.
You covered him with splendor and royal dignity.

You made him a blessing for all time.
You filled him with joy by being near him.

The king trusts in Yahweh.
Because of the Most High’s faithful love, he will never fall.

Your hand will hunt down all your enemies.
Your right hand will catch everyone who hates you.

You will wipe their children off the earth
and their families from the human race.

They may plot evil against you
and think up schemes, but they will fail.

You will make them turn and run.
You will point your bows at their faces.

Rise high, Yahweh, in your power!
We will sing and play music about your strength.

notes.text: Some Hebrew copies read “victories” with a different spelling.
Hebrew “at the time of your face.”

chapters.title: For the music director. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
My God, I call all day, and you give no answer.
I call all night and cannot rest.

But you are holy.
You sit enthroned where Israel sings your praise.

Our ancestors put their trust in you.
They trusted, and you rescued them.

They called out to you and got away.
They trusted you and were not let down.

But I am a worm, not a man.
People look down on me and everyone hates me.

Everyone who looks at me laughs.
They curl their lips and wag their heads.

It was you who drew me out at birth.
You gave me peace at her breast.

I was placed in your care from the day I was born.{e}
Since before I was born, you have been my God.

Do not stay far from me, since trouble is near
and no one else will help.

Many bulls are circling me.
Strong bulls from Bashan{f} have closed in.

They open their mouths wide at me,
like lions that rip and roar.

My strength drains out like water.
All my bones are out of place.
My heart has turned to wax
and melted inside me.{g}

My power is baked dry like a cracked clay dish.
My tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth.
You have put me in the dirt where the dead lie.

I can count every bone in my body.
They stare at me and gloat.

They share out my clothes among themselves
and throw dice for my robe.{i}

But you, Yahweh, please do not stay away.
You are my strength. Hurry to help me!

Rescue my life from the sword.
Save my precious life{j} from the dogs’ power.

Save me out of the lion’s mouth.
You have answered me, even from the horns of wild bulls.{k}

I will tell my relatives who you are.
Right in the congregation, I will sing your praise.{l}

You who fear Yahweh, praise him!
All of Jacob’s children, honor him.
All of Israel’s children, stand in awe of him.

He has not looked down on those in pain,
and he has not hated their suffering.
He has not hidden his face from them.
He listened when they called to him for help.

In the great gathering, my praise will be for you.
Before those who fear him, I will keep my promises.

The poor will eat their fill.
Those who search for Yahweh will give him praise.
May your hearts live on and on.

People from every end of the earth will remember and turn to Yahweh.
Every nation’s families will bow before you.{m}

The kingdom belongs to Yahweh.
He is ruler over the nations.

Their children will serve him.
People will tell the next generation about the Lord.{o}

They will come and announce his goodness
to a people not yet born.
They will say, “He did it!”

notes.text: Hebrew ‘ayyelet hashshachar, probably the name of a tune.
Jesus cried out these words on the cross in Aramaic. See Matthew 27:46 and Mark 15:34.
Hebrew “my roaring.”
Hebrew “Roll it onto Yahweh,” which means hand your troubles to him. Compare Matthew 27:43.
Hebrew “from the womb.”
Bashan was the rich grassland east of the Sea of Galilee. It was famous for cattle. See Amos 4:1.
Hebrew “inside my bowels.”

Some Hebrew copies, the Septuagint (“they dug”), the Syriac, and Jerome have this reading. A Dead Sea Scroll from Nahal Hever has a word that may mean “they dug.” The common Hebrew text has a word that means “like a lion.”
See John 19:24 and Matthew 27:35.
Hebrew “my only one,” meaning my one precious life.
The sudden “you have answered me” is where the psalm turns from sorrow to praise. The Septuagint says, “and save my lowly self from the horns of the unicorns.”
Hebrews 2:12 quotes this verse.
Most Hebrew copies say “before you.” Some Hebrew copies, the Septuagint, and the Syriac say “before him.”
The Hebrew of this verse is hard. The word for “wealthy” literally means “fat ones.”
Or “to the next generation.” With the Septuagint, the Hebrew may be read, “and my children will serve him.”

chapters.title: For the music director, to the tune “Deer of the Dawn.”{a} A psalm of David.

subheads.9: You Have Been With Me Since Birth
subheads.25: All the Earth Will Turn to Yahweh

verses.text:
Yahweh is the shepherd who looks after me.
I will never lack anything.

He makes me lie down in meadows of fresh grass.
He leads me to quiet pools.{a}

You set out a feast for me
while my enemies look on.
You pour oil on my head.
My cup spills over.

Surely goodness and faithful love will chase after me
through all my days,
and I will make my home{d} in Yahweh’s house
as long as I live.

notes.text: Hebrew “waters of rest.”
Or “paths of what is right.”
Or “the valley of the shadow of death.” The Hebrew word tsalmavet was read as “death’s shadow” by old translators. Many scholars read it as “deep darkness.”
The Septuagint says “I will live.” The Hebrew vowels say “I will return to.”

chapters.title: A psalm of David.

verses.text:
The earth belongs to Yahweh, along with all it holds,
the world and the people living in it.

He built it on top of the seas
and anchored it over the rivers.

Who may go up Yahweh’s mountain?
Who may stand in his holy place?

Anyone whose hands are clean and whose heart is pure,
who has not set his heart{a} on what is false
and has not made lying promises.

That person will receive a blessing from Yahweh,
and will be declared right by the God who saves him.

Gates, lift your heads high!
Ancient doors, swing wide open!
The glorious King is coming in.

Who is this glorious King?
He is Yahweh, strong and mighty.
Yahweh, the hero of battle.

Gates, lift your heads high!
Ancient doors, swing wide open!
The glorious King is coming in.

Who then is this glorious King?
Yahweh of Armies{d}
is the glorious King!
Selah

notes.text: Hebrew “his soul.” Some copies say “my soul,” as if to say, has not misused my name. Compare Exodus 20:7.
Many copies read “those who seek him” in the plural. Others have the singular.
The Septuagint and the Syriac say “God of Jacob.” The Hebrew has only “Jacob.”
Hebrew YHWH tsebaot, often rendered “the LORD of hosts.” The “armies” are the heavenly hosts of angels and stars, and the armies of Israel.

chapters.title: By David. A psalm.

verses.text: Yahweh, I give my life to you.

My God, you are the one I trust.
Do not let me be shamed.
Do not let my enemies cheer at my fall.

Nobody who hopes in you will ever be shamed.
The ones put to shame will be those who cheat for no reason.

Yahweh, let me know your roads.
Show me the way you walk.

Guide me in your truth. Teach me,
since you are the God who rescues me.
I keep hoping in you all day.

Yahweh, remember your tender love and faithful love.
They go back to the very beginning.

Forget the sins I committed when I was young, and my rebellion.
Think of me with your faithful love,
because you are so good, Yahweh.

Yahweh is good and fair,
so he shows sinners the right road.

He steers the humble toward justice.
He teaches the humble how he wants them to live.

Every path of Yahweh is faithful love and truth
for those who obey his agreement and his reminders.

For the sake of your name, Yahweh,
forgive my guilt, though it is large.

Who is the person that fears Yahweh?
Yahweh will show him which way to choose.

His life will be full of good things,
and his children will own the land.

Yahweh’s friendship{b} goes to those who fear him,
and he lets them in on his agreement.

My eyes are always on Yahweh,
because he will free my feet from the trap.

Face me and show me kindness,
because I am alone and in pain.

The troubles in my heart keep growing.{c}
Lead me out of my worries.

Notice my pain and my trouble,
and pardon every one of my sins.

See how many enemies are against me,
and how cruelly they hate me.

Guard my life and set me free.
Let me not be put to shame, because you are my hiding place.

May honesty and goodness keep me safe,
because I wait for you.

God, buy Israel back
from all of his troubles.

notes.text: This psalm is an acrostic. Each verse starts with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet, with a few irregularities. The letter waw has no verse, and the letter qof is replaced. Verse 22 is outside the pattern.
Or “the private counsel” or “the inner circle.”
Or, dividing the Hebrew words differently, “Ease the troubles in my heart.”

chapters.title: By David.{a}

verses.text:
Declare me innocent, Yahweh, for I have lived honestly.
I have trusted Yahweh and never doubted.

Question me, Yahweh, and put me to the test.
Look deep into my heart and thoughts.{a}

Your faithful love stays before my eyes,
and your truth is the path I have followed.

I do not sit with liars.
I stay away from people who wear masks.

I loathe the crowds that do evil,
and I will not take a seat among the wicked.

I rinse my hands to show they are clean,
and I walk around your altar, Yahweh,

singing out my thanks
and telling about all your wonderful deeds.

Yahweh, I treasure the home where you live,
the spot where your glory rests.

Do not sweep me away with sinners,
or take my life along with killers.

Their hands are busy with evil plans,
and their right hands are loaded with bribes.

But I will live an honest life.
Buy me back and be kind to me.

My feet are on level ground.
In the great gatherings I will praise Yahweh.

notes.text: Hebrew “my kidneys and my heart.”

chapters.title: By David.

verses.text:
Yahweh is my light and my savior.
Whom should I fear?
Yahweh is the fortress guarding my life.
Whom should I dread?

Evil people came close to eat me alive,
my attackers and my enemies,
but they were the ones who tripped and fell.

Though a whole army surrounds me,
my heart will not shake.
Though war breaks out against me,
I will still be calm.

I have asked Yahweh for just one thing,
and I will keep looking for it:
to live in Yahweh’s house
all the days of my life,
to gaze at how lovely Yahweh is,
and to ask my questions{a} in his temple.

When trouble comes, he will keep me hidden in his shelter.
He will conceal me deep in his tent
and set me up high on a boulder.

So now I hold my head up above the enemies that surround me.
I will bring joyful offerings to his tent,
singing and making music for Yahweh.

Hear me, Yahweh, when I call out loud.
Be kind to me and answer.

My heart told me to look for your face.{b}
Your face, Yahweh, is what I will look for.

Do not hide your face from me.
Do not send away your servant in your anger.
You have been my helper.
Do not throw me aside or walk out on me,
God my savior.

Even if my own father and mother walk away,
Yahweh will take me in.

Teach me your way, Yahweh.
Lead me on a smooth road,
because so many are watching for me to fall.

Do not give me over to my enemies’ wishes.
Liars have stood up to accuse me,
and they breathe out violence.

I am sure I will see Yahweh’s goodness
while I am still alive on earth.{c}

Wait for Yahweh.
Be strong and brave in your heart.
Yes, wait for Yahweh.

notes.text: Or “to think about him” or “to ask for guidance.”
Hebrew “To you my heart said, ‘Seek my face.’” The meaning is uncertain.

The Hebrew begins with a word meaning “unless,” which the Hebrew scribes marked as doubtful. With it, the line reads, “If I had not believed that I would see...” The Septuagint does not have the word.

chapters.title: By David.

verses.text:
Yahweh, I am calling to you.
You are my rock, so do not shut your ears.
If you say nothing,
I will join those who sink to the pit.

Listen to my pleading voice
when I call to you for help,
when I raise my hands
toward your holy inner room.{a}

Do not drag me off with the wicked,
the people who do evil,
who speak kindly to their neighbors
while hatred fills their hearts.

Give them what their actions deserve,
what their evil deeds have earned.
Pay them for what their hands have done.
Hand them their due.

They have no interest in what Yahweh does
or in the work of his hands.
So he will knock them down and never rebuild them.

Blessed be Yahweh,
because he heard me begging for kindness.

Yahweh is my strength and my shield.
My heart put its trust in him, and he came to my aid.
My heart leaps for joy,
and my song will thank him.

Yahweh is the strength of his people,{b}
and a safe fortress for the king he chose.

Save your people and bless the ones who are yours.
Be their shepherd and hold them up always.

notes.text: Hebrew debir, the innermost room of the temple, the Most Holy Place.
Some Hebrew copies, the Septuagint, and the Syriac say “his people.” Most Hebrew copies say “their strength.”

chapters.title: By David.

verses.text:
Give to Yahweh, you heavenly beings,{a}
give to Yahweh glory and strength.

Give to Yahweh the honor his name deserves.
Bow to Yahweh in his holy splendor.{b}

Yahweh’s voice rolls over the waters.
The glorious God thunders.
Yahweh is over the mighty waters.

Yahweh’s voice is full of power.
Yahweh’s voice is full of majesty.

Yahweh’s voice snaps cedar trees.
Yahweh snaps the cedars of Lebanon.{c}

He makes the mountains jump like a calf,
Lebanon and Sirion{d} like a young wild bull.
Yahweh’s voice flashes out flames of fire.

Yahweh’s voice makes the desert shake.
Yahweh shakes the desert of Kadesh.{e}

Yahweh sat on his throne above the great flood.{g}
Yahweh sits on his throne as King forever.

May Yahweh give strength to his people.
May Yahweh bless his people with peace.

notes.text: Hebrew bene ‘elim, “sons of gods.” They are the heavenly beings around God’s throne.
Or “in holy clothing.”
Lebanon means “white,” probably for its snowy peaks or white rock.
Sirion is the Sidonian name for Mount Hermon. See Deuteronomy 3:9.
Kadesh is a desert place south of Canaan. Its name means “holy.”
Or, with a small change, “twists the oak trees.”
Hebrew mabbul, used elsewhere only for Noah’s flood. See Genesis 6–11.

chapters.title: A psalm of David.

verses.text:
I will honor you, Yahweh, for you pulled me up from the deep.
You never let my enemies cheer over me.

Yahweh my God, I shouted to you for help,
and you cured me.

Yahweh, you hauled me up out of the grave.{b}
You gave me life, so I did not drop into the pit.

Sing to Yahweh, all his loyal people.
Thank him as you recall his holy name.{c}

Anger lasts him only a moment,
but his goodness lasts all through life.
Tears may stay the night,
but a shout of joy comes with the morning.

When all was going well, I said,
“Nothing will ever shake me.”

Yahweh, in your kindness you made my mountain firm.
But when you covered your face, I panicked.

I called out to you, Yahweh.
I begged the Lord for mercy.

I said, “What good is my death,
if I go down to the pit?
Can dust sing your praise?
Can it tell people you are true?

Listen, Yahweh, and be kind to me!
Yahweh, help me!”

You changed my crying into dancing.
You took off my sackcloth and dressed me in joy,

so that my heart{d} will sing to you without ever falling silent.
Yahweh my God, my thanks to you will never end!

notes.text: This may be the temple or David’s palace. Jewish tradition uses this psalm at Hanukkah, the feast that remembers the temple being made holy again.
Hebrew Sheol, the place of the dead.
Hebrew “at the memory of his holiness.”
Hebrew “my glory,” meaning my soul or my whole self.

chapters.title: A psalm. A song for the dedication of the house.{a} By David.

verses.text:
Yahweh, you are where I run to be safe.
Never let me be put to shame.
Rescue me, since you are just.

Lean down and listen to me.
Hurry and rescue me.
Be a solid rock for me,
a fort that keeps me safe.

You are my cliff and my fortress.
So lead me and guide me, because of who you are.

Pull me out of the net they hid for me,
since you are where I am safe.

I put my spirit into your hands.{a}
You have set me free, Yahweh, God of truth.

I cannot stand people who hold on to worthless idols,{b}
but I trust in Yahweh.

I will be glad and celebrate your faithful love,
because you noticed my suffering.
You understood how hard it was for my soul,

and you did not give me into the enemy’s hands.
You put my feet down in open space.

Yahweh, take pity on me, because I am in trouble.
My eyes are tired from crying,
and my soul and body are tired too.

My life is used up by sadness,
and my years by groaning.
My strength is failing because of my sin.{c}
My bones are wasting away.

With all my enemies around, people sneer at me.
My neighbors are the worst.
My friends are afraid of me.
Those who see me out in the street hurry away.

I am forgotten like a dead person.
I am like a smashed pot.

I have heard many people whispering.
There is terror everywhere.
They gather and plot against me.
They plan to take my life.

But I trusted you, Yahweh.
I said, “You are my God.”

My times are in your hands.
Save me from the enemies who chase me.

Make your face shine on your servant.
Save me, because you love me faithfully.

Yahweh, do not let me be shamed, since I call on you.
Let the wicked be shamed.
Let them lie silent in the grave.

Let lying lips be shut tight.
They speak with pride and contempt
against people who do right.

What a store of goodness you keep
for people who fear you!
You hand it out in full view of everyone
to those who run to you for safety.

You tuck them away in the cover of your presence
from human plots.
You keep them safe inside a shelter
from fighting tongues.

Blessed be Yahweh,
because he showed me amazing faithful love
when I was in a city under attack.

In my panic I said,
“You can no longer see me.”
But you heard my pleading voice
when I called to you.

Love Yahweh, all his faithful people!
Yahweh protects the faithful,
but he pays back in full anyone who acts with pride.

Be strong and brave in your hearts,
all of you who wait for Yahweh.

notes.text: Jesus said these words as he died. See Luke 23:46.
Hebrew “vanities of emptiness.” The Septuagint and some Hebrew copies say this. The standard Hebrew text says “I hate.”
The Septuagint and the Syriac say “because of my suffering.”

chapters.title: For the music director. A psalm of David.

subheads.14: My Times Are in Your Hands

verses.text:
Happy is the person whose wrongdoing is forgiven,
whose sin is wiped from sight.{b}

Happy is the person whose guilt Yahweh does not hold against him,
and whose spirit has no trickery.

When I said nothing about my sin, my bones wasted away
while I groaned all day.

Then I told you my sin
and did not hide my guilt.
I said, “I will admit my rebellion to Yahweh.”
And you forgave my guilt and sin.
Selah

So let every loyal person pray to you
while you can still be found.{d}
When a flood of water rises,
it will not touch them.

You are my hiding place.
You keep me out of trouble.
You wrap me in shouts of rescue.
Selah

I will teach you and show you the road to take.
I will advise you, and my eye will be on you.

Do not act like a horse or a mule that has no sense.
They must be held in line with a bit and bridle,
or they will not stay close to you.

The wicked have many sorrows,
but faithful love surrounds the person who trusts Yahweh.

Celebrate in Yahweh and be glad, you who do right.
Sing for joy, all who have honest hearts.

notes.text: Hebrew maskil. Its meaning is uncertain. It is in thirteen psalm titles. It may mean “a skillful psalm” or “a teaching psalm.” Verse 8 uses a word from the same root: “I will teach you.”
Romans 4:7–8 quotes verses 1–2.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
Hebrew “at a time of finding.” The meaning is uncertain.

chapters.title: By David. A maskil.{a}

verses.text:
Shout for joy to Yahweh, you who do right.
Praise looks good on honest people.

Thank Yahweh with the lyre.
Play to him on the ten-string harp.

Sing him a brand-new song.
Play well, and shout out loud.

Yahweh’s word is true,
and everything he does can be trusted.

He loves justice and fairness.
Yahweh’s faithful love fills the whole earth.

Yahweh spoke, and the skies were made.
The breath of his mouth made every star.

He heaps up the ocean water like a pile.{a}
He puts the deep seas in storerooms.

Let the whole earth fear Yahweh.
Let everyone in the world be in awe of him.

He spoke, and it happened.
He gave an order, and it stood there.

Yahweh wrecks the plans of nations.
He ruins what the peoples have in mind.

Yahweh’s plans stand forever,
and so do the purposes of his heart, age after age.

Joyful is the country that has Yahweh as its God,
the people he picked to belong to him.

From heaven Yahweh gazes down
and spots every person alive.

From the home where he sits, he looks out
over everyone who lives on earth.

He formed the heart of every one of them,
and he understands all they do.

No king wins because his army is big.
No warrior escapes because he is strong.

Hoping that a horse will save you is a joke.
With all its strength, it cannot rescue anyone.

Look, Yahweh’s eyes are on those who fear him,
on those who count on his faithful love.

He will save their lives from death
and keep them alive when food runs out.

We are waiting for Yahweh.
He is our helper and our shield.

Our hearts are glad because of him,
for we trust his holy name.

Yahweh, may your faithful love rest on us,
just as we have put our hope in you.

notes.text: Some ancient versions say “as in a leather bag.”

subheads.4: The Word That Made the World

verses.text:
I will bless Yahweh at all times.
His praise will always be on my lips.

I will boast about Yahweh.
Let the humble listen and rejoice.

Declare with me how great Yahweh is.
Together let us make his name high.

I searched for Yahweh, and he replied.
He freed me from everything I feared.

Those who looked to him lit up with joy,{b}
and their faces were never ashamed.

This poor man called out, and Yahweh heard him.
He saved him from every trouble.

Yahweh’s angel makes camp around those who fear him
and saves them.

Taste and see how good Yahweh is.{c}
Happy is the person who hides in him.

Fear Yahweh, you who are his holy people,
because those who fear him lack nothing.

Young lions may go without and grow hungry,
but those who look for Yahweh will not miss out on any good thing.

Come, children, and listen to me.
I will teach you to fear Yahweh.

Who among you wants to enjoy life
and see many good days?{d}

Hold back your tongue from harmful talk,
and keep your lips from deceiving anyone.

Walk away from evil and do good.
Chase after peace and go get it.

Yahweh’s eyes are on those who do right,
and his ears hear their cries.

Yahweh turns against those who do evil.
He wipes out even the memory of them from the earth.

When good people cry out,{e} Yahweh hears.
He rescues them from every trouble.

Yahweh is close to people with broken hearts.
He rescues those whose spirits are crushed.

A good person may have many troubles,
but Yahweh rescues him from every one.

He protects every bone in his body.
Not a single one will be snapped.{f}

Evil will be the death of the wicked,
and those who hate good people will be punished.

Yahweh buys back the lives of his servants.
No one who hides in him will have to pay.

notes.text: This psalm is an acrostic. Each verse begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet. The letter waw has no verse, and verse 22 stands outside the pattern, as in Psalm 25. The title points to 1 Samuel 21:10–15, where the king is called Achish. Abimelech may have been a title for Philistine kings, as in Genesis 20 and 26.
Some Hebrew copies, the Septuagint, and the Syriac say, “Look to him and be bright with joy, and your faces will never be ashamed.”
Compare 1 Peter 2:3.
1 Peter 3:10–12 quotes verses 12–16.
Hebrew “They cry.”
Compare John 19:36.

chapters.title: By David, when he pretended to be out of his mind in front of Abimelech.{a} Abimelech threw him out, and he left.

subheads.4: The Angel Guards Those Who Fear Him

verses.text:
Yahweh, take on those who take me on.
Fight those who fight me.

Pick up your small shield and your large one,
and stand up to help me.

Pull out your spear and battle-ax{a} against those chasing me.
Tell me, “I am the one who saves you.”

Let those who hunt for my life
be shamed and embarrassed.
Let those who plan to hurt me
turn back in confusion.

Let them be like husks in the wind,
with Yahweh’s angel driving them on.

Let their path be dark and slippery,
with Yahweh’s angel chasing them.

They hid their net in a pit for me, though I did nothing.
They dug a trap for my life, though I did nothing.

Let disaster hit him by surprise.
Let the net he hid catch him.
Let him fall into that same disaster.

Then I will celebrate in Yahweh
and be thrilled that he saves me.

Every bone in my body will say,
“Yahweh, no one compares to you!
You rescue the weak from people far stronger.
You rescue the poor and needy from those who rob them.”

Witnesses who lie take the stand.
They quiz me about matters I know nothing of.

They repay my kindness with cruelty,
and leave me feeling empty and alone.{b}

I walked about as sad as if I had lost a friend or brother.
I bent low in sorrow,
like someone crying for his mother.

But when I limped, they gathered and cheered.
Attackers I did not know came together against me.
They tore at me and would not stop.

Like ungodly clowns who mock for a piece of cake,{d}
they gritted their teeth at me.

Lord, how long will you just look on?
Save my life from their ruin,
my precious life{e} from these lions.

I will thank you in the large assembly.
Among a huge crowd, I will praise you.

Do not let my enemies celebrate over me without cause.
Do not let people who hate me for nothing wink at each other.{f}

They do not talk of peace.
They plot lies
against quiet people in the land.

They opened their mouths wide at me and said,
“Ha! Ha! We saw it ourselves!”

You have seen it, Yahweh, so do not stay quiet.
Lord, do not stand far from me.

Wake up and stand up for my rights,
for my case, my God and my Lord.

Yahweh my God, say I am in the right, since you are fair.
Do not let them cheer over me.

Do not let them think, “Ha, we got what we wanted!”
Do not let them say, “We swallowed him whole.”

May all who are happy about my trouble
be ashamed and confused.
May those who put themselves above me
be wrapped in shame and disgrace.

May those who want me proved right
shout for joy and be glad.
May they always say,
“Yahweh is great! He is pleased when his servant is well!”

Then my tongue will tell of your goodness
and your praise all day long.

notes.text: Or “and block the way.”
Hebrew “loss of children to my soul.”
Maybe it means he prayed with his head down on his chest, or that his prayer did no good.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
Hebrew “my only one,” as in Psalm 22:20.
Compare John 15:25, “They hated me for no reason.”

chapters.title: By David.

verses.text:
He thinks so well of himself
that he will never be caught and despised for his guilt.

His mouth is full of harm and lies.
He has stopped being wise and stopped doing good.

He plans trouble while lying in bed.
He sets out on a road that is not good,
and he never turns down evil.

Yahweh, your faithful love reaches up to the sky,
and your trustworthiness to the clouds.

Your goodness is as high as the mountains of God.
Your decisions are as deep as the ocean.
You take care of people and animals alike, Yahweh.

How priceless your faithful love is, God!
Human beings hide in the shade of your wings.

They eat their fill of the rich food in your house,
and you give them drinks from your river of delights.{c}

With you is the spring of life.
In your light we see light.

Keep on loving those who know you,
and keep on doing right for the honest of heart.

Do not let proud feet step on me,
or wicked hands push me away.

See where the evildoers have fallen!
They lie flat and cannot stand again.

notes.text: Some Hebrew copies, the Septuagint, and the Syriac say “his heart.” Most Hebrew copies say “my heart.” The Hebrew literally says “A message of sin to the wicked.”
Romans 3:18 quotes this line.
Hebrew ‘adanekha, from the same root as “Eden.”

chapters.title: For the music director. By David, Yahweh’s servant.

subheads.10: Keep Loving Those Who Know You

verses.text:
Do not get upset over people who do evil,
or envy those who do wrong.

They will soon dry up like grass
and wilt like green plants.

Trust Yahweh and do good.
Make your home in the land and enjoy its safe pastures.{b}

Find your joy in Yahweh,
and he will give you what your heart asks.

Hand over your future to Yahweh.
Trust him, and he will take action.

He will make your goodness shine like the dawn,
and your fair treatment like the noonday sun.

Be still in front of Yahweh and wait calmly for him.
Do not be angry over those who get ahead,
who make their evil plans work.

Stop being angry and give up your rage.
Do not worry. It leads only to harm.

Evildoers will be removed,
but those who wait for Yahweh will receive the land.

Before long, the wicked will be gone.
You will look for where they were, and they will not be there.

But humble people will receive the land{c}
and enjoy great peace.

The wicked plot against good people
and grind their teeth at them.

But the Lord laughs at them,
because he sees their day coming.

The wicked pull out swords and string their bows
to bring down the poor and needy,
to kill those who live honestly.

Their swords will go through their own hearts,
and their bows will snap in two.

The little a good person owns is better
than the great riches of many wicked people.

The arms of the wicked will be broken,
but Yahweh holds up the good.

Yahweh knows how many days honest people will have,
and what they own will last forever.

Bad times will not shame them.
When food is scarce, they will have enough.

The wicked borrow and never pay back,
but the good are kind and give.

Those whom he blesses{e} will receive the land,
but those he curses will be removed.

Yahweh makes a person’s steps firm
when he is pleased with that person’s way.

If he trips, he will not be thrown down hard,
because Yahweh holds his hand.

In my youth and now in my old age,
I have never seen a good person left alone,
or his children begging for food.

He is generous, always lending,
and his children turn out to be a blessing.

Walk away from evil and do good,
and you will have a home forever.

Yahweh loves what is fair.
He will not leave those who are loyal to him.
They are looked after forever,{f}
but the children of the wicked will be removed.

Good people will receive the land
and make their homes there for good.

The mouth of a good person speaks wisdom,
and his tongue says what is fair.

His God’s teaching is in his heart,
and his feet do not slip.

The wicked person lies in wait for the good one
and tries to kill him.

Yahweh will not leave him in the wicked person’s power,
or let a judge find him guilty.

Wait for Yahweh and follow his road.
He will lift you up to receive the land,
and you will watch the wicked be removed.

I have seen a wicked man with great power,
spreading out like a leafy tree in its own soil.{g}

Then he was gone,{h} and look, he was no more.
I searched for him, but could not find him.

Watch the blameless person and notice the honest one,
because the peaceful person has a future.{i}

But those who break the law will all be destroyed.
The wicked have no future.

Yahweh saves good people.
He is their fortress when trouble comes.

Yahweh helps them and rescues them.
He rescues them from the wicked and saves them,
because they trust him.

notes.text: This psalm is an acrostic. About every second verse starts with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet, so each letter begins a stanza of about two verses.
Or “and be a friend of faithfulness,” or “and you will eat in safety.”
Compare Matthew 5:5.
Or “like the burning of ovens.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
That is, blessed by Yahweh.
The Septuagint has “The lawless will be driven out,” which some think keeps the Hebrew letter pattern.
The Hebrew says “in its own soil.” The Septuagint says “like the cedars of Lebanon.”
The Septuagint, the Syriac, and the Latin Vulgate say “he passed away.” Some Hebrew copies say “he passed away” and others say “someone passed by.”
Or “children after him.”

chapters.title: By David.{a}

subheads.1: Do Not Worry About Evil People
subheads.12: Their Own Swords Will Cut Them
subheads.14: The Little That Good People Have
subheads.27: He Does Not Leave His Faithful
subheads.32: He Will Not Let Them Be Condemned

verses.text:
Yahweh, do not correct me while you are angry,
or punish me in your rage.

Your arrows have pierced me deeply,
and your hand has landed hard on me.

My body is not healthy because of your anger.
My bones ache because of what I did wrong.

My guilt has piled up over my head.
It is a load too heavy for me.

My sores stink and rot
because of my foolish ways.

I am bent over and crushed.
I walk around sad all day.

My back burns with fever,
and my body has no health left.

I am weak and flattened.
I groan from the turmoil in my heart.

Lord, you know everything I long for.
My groaning is no secret from you.

My heart pounds. My strength is gone.
Even the light in my eyes has faded.

My friends and companions keep away from my sickness,
and my relatives stay far off.

Those out to kill me set traps.
Those who want to hurt me talk about my ruin
and plan lies all day.

But I am like a man who is deaf and hears nothing,
like one who cannot speak and says nothing.

I am like someone who does not hear,
who has no answers in his mouth.

But I wait for you, Yahweh.
You are the one who will answer, Lord my God.

I said, “Do not let them celebrate over me
or boast when my foot slips.”

I am ready to collapse,
and my pain never leaves me.

I confess that I am guilty.
My sin weighs on my mind.

But my enemies are alive and strong,{b}
and many hate me for no good reason.

Those who repay good with evil attack me
because I try to do good.{c}

Yahweh, do not leave me!
My God, stay close to me.

Hurry to help me,
Lord, my savior.

notes.text: Hebrew lehazkir, “to bring to remembrance.” The same word is in the title of Psalm 70. It may refer to the memorial part of the grain offering. See Leviticus 2:2.
Hebrew “my enemies are living.” A Dead Sea Scroll (4QPs-a) reads “for no reason,” which matches the next line.
Some Hebrew copies spell this word differently. The meaning is the same.

chapters.title: A psalm of David, to bring to mind.{a}

verses.text:
I decided, “I will guard my steps
so my own tongue does not make me sin.
I will keep my lips shut tight
while wicked people stand nearby.”

My heart burned inside me.
As I thought, a fire began to blaze,
and then I spoke:

“Yahweh, show me how my life will end,
and how many days I have,
so I will know how short my life is.

You made my life only a few inches long.{c}
My years are nothing to you.
Every person, even when strong, is just a puff of air.
Selah

Everyone walks about like a shadow.
They bustle about for nothing.
They pile up wealth and do not know who will get it.

So what am I waiting for now, Lord?
You are my only hope.

Free me from every wrong I have done.
Do not let fools make fun of me.

I stayed silent and did not open my mouth,
because you were the one who did this.

Take your blows away from me.
Your heavy hand is wearing me out.

When you scold a person to correct his sin,
you make everything he treasures vanish like cloth that moths have chewed.
Each person is only a breath.
Selah

“Yahweh, listen to my prayer.
Pay attention to my cry.
Do not turn away from my tears.
I am only a guest in your house,
a wanderer like every ancestor of mine.

Look away from me so I can smile again
before I leave this life and am gone.”

notes.text: Jeduthun was one of David’s chief musicians. See 1 Chronicles 16:41–42 and 25:1. His name is also in the titles of Psalms 62 and 77.
Hebrew “away from good.”
Hebrew “a handbreadth,” about 3 inches or 7.5 centimeters. The word hebel, “breath,” is the word often translated “meaningless” in Ecclesiastes.

chapters.title: For the music director, for Jeduthun.{a} A psalm of David.

verses.text:
I waited and waited for Yahweh.
He turned to me and heard my cry.

He hauled me out of a terrible pit,{a}
out of thick, sticky mud.
He placed my feet on a rock
and steadied me as I walked.

He placed a fresh song in my mouth,
a hymn of praise for our God.
Many will see it and be amazed,
and they will trust Yahweh.

Happy is the person who trusts in Yahweh,
who pays no attention to proud people
or to those who chase after lies.

Yahweh my God, you have done so many wonders.
Your plans for us are beyond compare.
If I tried to announce and describe them,
they would be more than anyone could count.

You were not looking for sacrifices and gifts.
You made my ears open to you.{b}
You did not demand burnt offerings
or sin offerings.

Then I answered, “I am coming.
My story is written in the scroll.

I love doing what you want, my God.
Your teaching is deep inside me.”

I have told the good news of your justice to the great crowd.
I have not shut my mouth.
Yahweh, you know it.

I never kept your goodness locked in my heart.
I spoke of your trustworthiness and rescue.
I told the great assembly
about your steady love and truth.

Yahweh, you will not hold back your kindness from me.
Your faithful love and truth will always keep me safe.

Troubles past counting have closed in on me.
My sins have grabbed me, and I cannot see my way.
They are more than the hairs on my head,
and my courage is gone.

Please, Yahweh, rescue me!{c}
Yahweh, come quickly to help me.

May those who are trying to end my life
be ashamed and confused.
May those who wish me harm
be pushed back in disgrace.

May those who laugh at me, “Ha! Ha!”
be stunned by their own shame.

May all who search for you
be glad and full of joy in you.
May those who love your saving help
always say, “Great is Yahweh!”

But I am poor and needy.
The Lord still thinks of me.
You are my helper and my savior.
My God, do not wait.

notes.text: Or “the pit of noise.”
Hebrew “you dug ears for me.” The Septuagint says, “but you prepared a body for me.” Hebrews 10:5–7 quotes it this way.
Verses 13–17 appear again, with small changes, as Psalm 70.

chapters.title: For the music director. By David. A psalm.

verses.text:
Happy is the one who thinks of the poor.
Yahweh will rescue him on a day of trouble.

Yahweh will hold him up on his sickbed.
You will turn over his bed and heal him in his illness.{b}

I said, “Yahweh, be kind to me.
Heal me, for I have sinned against you.”

My enemies say cruel things about me:
“How long until he dies and his name is gone?”

If one of them comes to visit, his words are hollow.
His heart collects bad news,
and he spreads it once he is outside.

Everyone who hates me whispers about me.
They imagine the worst for me.

They say, “Some terrible sickness{c} has taken hold of him.
He has lain down and will not get up again.”

But you, Yahweh, be kind to me.
Raise me up, and I will give them what they have earned.

This is how I know you delight in me:
my enemy has not won against me.

You hold me up because I am honest,
and you keep me in your presence forever.

notes.text: Some Hebrew copies say “and may he be called happy.”
Hebrew “you turn over all his bed in his sickness.”
Hebrew “a thing of Belial,” meaning worthlessness or ruin.
Hebrew “the man of my peace.” Jesus applies this verse to Judas in John 13:18.
This blessing ends Book One of the Psalms (Psalms 1–41). Each of the five books ends with a blessing like it (41:13, 72:18–19, 89:52, 106:48), and Psalm 150 ends the whole collection.

chapters.title: For the music director. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Like a deer that craves a stream of water,
my soul craves you, God.

The living God is who I thirst for.
When can I go to see his face?

This is what I remember as I pour out my heart:
I used to walk along with the crowd,
leading them to God’s house
with shouts of joy and praise,
a huge throng celebrating a holy day.

Why are you so low, my soul?
Why are you groaning inside me?
Hope in God! I will praise him once more,
my savior who is near.{b}

Deep waters call to deep waters
in the roar of your waterfalls.
Every one of your breakers and waves
has rolled over me.

By day Yahweh sends out his faithful love,
and at night I have his song with me,
a prayer to the God of my life.

I say to God, my rock,
“Why have you forgotten me?
Why must I walk about grieving
while the enemy bullies me?”

Why are you so low, my soul?
Why are you groaning inside me?
Hope in God! I will praise him once more,
my savior and my God.

notes.text: This is the start of Book Two of the Psalms (Psalms 42–72). In Psalms 42–83 the name Yahweh appears much less often and the word “God” (Elohim) much more often than in the rest of the Psalms. Korah’s family were temple singers. See 1 Chronicles 6:31–37. Maskil is a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps “a skillful psalm.”
Hebrew “the saving acts of his face.” Some Hebrew copies, the Septuagint, and the Syriac move the first word of verse 6 here and read, “my savior and my God,” as in verse 11 and in 43:5.
Mount Mizar means “little mountain.” It is not known from anywhere else. The setting is the upper Jordan below Mount Hermon.
Or “like a sword in my bones.” The Hebrew is uncertain.

chapters.heading: Book Two (Psalms 42–72)
chapters.title: For the music director. A maskil of the sons of Korah.{a}

verses.text:
Clear my name, God, and argue my case
against a people who are not loyal.
Rescue me from the liar and the cheat.

You are the God who keeps me safe,
so why have you pushed me away?
Why must I walk about grieving
while the enemy bullies me?

Send out your light and your truth as my guides.
May they bring me up to your holy mountain,
the place where you live.

Then I will come to God’s altar,
to God, my greatest delight.
I will praise you with the harp,
God, my God.

Why are you so low, my soul?
Why are you groaning inside me?
Hope in God! I will praise him once more,
my savior and my God.

We heard the story, God, with our own ears.
Our ancestors passed it down to us:
the deeds you did in their time,
in days long gone.

With your own hand you drove nations out
and planted our ancestors in their place.
You crushed other peoples
and let our ancestors spread out.{a}

They did not take the land by the edge of a sword.
Their own muscles did not give them the win.
The victory came from your right hand and your arm,
and from the light of your face,
because you loved them.

You are my King, God.
Order victories{b} for Jacob.

Through you we shove back those who attack us.
By your name we trample those who rise against us.

I do not trust in my bow,
and my sword cannot give me the win.

You are the one who rescued us from our attackers.
You embarrassed those who hate us.

All day long we have praised God,
and we will thank your name forever.
Selah

But now you have turned us away and shamed us.
Our armies march out without you.

You make us run from our attackers,
and those who hate us take whatever they please.

You gave us away like sheep for dinner,
and you spread us out among the nations.

You sold your people for next to nothing,
and you made no profit from the sale.

Our neighbors now laugh at us.
Those around us tease and sneer.

To the nations we have become a byword.
Peoples toss their heads over us.

My shame is in front of me all day,
and disgrace covers my face,

at the sound of those who insult and curse me,
and at the sight of my enemy getting even.

All this has happened to us,
yet we have not forgotten you
or broken faith with your agreement.

Our hearts have not turned back.
Our feet have not left your path.

You crushed us and left us among jackals{c}
and covered us with deep darkness.

Had we forgotten our God’s name
or reached out to a foreign god,

Would God not find that out?
He knows what is hidden in every heart.

But for your sake we are killed all day long.
We are treated like sheep for the butcher.{d}

Wake up! Why are you asleep, Lord?
Get up! Do not push us away for good.

Why are you hiding?
Why do you forget how we suffer and are bullied?

We are sunk down in the dust.
Our bodies are pressed to the ground.

Get up and help us!
Buy us back, because of your faithful love.

notes.text: Or “but you set them free.”
The Hebrew says “victories.” The Septuagint and Syriac say, “You are my King and my God, who orders victories.”
The Hebrew says “jackals.” Some copies read “sea monster.”
Romans 8:36 quotes this verse.

chapters.title: For the music director. By the sons of Korah. A maskil.

verses.text:
My heart overflows with a lovely theme.
I recite my poem to the king.
My tongue is like the pen of a fast writer.

You are better looking than any other man.
Kind words flow from your lips.
This shows that God has blessed you forever.

Strap your sword at your side, mighty one.
Put on your glory and majesty.

Your sharp arrows pierce the king’s enemies through the heart.
Nations collapse beneath you.

Your throne, God, lasts forever and ever.{d}
Your kingdom is ruled with a fair rod.

You love goodness and hate evil.
So God, your God, has poured the oil of joy
on you more than on your friends.

All your robes smell of myrrh, aloes, and cassia.
Music from ivory palaces makes you glad.

Daughters of kings are among your honored guests.
The queen stands on your right, wearing gold from Ophir.

Listen, daughter, think it over and pay attention.
Put your own people and your father’s house behind you.

The king will long for your beauty.
He is your lord, so honor him.

The people of Tyre will bring a gift.
The richest people will ask for your favor.

The princess is dressed in splendor inside the palace.{e}
Her gown is woven with gold.

In colorful clothes she is led to the king.
Her bridesmaids follow behind her,
and are brought to you.

They are led along with happiness and joy.
They enter the king’s palace.

Your sons will follow your ancestors on the throne.
You will name them princes across the whole land.

I will make your name remembered in every generation.
So the nations will praise you forever and ever.

notes.text: Hebrew shoshannim, probably a tune name. It is also in the titles of Psalms 60, 69, and 80.
This is a song for a royal wedding. It speaks to the king (verses 2–9) and to his bride (verses 10–15).
The Hebrew is unusual. It may mean “for truth and humble goodness.”

This follows the Hebrew and the Septuagint, which call the king “God” (Elohim). Hebrews 1:8–9 quotes verses 6–7 about the Son. Other possible readings are “Your throne is God’s throne forever and ever,” or “Your throne is like God’s.”
Hebrew “within.”

chapters.title: For the music director, to the tune “Lilies.”{a} By the sons of Korah. A maskil. A love song.{b}

subheads.2: You Are the Finest of Men

verses.text:
God is our hiding place and our strength,
always ready to help in trouble.

So we will not be afraid when the earth shakes,
or when mountains slide into the heart of the sea,

when its waters roar and foam,
and the mountains tremble at its heaving.
Selah

A river with its streams makes the city of God glad,
the holy place where the Most High lives.

God is inside her, so she will not fall.
God will help her when morning comes.

Nations roared and kingdoms toppled.
He spoke up, and the earth melted.

Yahweh of Armies is on our side.
Jacob’s God is our high fortress.
Selah

Come and see what Yahweh has done,
the ruins he has left on the earth.

He stops wars all over the world.
He snaps the bow and breaks the spear.
He burns the carts{b} with fire.

“Stop your fighting! Know that I am God.
The nations will honor me.
