The whole earth will honor me.”

Yahweh of Armies is on our side.
Jacob’s God is our high fortress.
Selah

notes.text: Hebrew ‘alamot, perhaps “young women,” so soprano voices. Compare 1 Chronicles 15:20.
The Hebrew says “carts.” The Septuagint says “shields.”

chapters.title: For the music director. By the sons of Korah. For high voices.{a} A song.

subheads.4: A River in the City of God

verses.text:
All you nations, clap your hands!
Cheer for God with a loud, happy shout!

Yahweh, the Most High, inspires awe.
Over all the earth he reigns as the great King.

He puts nations beneath our control,
and peoples beneath our feet.

He picked out our homeland for us,
the pride of Jacob, whom he loves.
Selah

God has gone up among shouts of joy.
Yahweh has gone up with a horn blowing.{a}

Make music for God, make music!
Make music for our King, make music!

God is King over the entire earth.
Sing him a song of wisdom.{b}

God rules over the nations.
God is seated on his holy throne.

The princes of the nations have gathered
with the people of Abraham’s God.
All the rulers{c} on earth are God’s.
He is raised high above them all.

notes.text: Hebrew shofar, a ram’s horn.
Hebrew maskil. See the note on the title of Psalm 32.
Hebrew “shields,” meaning rulers.

chapters.title: For the music director. By the sons of Korah. A psalm.

verses.text:
Yahweh is great and worthy of endless praise
in our God’s city, on his holy mountain.

Mount Zion rises beautifully, the joy of the whole world.
Far to the north{a} stands
the city of the great King.

Inside her fortresses God has shown
that he is a safe refuge.

Look, the kings joined forces.
They marched in together.

They saw the city, and they were stunned.
They panicked and ran off.

Shaking took hold of them there,
pain like a woman giving birth,

like a wind from the east
that smashes the ships of Tarshish.

What we were told, we have now seen
in the city of Yahweh of Armies,
in the city of our God.
God will keep it secure forever.
Selah

God, inside your temple
we have thought about your faithful love.

God, your praise reaches the ends of the earth,
just as your name does.
Your right hand is full of justice.

Let Mount Zion be glad!
Let the towns of Judah celebrate
because of your decisions.

Walk around Zion and circle her.
Count her towers.

Examine her walls closely.
Walk through her fortresses,
so you can describe them to the next generation.

notes.text: Hebrew tsaphon, “north.” It was also the name of the sacred mountain in Canaanite stories, Mount Zaphon. This psalm gives Zion the honor that others gave to Zaphon.
Hebrew ‘al-mut, “over death” or “to death.” The Septuagint and some Hebrew copies read ‘olamot, “forever.” The words may be a music note that belongs to the title of the next psalm.

chapters.title: A song. A psalm by the sons of Korah.

subheads.1: The City of the Great King
subheads.9: We Thought About Your Faithful Love

verses.text:
Listen to this, all nations.
Pay attention, everyone alive in the world,

whether common or important,{a}
whether rich or poor.

My mouth will speak wise words,
and the thoughts of my heart will bring understanding.

I will lean in to hear a saying.
I will explain my puzzle to the sound of the harp.

Why should I fear in dangerous days,
when the wrongs of those who hunt me surround me,{b}

people who count on their wealth
and brag about how rich they are?

No one can buy back a brother’s life.{c}
He cannot pay God the price for him.

The price for a life is too high,
and no one can ever pay it,

so that someone could live on forever
and never see the grave.

Everyone can see that clever people die too.
The foolish and the dull die as well,
and leave their riches to other people.

Their tombs{d} are their permanent homes,
where they stay from one age to the next,
though they once gave their own names to pieces of land.

A person with great honors does not stay.
He ends up like the animals that die.

This is the road of those who trust in themselves foolishly,
and of their followers who agree with what they say.
Selah

Like a flock, they are sent to the grave,
with death as their shepherd.
By morning the honest will be in charge over them.
Their bodies will waste away in the grave,
far from any palace.{e}

But God will pay the price to free me
from the grave’s power,
because he will take me to himself.
Selah

Do not be afraid when someone gets rich,
when the splendor of his house grows.

When he dies, he takes nothing along.
His glory will not go down with him.

While he lived he congratulated himself,
and people praise you when you do well for yourself.

Still, he will join his ancestors.
They will never see daylight again.

People with great honors but no understanding
are like the animals that die.

notes.text: Hebrew “both sons of Adam and sons of man.”
Hebrew “the sin of my heels.”
Or “No one can truly buy back a brother.” Some Hebrew copies read, “A man cannot buy himself back.”
The Septuagint and the Syriac say “tombs.” The Hebrew says “their inner thoughts.”
The second half of this verse is very hard to read in Hebrew.

chapters.title: For the music director. By the sons of Korah. A psalm.

verses.text:
The Mighty One, God, Yahweh,{b} speaks.
He calls the earth together
from where the sun rises to where it sets.

From Zion, perfect in beauty,
God shines out.

Our God is coming, and he will not stay silent.
A fire eats up all in front of him,
and a wild storm whirls around him.

He calls out to the heavens above
and to the earth, so he can judge his people:

“Bring in my faithful people,
who sealed an agreement with me through sacrifice.”

The skies announce that he is fair,
for God himself is the judge.
Selah

“Hear me, my people, while I speak.
Israel, I am going to testify against you.
I am God, your God.

I am not scolding you about your sacrifices
or your burnt offerings, which are always in front of me.

I do not need a bull from your barn
or goats from your pens.

Every animal in the forest is mine,
and so are the cattle on a thousand hills.

I know all the birds of the hills,
and the creatures crawling in the fields belong to me.

Were I hungry, I would never mention it to you,
since the world and all that fills it is mine.

Do I dine on bull meat?
Do I drink goat blood?

Give thanks as your gift to God,
and keep your promises to the Most High.

Call out to me in times of trouble.
I will pull you out, and you will give me glory.”

But God tells the wicked,
“How dare you recite my laws
or speak about my agreement?

You hate being corrected,
and you throw my words behind you.

If you spot a thief, you run with him.
You spend time with those who cheat on their husbands or wives.

You let your mouth run loose for evil,
and your tongue weaves lies.

You sit and talk against your brother.
You slander your own mother’s son.

You did these things while I stayed silent.
You imagined that I was just like you.
But now I will accuse you and set out the whole case before you.

“Consider this, you who ignore God,
or I will rip you to shreds, with no one to rescue you.

Whoever offers thanks gives me honor.
To the one who walks the right road
I will show God’s rescue.”

notes.text: Asaph was a Levite David put in charge of the temple singers. See 1 Chronicles 15:17, 16:5, and 25:1. His name later belonged to a guild of singers from his family. See Ezra 2:41. Psalms 50 and 73–83 carry his name.
Hebrew ‘el ‘elohim YHWH, three names of God side by side, as in Joshua 22:22.

chapters.title: A psalm of Asaph.{a}

subheads.1: God Calls the Earth to Court

verses.text:
Show me kindness, God, out of your faithful love.
In your great tenderness
erase the wrong things I have done.

Scrub me clean of my guilt,
and make me pure from my sin.

I know the wrong I have done,
and my sin is always in front of me.

Against you, and you alone, I have sinned.
I did what you see as evil.
So your words prove right,
and your verdict is fair.{b}

Look, I was guilty from the moment I was born.
I was sinful from the time my mother carried me.

Look, you want truth deep inside a person,
and in the secret places you teach me wisdom.

Clean me with hyssop,{c} and I will be clean.
Wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.

Let me hear happiness and joy again.
Let the bones you broke dance.

Do not look at my sins any longer,
and wipe away all my guilt.

Make a clean heart in me, God,
and put a new, steady spirit inside me.

Do not banish me from where you are,
and keep your Holy Spirit with me.

Bring back the joy that comes from your saving me,
and sustain me with a willing spirit.

Then I will teach rebels your ways,
and sinners will return to you.

Free me from the guilt of spilling blood, God,
God who saves me,
and my tongue will sing out about your goodness.

Lord, open my lips,
and my mouth will tell your praise.

You do not enjoy sacrifices, or I would bring them.
A burnt offering does not please you.

The sacrifice that God wants is a broken spirit.
A broken and crushed heart, God, you will never look down on.

In your kindness, do good for Zion.
Rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.

Then right sacrifices will please you,
the burnt offerings and whole offerings.
Then bulls will be placed on your altar.

notes.text: See 2 Samuel 11–12. In the Hebrew text the title counts as verses 1–2, so the Hebrew verse numbers in this psalm are two higher than the numbers here.
Paul quotes this verse from the Septuagint in Romans 3:4: “so that you are proved right in your words and win when you are judged.”
Hyssop is a small bushy plant. It was used to sprinkle water and blood in cleansing rituals. See Exodus 12:22, Leviticus 14:4–7, and Numbers 19:18.

chapters.title: For the music director. A psalm of David, when the prophet Nathan came to him after he had slept with Bathsheba.{a}

verses.text:
Strong man, why boast of your evil?
All day long God is faithful to those who are loyal.{b}

Your tongue plans ruin
like a sharp razor, you master of lies.

You prefer evil to good,
and lies to the truth.
Selah

You love every word that destroys,
you lying tongue.

God will tear you down for good.
He will snatch you up and rip you out of your tent.
He will pull you out of the land of the living.
Selah

Good people will see it and be afraid.
They will laugh at that man and say,

But I am like a green olive tree growing in God’s house.
I trust in God’s faithful love for all time.

For what you have done I will give thanks forever.
I will wait for your name, because it is good,
in the presence of your faithful people.

notes.text: See 1 Samuel 21:1–9 and 22:9–19. The Hebrew text counts the title as verses 1–2.
Hebrew “God’s chesed is all the day.” The Syriac says “against the godly.”
Or “by his own wishes,” following the Syriac and the Aramaic translation.

chapters.title: For the music director. A maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite went to Saul and told him, “David has come to Ahimelech’s house.”{a}

verses.text:
Fools tell themselves, “There is no God.”
They are rotten and do horrible wrongs.
Nobody does good.

From heaven God looks down
on the human family.
He is checking to see if anyone is wise,
if anyone is searching for God.

Everyone has turned back. Together they have gone bad.
Nobody does good.
Not even one.

Do these evildoers know nothing?
They eat up my people as they eat bread,
and they never call on God.

They were gripped by fear there,
where there was nothing to fear!{b}
God scattered the bones of those who camped against you.
You shamed them, because God turned them down.

notes.text: Hebrew mahalat. It may be a tune name, or a word for “sickness” or “sorrow.” It is also in Psalm 88. This psalm is almost the same as Psalm 14, but it uses “God” (Elohim) where Psalm 14 uses “Yahweh.”
Compare Psalm 14:5–6, which reads differently.
Or “brings back the captives of his people,” as in Psalm 14:7.

chapters.title: For the music director, to the tune “Mahalath.”{a} A maskil of David.

subheads.4: Terror Where There Was No Reason

verses.text:
God, rescue me by your name,
and clear me by your power.

God, hear my prayer.
Listen to what I say.

Strangers{b} have risen up against me,
and cruel men are after my life.
They give no thought to God.
Selah

Look, God is the one who helps me.
The Lord is the one who holds up my life.{c}

He will turn the evil back on my enemies.{d}
Because you are true, put an end to them.

I will bring you a freewill offering.
I will thank your name, Yahweh, because it is good.

He has saved me from every trouble,
and I have looked my enemies in the eye.

notes.text: Hebrew neginot. See 1 Samuel 23:19 and 26:1. The Hebrew text counts the title as verses 1–2.
Some Hebrew copies and the Aramaic translation say “proud men,” as in Psalm 86:14.
Or “the Lord is among those who hold up my life.”
A note in the Hebrew margin has this reading. The main text has “The evil will return to my enemies.”

chapters.title: For the music director, with stringed instruments.{a} A maskil of David, when the people of Ziph went to Saul and said, “David is hiding among us, isn’t he?”

verses.text:
God, hear my prayer.
Do not hide from my plea.

Pay attention to me and answer.
I cannot settle down. I moan as I complain

because of the enemy’s shouting
and the wicked person’s pressure.
They pour trouble down on me
and attack me with fury.

My heart twists inside my chest.
The fears of death have fallen on me.

Fear and shaking have come over me,
and horror covers me like a blanket.

I thought, “I wish I could grow wings like a dove!
Then I would fly off and be at rest.

I would go far, far away
and stay in the wilderness.
Selah

I would hurry to a hiding place
away from the howling wind and storm.”

Lord, confuse them and make their speech a muddle.{a}
I have seen violence and fighting in the city.

Day and night they walk their rounds along its walls,
and evil and trouble live inside it.

Destruction is in the middle of it.
Cruelty and cheating never leave its market square.

It was not an enemy who insulted me.
I could have put up with that.
It was not someone who hated me who stood tall against me.
I could have hidden from him.

It was you, someone just like me,
my close friend, whom I knew well.

We used to share sweet talks together.
We walked with the crowd into God’s house.

But I cry out to God,
and Yahweh will rescue me.

At sunrise, at noon, and at sunset
I grumble and groan,
and he hears my voice.

God will hear and answer them.
He is the one who has sat on his throne since long ago.
Selah
They never change,
and they do not fear God.

That man{c} raised his hands against those at peace with him.
He broke his agreement.

His speech was smoother than cream,
but war was in his heart.
His words were softer than oil,
but they were drawn swords.

Hand your burden{d} to Yahweh, and he will hold you up.
He will never let good people fall.

But you, God, will push them down
into the pit of ruin.
Murderers and liars
will not live half as long as they could.
But I will trust in you.

notes.text: Compare Genesis 11:1–9.
Compare Numbers 16:30–33. Some Hebrew copies say, “Let death surprise them.” Others say, “Let ruins come on them.”
Hebrew “He.”
Or “what he has given you.” Compare 1 Peter 5:7.

chapters.title: For the music director, with stringed instruments. A maskil of David.

verses.text:
Be kind to me, God, because people are trampling me.
All day long attackers push me around.

My enemies trample me all day.
So many fight against me, and they are proud.{c}

On the day I am afraid,
I will lean on you.

I praise God for what he promised.
I trust God, so I have no fear.
What could mere flesh do to me?

All day long they twist my words.
Every plan of theirs is aimed to hurt me.

They gather and hide in wait.
They study my steps,
eager to end my life.

Because of their sin, push them out.{d}
In your anger, God, throw down these nations.

You keep track of my wandering.
Put my tears in your bottle.
Are they not written in your book?

Then my enemies will retreat
the day I call.
One thing I know: God is on my side.

The word of God is what I praise.
The word of Yahweh is what I praise.

I trust God, so I have no fear.
What could a human being do to me?

I owe you promises, God,
and I will pay them with thank offerings.

You have rescued me from death,
and kept my feet from tripping,
so I can walk with God
in the light where the living are.

notes.text: Hebrew yonat ‘elem rechoqim, probably a tune name. See 1 Samuel 21:10–15.
Hebrew miktam, a word of uncertain meaning. It is also in the titles of Psalms 16 and 57–60.
Or “O Most High.”
Hebrew “For sin, escape for them?” The text is hard to read.

chapters.title: For the music director, to the tune “The Silent Dove of Faraway Places.”{a} A miktam{b} of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.

verses.text:
Be kind to me, God, be kind to me,
because my soul runs to you for safety.
I will hide in the shadow of your wings
until the storm of trouble has passed.

I cry out to God Most High,
to God, who completes what he plans for me.

He will send help from heaven and rescue me.
He will shame the one who stomps on me.
Selah
God will send out his faithful love and truth.

Lions are all around me.
I lie down among people who breathe fire,
human beings with teeth like spears and arrows,
and tongues like sharp swords.

Be lifted high above the heavens, God.
Let your glory fill all the earth.

They set out a net to trip my feet.
I was bent down low.
A pit was what they dug along my way,
but they fell into it themselves.
Selah

I am firm and confident, God, absolutely firm.
I will sing and make my music.

I will thank you, Lord, wherever peoples gather.
I will sing about you in every land.

Your faithful love is so great that it reaches the sky,
and your truth reaches the clouds.

Be lifted high above the heavens, God.
Let your glory cover all the earth.

notes.text: Hebrew ‘al-tashchet, probably a tune name. It is also in the titles of Psalms 58, 59, and 75. See 1 Samuel 22:1 and 24:3. Verses 7–11 appear again as Psalm 108:1–5.
Hebrew “my glory,” meaning my soul or my whole self.

chapters.title: For the music director, to the tune “Do Not Destroy.”{a} A miktam of David, when he ran away from Saul into the cave.

verses.text:
Rulers,{a} are your words really right?
Do you judge people evenly?

No. In your hearts you plan crimes,
and your hands hand out violence across the land.

The wicked go wrong from birth.
They tell lies and stray from the day they are born.

Their venom is like snake venom,
like a deaf cobra that plugs its ears,

so it cannot hear the song of the snake charmers,
however skilled they are.

God, smash the teeth in their mouths.
Yahweh, break the fangs of these young lions.

Let them drain away like water running down a hill.
When he aims his bow, let his arrows be dull.{b}

Let them be like a snail that melts as it crawls,
like a baby born dead that never sees the sun.

Before your pots feel the heat of a thorn fire,
green or burning, may he sweep them away.{c}

Good people will be glad when they see justice done.
They will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.

Then people will say, “The good truly do get a reward.
A God truly does judge on earth.”

notes.text: Hebrew ‘elem, “silence.” It is probably to be read ‘elim, “gods,” meaning rulers or heavenly beings set over the nations. Compare Psalm 82.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.

chapters.title: For the music director, to the tune “Do Not Destroy.” A miktam of David.

subheads.10: There Is a God Who Judges

verses.text:
My God, rescue me from my enemies.
Set me up high, out of reach of those who attack me.

Rescue me from evildoers,
and save me from killers.

Look, they are waiting to catch me.
Fierce men gather against me,
though I have done no wrong or sin, Yahweh.

I have done nothing wrong, yet they run and get ready.
Wake up, come to me, and look.

You, Yahweh, God of Armies, God of Israel,
get up and visit all the nations.
Be kind to no wicked traitor.
Selah

They come back as evening falls.
They growl like dogs
and prowl around the city.

Look at what spills from their mouths.
Swords are on their lips.
“Who is listening?” they say.

But you, Yahweh, laugh at them.
You scoff at every nation.

My strength, I keep watch for you,{b}
because God is my high tower.

My faithful God will meet me on the road.{c}
God will let me see my enemies beaten.

Do not finish them off yet, or my people may forget.
Make them stagger by your strength and bring them low,
Lord, our shield.

Finish them off in your anger. Finish them until they are gone.
Then they will know, all the way to the ends of the earth,
that God rules in Jacob.
Selah

They come back as evening falls.
They growl like dogs
and prowl around the city.

They roam about looking for food,
and if they go hungry, they howl all night.{d}

But I will sing about your strength.
At daybreak I will sing happily about your faithful love.
You have been my fortress
and my safe place when I was in trouble.

You are my strength, and I will make music for you,
because God is my high tower,
the God who shows me faithful love.

notes.text: See 1 Samuel 19:11–17.
Some Hebrew copies, the Septuagint, and the Aramaic translation say “my strength” (compare verse 17). Most Hebrew copies say “his strength.”
Some Hebrew copies say, “My faithful God.” The usual text says “The God of my faithful love.”
The Hebrew says “stay all night.” The Septuagint and the Latin Vulgate say “and grumble.”

chapters.title: For the music director, to the tune “Do Not Destroy.” A miktam of David, when Saul sent men to watch the house so they could kill him.{a}

subheads.16: I Will Sing of Your Strength

verses.text:
God, you turned us away and broke through our walls.{c}
You were angry. Bring us back!

You made the land shake and cracked it open.
Heal its cracks, because it is about to fall.

You made your people see hard times.
You gave us wine to drink that made us stagger.

So the ones you love may be rescued,
save with your right hand and answer us.{e}

Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine.
Ephraim is my helmet.
Judah is my royal rod.

Who will bring me into the walled city?
Who will guide me to Edom?

Is it not you, God, who rejected us?
You no longer march out with our armies.

Give us aid against the enemy,
because human help is useless.

With God we will do brave things.
He is the one who will stamp on our enemies.

notes.text: Hebrew shushan ‘edut, probably a tune name. The Hebrew text counts the title as verses 1–2.
See 2 Samuel 8:3–14 and 1 Chronicles 18:3–13, where Abishai is the one credited with 18,000. Verses 5–12 appear again as Psalm 108:6–13.
Hebrew “broke us.”
Or “so they could run to it from the bow.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
Some Hebrew copies say “answer us.” Others say “answer me.”
Or “from his sanctuary.”
Throwing a sandal was a way of claiming ownership. Compare Ruth 4:7.

chapters.title: For the music director, to the tune “Lily of the Reminder.”{a} A miktam of David, for teaching, when he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and when Joab came back and struck down 12,000 men of Edom in the Valley of Salt.{b}

subheads.5: Save Us With Your Right Hand

verses.text:
Hear my cry, God.
Listen to my prayer.

From the far edge of the earth I call to you,
while my heart grows weak.
Lead me to a rock that is higher than I can climb,

because you have been my shelter,
a mighty tower against my enemy.

Let me stay in your tent for all time.
Let me take cover under your wings.
Selah

You, God, have heard my promises.
You gave me what belongs to those who fear your name.

Add more days to the king’s days.
May his years go on for generations.

May he sit on his throne in God’s presence forever.
Send faithful love and truth to protect him.

Then I will sing praise to your name always
and keep my promises day after day.

chapters.title: For the music director, on stringed instruments. By David.

subheads.1: From the Ends of the Earth

verses.text:
My soul waits quietly{a} for God alone.
My rescue comes from him.

He alone is my rock and my savior,
my high fortress. I will not be badly shaken.

How long will all of you attack one man
and try to knock him down,
like a leaning wall or a wobbly fence?

They plan only to push him off his high place.
They enjoy telling lies.
Their mouths say blessings,
but inside they curse.
Selah

My soul, wait quietly for God alone,
for my hope comes from no one else.

He alone is my rock and my savior,
my high fortress. I will not be shaken.

My rescue and my honor depend on God.
My strong rock and my hiding place are in God.

Trust him at all times, people.
Open your hearts before him.
God is a shelter for us.
Selah

Ordinary people are only a breath.
Important people are a lie.
On a scale they rise up.
All of them together weigh less than a breath.

Do not trust in stealing money.
Do not put empty hope in robbery.
If your riches grow, do not set your heart on them.

God has spoken once.
Twice I have heard it:
power belongs to God,

and faithful love belongs to you, Lord.
You pay each person back for what he has done.{b}

notes.text: Or “waits in stillness.” The same word is in verse 5.
Compare Matthew 16:27 and Romans 2:6.

chapters.title: For the music director, for Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
God, you are my God. I search hard for you.
My soul thirsts for you.
My whole body aches for you,
like dry, worn-out land with no water.

That is why I have gazed at you in the sanctuary,
hoping to see your might and glory.

Your steady love is worth more than life,
so my lips will praise you.

I will bless you as long as I live.
I will raise my hands and pray in your name.

I will be as full as after a rich feast,
and my mouth will sing joyful praise to you,

when I remember you on my bed
and think of you during the night hours.

You have always come to my aid,
and under your wings’ shade I sing for joy.

I stay close to you.
Your right hand keeps me from falling.

But those who are out to ruin my life
will sink to the deepest parts of the earth.

The sword will get them.
Jackals will feast on them.

But the king will rejoice in God.
All who make promises in his name will celebrate,
while liars have their mouths shut.

notes.text: See 1 Samuel 22:5, 1 Samuel 23:14, and 2 Samuel 15:23–28.

chapters.title: A psalm of David, when he was in the desert of Judah.{a}

verses.text:
God, hear my complaint.
Keep my life safe from the terror of the enemy.

Hide me from the secret plots of evil people,
from the noisy mob of wrongdoers.

Their tongues are sharpened like swords.
Their bitter words are aimed like arrows,

shooting from hiding at the innocent.
They shoot suddenly and feel no fear.

They search out crimes and say,
“We have a perfect plot!”
The mind and heart of a person go deep.

But God will let fly an arrow at them.
All at once they will be hurt.

Their own tongues will make them trip.
Everyone watching them will gasp and look away.

Then everyone will be afraid.
They will tell what God has done
and think carefully about his work.

Good people will be glad in Yahweh
and hide in him.
All who are honest in heart will boast.

notes.text: The Hebrew says “see them.” Some Hebrew copies and the Syriac say “see us.”

chapters.title: For the music director. A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Praise is waiting for you{a} in Zion, God,
and promises will be kept to you.

You hear prayers,
so everyone will come to you.

My wrongs are too much for me,
but you wipe away our sins.

Happy is the one you pick out and welcome,
to live in your courtyards.
Your house will fill us with good things,
your holy temple.

You answer us with awesome acts of justice,
God who saves us.
You are the hope of everyone on earth
and of those far away on the seas.

By his power he set the mountains in place,
dressed in strength.

He quiets the roar of the seas,
the pounding of the waves,
and the uproar of the nations.

People at the far edges of the earth are amazed at your signs.
You make the east and the west shout for joy.

You visit the land and water it.
You make it rich and full.
God’s river is brimming with water.
You provide grain for people,
because this is how you ready the soil.

You soak the plowed rows.
You flatten the ridges.
You soften the soil with rain,
and you bless the plants that sprout.

You crown the year with your goodness,
and your wagon trails overflow with plenty.{b}

The desert pastures overflow,
and the hills wear joy like a coat.

The meadows are clothed with flocks.
The valleys are blanketed in grain.
Everything shouts and sings for joy.

notes.text: The Hebrew vowels say “Silence is praise to you.” The Septuagint says “Praise is right for you.”
Hebrew “drip with fat.” The picture is the wheel tracks of God’s chariot pouring out plenty as it passes.

chapters.title: For the music director. A psalm of David. A song.

verses.text: Everyone on earth, cheer for God!

Sing about the glory of his name.
Make his praise glorious.

Tell God, “Your deeds are awesome!
Your power is so great that your enemies pretend to obey you.

The whole earth bows to you.
They sing to you.
They sing about your name.”
Selah

Come and look at what God has done.
He is awe-inspiring in how he treats human beings.

By his might he rules forever.
His eyes keep a lookout over the nations.
Let rebels not lift themselves up.{b}
Selah

Peoples, bless our God.
Let the sound of his praise be heard.

He preserves our lives
and does not let our feet slip.

God, you put us through a test.
You have refined us as people refine silver.

You led us into a trap.
You put a heavy load on our backs.

I will enter your house with burnt offerings
and keep every promise I made to you,

the promises my lips made
and my mouth spoke when I was in trouble.

I will offer you fat animals as burnt offerings,
with the smoke of rams.
I will offer bulls and goats.
Selah

Everyone who fears God, come and hear,
and I will describe what he has done for my life.

I cried to him aloud,
and praise was ready on my tongue.

If I had held on to sin in my heart,
the Lord would not have listened.

But God really did listen.
He gave my prayer his attention.

Blessed be God,
who did not turn my prayer away
or take his faithful love from me.

notes.text: Compare Exodus 14:21–22 and Joshua 3:14–17.
Some Hebrew copies spell this word differently. The meaning is the same.
The Hebrew says “to plenty.” The Septuagint, the Syriac, and Jerome say “to a place of rest.”

chapters.title: For the music director. A song. A psalm.

verses.text:
Then everyone on earth will know your ways,
and every nation will see how you save.

Let the peoples thank you, God.
Let all the peoples thank you.

Let the nations be glad and sing out loud,
because you judge the peoples fairly
and lead the nations of the earth.
Selah

Let the peoples thank you, God.
Let all the peoples thank you.

The earth has given its harvest.
God, our own God, blesses us.

May God bless us,
and may all the far corners of the earth fear him.

notes.text: This echoes the priests’ blessing in Numbers 6:24–26.

chapters.title: For the music director, with stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.

verses.text:
God stands up, and his enemies scatter.
Those who hate him run from his face.{a}

As smoke is blown off by the wind, blow them off.
As wax melts near a fire,
let the wicked be lost before God.

But let good people be glad and celebrate in front of God.
Let them burst with joy.

In his holy home, God
is a father to orphans and a defender of widows.

God gives lonely people a family to live with.
He leads prisoners out to a good life,
but rebels live in a scorched land.

God, when you went out in front of your people,
when you marched across the wasteland,
Selah

You poured out generous rain, God.
Your tired land was made new by you.

Your flock{e} settled there.
God, from your goodness you gave to the poor.

The Lord gives the order.
A huge army of women bring the news:{f}

“Kings and their armies run away, run away!”
The woman at home divides up what was taken.

When Shaddai{h} scattered the kings there,
it snowed on Zalmon.{i}

Bashan’s mountain is a mountain of God.
Bashan’s mountain has many peaks.

Why are you jealous, you mountains with many peaks,
of the mountain God chose as his home?
Yes, Yahweh will live there forever.

God’s chariots number tens of thousands and thousands more.
The Lord is among them. Sinai has come into the holy place.{j}

Blessed be the Lord, who carries us{l} every day.
He is the God who saves us.
Selah

Our God is a God who rescues.
Yahweh the Lord holds the ways out of death.

Surely God will smash the heads of his enemies,
the hairy scalps of those who keep walking in guilt.

The Lord has said, “I will bring them back out of Bashan.
I will bring them up from the ocean floor,

so you can dip your foot in blood,{m}
and your dogs’ tongues can have a share of the enemy.”

Your parades are seen, God,
the parades of my God and King into the holy place.

Singers go first, and musicians come last.
Young women playing tambourines are in the middle.

“Bless God in the great gatherings.
Bless Yahweh, you who come from Israel’s spring.”

There is little Benjamin, leading the way.
There are the princes of Judah with their crowd,
the princes of Zebulun and the princes of Naphtali.

Your God has ordered your strength.{n}
Show that strength now, God, the way you did for us in the past.

Because of your temple above Jerusalem,
kings will bring you gifts.

Messengers will come from Egypt.
Cush{q} will hurry to lift her hands to God.

Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God.
Make music for the Lord.
Selah

He rides in the ancient heavens.
Hear it: his voice rolls out, a mighty voice.

Give God the credit for his power.
His majesty rests on Israel,
and his strength is in the clouds.

God, you are awesome in your holy place.
Israel’s God gives power and strength to his people.
Praise God!

notes.text: Compare Numbers 10:35, the cry when the ark set out.
Or “praise him who rides on the clouds.” Hebrew ‘arabot means “desert plains.” Compare verse 33.
Yah is the short form of the name Yahweh. Compare Exodus 15:2.
Or “even Sinai shook.” Compare Judges 5:4–5.
Hebrew chayyah, “living thing.” It may mean “your flock” or “your people.”
The Hebrew word for the bringers of news is feminine. Compare Exodus 15:20 and 1 Samuel 18:6.
The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain. Compare Judges 5:16.
Shaddai is the name often translated “the Almighty.”
Zalmon is a hill near Shechem (Judges 9:48). Another reading is “it snowed in the dark.” The verse is hard to read.
Or “the Lord has come from Sinai into the holy place,” with a small change to the Hebrew.
Ephesians 4:8 quotes this line as “he gave gifts to people,” like the Aramaic translation and the Syriac.
Or “who carries our loads.”
The Hebrew says “crush.” The Septuagint and the Syriac say “dip your foot.”
The Hebrew says “has ordered your strength.” The Septuagint, the Syriac, and some Hebrew copies say “Order your strength, God.”
This is probably Egypt, pictured as a crocodile or hippopotamus.
Or “until each one gives in with bars of silver.” The Hebrew is very hard.
Cush is the upper Nile region, south of Egypt.

chapters.title: For the music director. By David. A psalm. A song.

subheads.19: Praise the Lord Who Carries Us

verses.text:
Help me, God,
for the flood has risen to my chin.{a}

I am stuck in thick mud
where I find no footing.
I have slipped into the depths,
and the current is carrying me off.

I am worn out from shouting. My throat is dry.
My eyes give out as I wait for my God.

More people hate me for no reason{b}
than I have hairs on my head.
Strong enemies who lie about me want to destroy me.
Must I give back
what I never stole?

God, you know how senseless I have been,
and none of my wrongs are secret from you.

May no one waiting on you be disgraced because of what happens to me,
Lord Yahweh of Armies.
May no one searching for you be embarrassed through me,
God of Israel.

I have put up with insults for your sake,
and shame has covered my face.

My own brothers treat me like a stranger,
and my mother’s sons treat me like an outsider.

My love for your house has eaten me up,{c}
and the insults of those who insult you have landed on me.{d}

When I cried and went without food,
people used it to make fun of me.

When I put on sackcloth,
they turned me into a joke.

People sitting at the town gate gossip about me,
and drunks make up songs to mock me.

To you I direct my prayer, Yahweh,
in the season of your favor.
God, because your faithful love is so great,
answer me with your sure rescue.

Drag me out of this muck so that I do not go under.
Keep me away from those who hate me,
and out of the deep water.

Do not let the flood roll over me,
the deep gulp me down,
or the pit close its mouth above me.

Answer me, Yahweh, since your faithful love is so good.
Because you are so tender, turn toward me.

Do not turn your face from your servant.
Trouble is crushing me. Answer me fast!

Come near and buy me back.
Free me, since my enemies are all around.

You know what I put up with in insults,
my shame and humiliation.
Every one of my enemies is in your view.

Insults have crushed my heart, and I feel ill.
I hoped someone would feel sorry for me, but no one did.
I hoped for comforters, but I found none.

They mixed poison{e} into my meal,
and for my thirst they offered me sour wine.{f}

Let their table in front of them become a trap,
and their safe times become a snare.{g}

Let their eyes go dark so they cannot see,
and let their backs shake all the time.

Pour your fury out on them,
and let your burning anger catch them.

Let their camp turn into ruins.
Let no one live in their tents.{h}

They go after the one you hurt,
and they gossip about the pain of the ones you wounded.

Pile guilt on top of their guilt.
Let them have no part in your goodness.

May their names be scratched out of the book of life,
and kept off the list of good people.

But I am poor and in pain.
God, may your saving help set me high out of reach.

My song will praise God’s name,
and my thanks will honor him.

This will please Yahweh more than an ox,
more than a young bull with horns and split hooves.

The poor have seen it and are glad.
You who search for God, let your hearts revive.

Yahweh listens to the needy
and does not look down on his people in chains.

Let heaven and earth praise him,
with the seas and everything that moves in them.

Yes, God will rescue Zion
and rebuild the towns of Judah.
His people will settle there and own it.

The children of his servants will inherit it,
and those who love his name will make their homes there.

notes.text: Hebrew nephesh, used here in its basic meaning, “throat” or “neck.”
John 15:25 quotes this line.
John 2:17 quotes this line.
Romans 15:3 quotes this line.
Hebrew rosh, a bitter, poisonous plant. The Septuagint says “gall.”
Compare Matthew 27:34, Matthew 27:48, and John 19:28–29.
Or “and their peace offerings a snare.” Romans 11:9–10 quotes verses 22–23 from the Septuagint.
Acts 1:20 quotes this verse.

chapters.title: For the music director, to the tune “Lilies.” By David.

subheads.13: Pull Me Out of the Mud
subheads.22: May Their Table Be a Trap

verses.text:
God, hurry to save me!
Yahweh, hurry to help me!

May those who are after my life
be ashamed and confused.
May those who enjoy my pain
be pushed back in disgrace.

May those who say “Ha! Ha!”
turn back, paid in shame.

May all who search for you
be glad and joyful in you.
May those who love your saving help
keep saying, “God is great!”

I am poor and in need.
God, come quickly to me!
You are the one who helps and frees me.
Yahweh, do not be late.

notes.text: Compare the title of Psalm 38. This psalm is very close to Psalm 40:13–17. In the Hebrew numbering the title is verse 1, so the Hebrew has six verses.

chapters.title: For the music director. By David. To bring to mind.{a}

verses.text:
Yahweh, I run to you for safety.{a}
Never let me be shamed.

Because you do right, rescue me and set me free.
Lean down, hear me, and save me.

Be a rock where I can live,
a place I can always go.
You have ordered my rescue,
because you are my rock and my fortress.

My God, snatch me from the wicked,
from the grip of cruel and unfair people.

You are my hope, Lord Yahweh,
my trust since I was a boy.

Many people see me as a warning sign,
but you are my strong shelter.

My mouth is full of praise for you,
and of your splendor all day long.

Do not toss me out in my old age.
Do not desert me when my strength fails.

My enemies are talking about me.
Those who watch for a chance to kill me plot together.

They say, “God has left him.
Chase him and grab him,
because no one will save him.”

God, do not keep your distance.
My God, run to help me.{c}

May those who accuse me be shamed and finished.
May those who want to hurt me
be wrapped in insults and disgrace.

But I will keep hoping always,
and praise you more and more.

My mouth will tell of your goodness
and your acts of rescue all day,
though there are more than I can count.

I will come in the power of the Lord Yahweh.
Your goodness, and yours alone, is what I will mention.

God, you have been my teacher from my youth,
and even now I tell of your wonders.

Now that I am old, with gray in my hair,
God, do not leave me,
until I tell this generation about your strong arm,
and everyone to come about your power.

Your goodness, God, reaches the heights.
You have done great things.
God, who can compare with you?

You let me go through{d} many bitter troubles,
but you will bring me back to life.
From the deep places of the earth
you will lift me up again.

You will make me greater than before
and comfort me again.

My harp will praise you too,
for you are faithful, my God.
My lyre will make music for you,
Holy One of Israel.

My lips will sing out loud when I make music for you,
and so will my soul, which you bought back.

My tongue will talk about your goodness all day,
because those who wanted to hurt me
have been shamed and disgraced.

notes.text: This psalm has no title. Verses 1–3 are very close to Psalm 31:1–3.
Or “who cut my cord.” The Hebrew word is uncertain.
Some Hebrew copies spell this word differently.
Some Hebrew copies say “us” here and in the next lines.

subheads.7: Do Not Leave Me When I Am Old
subheads.17: Teaching You Since I Was Young
subheads.22: I Will Sing With the Harp

verses.text:
God, give the king your sense of what is fair,
and the king’s son your own goodness.

Let him judge your people with honesty
and your poor people with fairness.

May the mountains bring peace to the people,
and the hills bring goodness.

May he defend the poor among the people,
rescue the children of the needy,
and crush the one who bullies them.

May people honor you{b} for as long as the sun shines,
and for as long as the moon, through every age.

May he be like rain on a freshly cut field,
like showers that soak the ground.

May good people thrive in his time,
and may peace be everywhere until the moon is no more.

May his rule reach from sea to sea,
and from the River{c} to the ends of the earth.

May tribes of the desert kneel before him,
and his enemies lick the dust.

May the kings of Tarshish and the faraway coasts
bring him gifts.
May the kings of Sheba and Seba
hand over presents.

May every king bow to him,
and every nation serve him.

He saves the needy who call for help,
the poor, and anyone with no helper.

He feels sorry for the weak and needy,
and he saves the lives of the needy.

He buys their lives back from cruelty and violence,
and their blood is precious to him.

Long live the king! May Sheba’s gold be given to him.
May people pray for him constantly
and bless him all day long.

May the land overflow with grain,
waving on the mountaintops.
May its crops rustle like the trees of Lebanon,
and may city people bloom like grass on the earth.

May his name last forever.
May his fame{d} go on as long as the sun shines.
May every nation be blessed through him,{e}
and call him happy.

Blessed be Yahweh God, Israel’s God,
who alone does wonders.
Here end the prayers of David, Jesse’s son.{g}

notes.text: Or “For Solomon.” This is a prayer for the king. It closes Book Two.
The Hebrew says “may they fear you.” The Septuagint says “may he last.”
The River is the Euphrates.
Some Hebrew copies say “may his name sprout.”
Compare Genesis 12:3 and 22:18.
Verses 18–19 are the blessing that ends Book Two of the Psalms. Compare 41:13, 89:52, 106:48, and Psalm 150.
This note closes an earlier collection of David’s psalms. Some psalms of David come after it, such as 86, 101, 103, 108–110, and 138–145.

chapters.title: By Solomon.{a}

verses.text:
God is truly good to Israel,
to those with clean hearts.

But my feet almost went off the path.{b}
My steps nearly slid away.

I envied the proud
when I saw how the wicked do well.

They have no pain until they die.{c}
Their bodies are healthy and fat.

They do not share the hard work of ordinary people.
They are not hit with trouble like others.

So pride hangs on them like a necklace,
and violence covers them like a robe.

Their eyes bulge from so much fat.{d}
Their hearts spill over with plans.

They mock and speak with spite.
From high places they talk of crushing people.

They aim their mouths at the sky,
and their tongues strut across the earth.

So God’s people turn to them,{e}
and drink up all the water they offer.{f}

They say, “How could God find out?
Does the Most High know a thing?”

Look at them: this is what the wicked are like.
They are always comfortable and keep piling up riches.

It was pointless, then, to keep my heart clean
and to wash my hands to show I was innocent.

I am hit all day long,
and I am corrected every morning.

If I had said, “I will talk this way,”
I would have betrayed your children’s generation.

When I tried to figure it out,
it was too hard for me,

until I went into God’s holy places.{g}
Then I understood where they end up.

You put them on slippery ground.
You throw them down to ruin.

How quickly they are wiped out!
Terrors sweep them completely away.

Like a dream when someone wakes up, Lord,
when you get up, you will despise the shadows they were.

When my heart was bitter
and I felt stabbed deep inside,{h}

I was foolish and understood nothing.
I was like an animal toward you.

Still, I am always with you.
You hold my right hand.

You will guide me with your advice,
and then take me into glory.{i}

Whom do I have in heaven besides you?
Nothing on earth is what I want besides you.

My body and my heart may fail,
yet God remains the rock{j} of my heart, and my share forever.

Look! Those who keep far from you will be lost.
You destroy all who are unfaithful to you.

But for me, being near God is good.
I have made the Lord Yahweh my hiding place,
so I can tell about everything you do.

notes.text: Book Three of the Psalms begins here and ends with the blessing at 89:52. Psalms 73–83 are a group credited to Asaph, a Levite singer David put in charge. See 1 Chronicles 15:17 and 25:1.
Some Hebrew copies use different forms of both verbs. The meaning is the same.
Or, dividing the Hebrew differently, “they have no pain; their bodies are healthy and fat.”
The Hebrew says “from fat.” The Septuagint and the Syriac say “their sin comes out of fat.”
This follows the written Hebrew. The reading in the margin says “he brings his people back here.”
The meaning of the Hebrew in this verse is uncertain.
Or “God’s holy things.”
Hebrew “kidneys,” where feelings were thought to live.
Or “take me to glory.”
Hebrew tsur, “rock.”

chapters.heading: Book Three (Psalms 73–89)
chapters.title: A psalm of Asaph.{a}

subheads.27: Close to God Is My Good

verses.text:
God, why have you thrown us away for good?
Why does your anger smoke against the sheep you feed?

Remember the people you bought long ago,
the family you set free as your own,
Mount Zion, where you have made your home.

Walk over to the ruins that never end,
everything the enemy has wrecked in the holy place.

Your enemies roared in the middle of your meeting place.
They set up their own flags there as signs.

They looked like men swinging axes
up into a thick grove of trees.{b}

Now they smash all its carved panels{c}
with hatchets and hammers.

They set your holy place on fire.
They made the home of your name unholy by tearing it to the ground.

They said to themselves, “Let’s flatten them all.”
They burned every place in the land where God was worshiped.

We cannot see any signs.
No prophet is left,
and none of us knows how long it will go on.

God, how long will the enemy taunt you?
Will the foe insult your name without end?

Why do you keep your hand back, your right hand?
Pull it out from the fold of your robe{d} and finish them!

Yet God has been my King since long ago,
bringing rescue to the earth.

With your power you divided the sea.
The heads of the sea monsters in the waters were smashed by you.

You crushed the heads of Leviathan.{e}
You handed him over as meat for desert people.{f}

You cut open springs and streams.
You dried up rivers that never ran dry.

Day belongs to you, and so does night.
The moon{g} and sun were set in place by you.

You marked every border of the earth.
Both summer and winter came from you.

Remember this, Yahweh: the enemy insults you,
and a foolish people sneers at your name.

Do not hand your dove’s life to wild beasts.
Do not forget your poor people’s lives forever.

Remember your agreement,
because the dark corners of the land are full of violent hideouts.

Do not let the crushed go home shamed.
Let the poor and needy praise your name.

Get up, God, and argue your own case.
Remember how fools mock you every day.

Do not forget the shouting of your enemies,
the roar of those who rise against you, which never stops.

notes.text: This is a cry about the destruction of the temple, most likely by the Babylonians in 587 BC. See 2 Kings 25:8–9. For maskil, see Psalm 32.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
Some Hebrew copies spell this word differently.
This follows the margin note in the Hebrew. The written text says “your law.”
Leviathan is a many-headed sea serpent, a picture of chaos. Compare Job 41 and Isaiah 27:1.
Or “to the creatures of the desert.”
Hebrew “the light,” probably the moon.

chapters.title: A maskil of Asaph.{a}

subheads.22: Get Up and Argue Your Case

verses.text:
God, we are thanking you, thanking you, for your name is close.{a}
People tell about your wonderful deeds.

“When the time I have picked arrives,
I will judge with fairness.

When the earth and all its people shake,
I am the one who holds its pillars firm.
Selah

I tell the proud, ‘Stop bragging.’
I tell the wicked, ‘Do not raise your horn.{b}

Do not raise your horn high
or talk with your head held stiff.’”

Promotion does not arrive from the sunrise or the sunset,
or from the wilderness.{c}

It is God who judges.
He pulls one person down and lifts another up.

Yahweh holds a cup in his hand.
The wine in it foams and is spiced,
and he pours it out.

But I will tell about it forever.
I will sing praise to the God of Jacob.

“I will chop off every horn the wicked have,
but I will raise up the horns of the good.”

notes.text: The Hebrew says “your name is near.” The Septuagint says “we will call on your name.”
A horn pictures strength and pride. See also verses 5 and 10.
Or “from the desert of the mountains.”

chapters.title: For the music director, to the tune “Do Not Destroy.” A psalm of Asaph. A song.

verses.text:
God is known in Judah.
His name is great in Israel.

His tent{a} is set up in Salem.{b}
His den is in Zion.

There he snapped the blazing arrows,
the shield, the sword, and all the gear of war.
Selah

You shine,
more glorious than the mountains full of prey.{c}

The brave were robbed of their loot.
They sank into sleep.
None of the soldiers could lift a hand.

At your shout, God of Jacob,
both chariot and horse froze.

You are the one to be feared.
Once you are angry, who can hold their ground before you?

From heaven you gave your verdict.
The earth was afraid and went quiet

when God stood up to judge,
to rescue all the humble people of the earth.
Selah

Even human rage will bring you praise.
What is left of the rage, you will wear like a belt.{d}

Make your promises to Yahweh your God, and keep them.
Everyone near him should carry gifts to the Awesome One.

He cuts short the lives of rulers.
The kings of the earth tremble before him.

notes.text: Or “his hut.” The picture is a lion’s thicket.
Salem is an old name for Jerusalem. Compare Genesis 14:18.
The Hebrew says “mountains of prey.” The Septuagint says “everlasting mountains.”
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.

chapters.title: For the music director, with stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.

verses.text:
I lift my voice to God and shout.
I lift my voice to God, so he will hear me.

In my day of trouble I searched for the Lord.
At night I held out my hand and never tired.
My soul would not be comforted.

I think of God and I groan.
I wonder, and my spirit grows faint.
Selah

You keep my eyes from closing.
I am too upset to speak.

I think about days long ago,
years from ages past.

I remember my songs in the night.
I talk with my heart,
and my spirit searches for answers:

“Will the Lord reject us forever?
Will he never be kind again?

Has his faithful love ended for good?
Has his promise failed for all time?

Has God forgotten how to be kind?
Has his anger shut off his tenderness?”
Selah

Then I said, “This is what hurts me:
the right hand of the Most High has changed.”{b}

I will recall the deeds of Yah.{c}
Yes, I will remember your wonders from long ago.

I will go over everything you have done
and think about your mighty acts.

God, your way is holy.
Is any god as great as ours?

You are the God who does wonders.
You showed your power among the peoples.

With your strong arm you bought your people back,
the children of Jacob and Joseph.
Selah

The waters saw you, God.
The waters saw you and twisted in fear.
Even the deep places shook.

The clouds poured out rain.
The skies rumbled with thunder.
Your arrows flashed in every direction.

Your thunder rolled in the whirlwind.
Lightning lit up the world.
The earth shook and trembled.

Your road ran through the sea,
your path through the mighty waters,
but no one saw your footprints.

Moses and Aaron were your hands,
and you led your people like a flock.

notes.text: Some Hebrew copies spell the name differently. Compare Psalms 39 and 62.
Or “I will appeal to the years of the right hand of the Most High.” The Hebrew is uncertain.
Yah is the short form of the name Yahweh. Some Hebrew copies read “I will recall the deeds of Yah.”

chapters.title: For the music director, for Jeduthun.{a} By Asaph. A psalm.

subheads.13: Your Road Went Through the Sea

verses.text:
My people, listen to my teaching.{b}
Pay close attention to my words.

My mouth will open with a story.
I will pour out puzzles from long ago,{c}

things we have heard and learned,
which our ancestors told us.

We will not hide them from their children.
We will tell the next generation
about Yahweh’s praiseworthy deeds and his power,
and the wonders he did.

He set up a reminder in Jacob
and made a law for Israel.
He ordered our ancestors
to pass it on to their children,

so that the generation after them would know it,
the children still to be born,
and these in turn would pass it to theirs.

Then they would put their hope in God,
and not forget what God has done.
They would keep his commands.

They would not copy their ancestors,
a stubborn people who would not listen,
people whose hearts were not steady,
whose spirits were not loyal to God.

The men of Ephraim carried bows and were armed{d},
but on the day of battle they turned and fled.

They did not honor God’s agreement,
and they refused to live by his law.

They forgot what he had done,
and the wonders he had shown them.

While their ancestors watched, he did wonders
in Egypt’s land, on the plain of Zoan.{e}

He cut the sea in two and walked them across.
The water piled up like a wall.

In the daytime he led them with a cloud.
All night long he led them with firelight.

He split rocks in the desert
and gave them water as if from the deep sea.

Streams came pouring from a cliff,
and water ran down like rivers.

But they went on sinning against him,
rebelling in the desert against the Most High.

Inside they tested God
by insisting on the food they wanted.

They talked against God. They said,
“Can God set a table in the desert?

Yes, he hit the rock, and water gushed out.
Streams poured down.
But can he give bread as well?
Can he supply meat to his people?”

When Yahweh heard this, he was angry.
A fire blazed against Jacob,
and his anger flared against Israel,

They did not believe God,
and they did not rely on him to save them.

Still, he gave an order to the clouds above
and opened the doors of heaven.

He rained down manna for them to eat
and gave them grain from heaven.

People ate angels’ bread.{f}
He sent more food than they could finish.

He stirred up the east wind in the sky
and drove the south wind with his power.

He rained meat on them like dust,
and birds like the sand of the sea.

He let them fall inside their camp,
right beside their tents.

They ate and ate until they were full,
because he gave them what they craved.

But they had not yet given up their craving.
Meat was still between their teeth

Even so, they kept sinning.
They did not believe his wonders.

So he ended their days like a puff of air,
and their years in sudden terror.

Whenever he killed some, the rest looked for him.
They turned back and eagerly searched for God.

They remembered that God was their rock,
and that God Most High was the one who bought them back.

But they flattered him with their mouths
and lied to him with their tongues.

Their hearts were not firm toward him.
They did not stay true to his agreement.

Yet he was full of tenderness.
He forgave their guilt and did not destroy them.
Time after time he held back his anger
and refused to unleash all his fury.

He recalled that they were only flesh,
a wind that blows past and never returns.

How many times they rebelled against him in the desert
and made him sad in the wasteland!

Over and over they tested God
and hurt{h} the Holy One of Israel.

They did not remember his power,
or the day he bought them back from the enemy,

when he did his signs in Egypt
and his wonders in the fields of Zoan.

Their rivers became blood,
and they could not drink from their streams.

Swarms of flies came and ate them up.
Frogs came and ruined them.

Their crops went to grasshoppers,
and what they had worked for went to the locusts.

Hail destroyed their vines,
and frost destroyed their fig trees.{i}

He gave their cattle to the hail,
and their herds to lightning.

He let loose on them his burning anger,
his fury, rage, and trouble,
a team of messengers who bring disaster.

He cleared a path for his anger.
He gave no rescue from death,
but handed their lives over to plague.

He struck down the oldest son in every Egyptian home,
the first of their strength, in the tents of Ham.{j}

Next he led out his own people like sheep
and guided them through the desert like a flock.

He led them safely, with nothing to fear,
while the sea closed over their enemies.

He brought them to the edge of his holy land,
to this mountain, which his right hand had won.

He drove nations out ahead of them.
He gave them their inheritance with a measuring line
and settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.

But they put God Most High to the test and fought against him.
They did not keep his reminders.

They turned away and were as unfaithful as their ancestors.
They twisted like a warped bow.

They made him angry with their hilltop altars.
They made him jealous with their carved idols.

When God heard it, he was furious.
He completely turned his back on Israel.

He gave up his home at Shiloh,{k}
the tent he had set up among people,

and handed over his strength{l} to be captured,
his glory into enemy hands.

He gave his people to the sword
and was furious with those who were his own.

Flames swallowed their young men,
and no wedding songs were sung for their young women.

Swords cut down their priests,
and their widows could not cry.{m}

Then the Lord woke up like someone from sleep,
like a strong man shouting from too much wine.

He drove his enemies back.
He gave them shame that would last.

He turned down Joseph’s tents
and passed over the tribe of Ephraim.

His pick was Judah,
and beloved Mount Zion.

He built his holy place like the heights,{n}
like the earth, which he set up to last forever.

He picked out his servant David
and took him from the sheep pens.

From following the nursing sheep he brought him
to be shepherd of Jacob, his people,
and of Israel, his own inheritance.

David led them as a shepherd, with a heart of integrity,
and guided them with skillful hands.

notes.text: This is a long teaching psalm that tells Israel’s story from the exodus to David. Compare Psalms 105 and 106. Maskil is a word of uncertain meaning.
Hebrew torah, “teaching.”
Matthew 13:35 quotes this verse.
Hebrew “armed ones, shooters of the bow.”
Zoan is a city in the eastern Nile delta. It is also called Tanis.
Or “the bread of angels,” as the Septuagint has it.
Compare Numbers 11:31–34.
Or “made angry” or “set limits on.” The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
Ham is a poetic name for Egypt. See Genesis 10:6.
Compare 1 Samuel 4 and Jeremiah 7:12–14.
This means the ark of the agreement. Compare Psalm 132:8.
Compare 1 Samuel 4:11 and 4:19–22.
Or “like the high heavens.”

chapters.title: A maskil by Asaph.{a}

verses.text:
God, foreign nations have marched into the land that is yours.
They have made your holy temple unclean
and left Jerusalem a pile of stones.

The bodies of your servants
lie there as food for the birds of the sky,
and the flesh of your faithful people feeds wild animals.

Their blood ran like water
all around Jerusalem,
and no one was left to bury them.

Our neighbors look down on us.
Everyone around us laughs and sneers.

How long, Yahweh? Will you stay angry for good?
Will your jealous fury keep burning like a fire?

Pour your rage out on nations that have never known you,
on kingdoms that never pray to you by name.

They have devoured Jacob
and wrecked his home.

Help us, God who saves us,
for the honor of your name.
Rescue us and wipe away our sins
for your name’s sake.

Why should the nations ask,
“Where is their God?”
Show the nations, right in front of us,
that you pay back those who shed your servants’ blood.

Pay our neighbors back seven times over,{c}
for the insults they hurled at you, Lord.

Then we, your people, the sheep of your pasture,
will thank you forever.
From one generation to the next, we will tell your praise.

notes.text: Or “our own earlier wrongs.”
Hebrew “the sons of death.”
Hebrew “into their lap,” the fold of a robe used as a pocket.

chapters.title: A psalm of Asaph.

subheads.9: Help Us for Your Name’s Sake

verses.text:
Shepherd of Israel, hear us,
you who lead Joseph as a flock.
You who sit on the throne above the winged guardians,{a} shine out

in front of Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh.
Call up your strength
and come to save us.

Bring us back, God.
Let your face glow, and we will be rescued.{b}

Yahweh, God of Armies,
how long will you be angry when your people pray?

You fed them bread made of tears
and gave them tears to drink by the bowlful.{c}

You let our neighbors fight over us,
and our enemies laugh among themselves.

God of Armies, bring us back.
Let your face glow, and we will be rescued.

You pulled up a vine in Egypt.
You pushed out nations and planted it in their place.

You cleared the ground for it.
It sank deep roots and covered the land.

Its shade covered the mountains,
and its branches covered the giant cedars.{d}

It sent its branches to the Sea
and its shoots to the River.{e}

Why did you knock down its walls,
so that everyone walking by picks its fruit?

Wild pigs from the forest tear at it,
and field animals graze on it.

God of Armies, please return!
Look down from heaven and notice.
Look after this vine,

the root{f} that your own right hand set in the ground,
the young branch you made strong for yourself.

It has been chopped down and burned.
May they be destroyed when you frown at them.

Put your hand on the man beside you,
the human being you made strong for yourself.

After that we will not walk away from you.
Revive us, and we will cry out your name.

Yahweh, God of Armies, bring us back.
Let your face glow, and we will be rescued.

notes.text: These are the winged figures over the ark of the agreement. Compare Exodus 25:18–22.
This chorus comes back, a little fuller each time, in verses 7 and 19.
Hebrew shalish, “a third,” a measure of about a third of an ephah.
Hebrew “the cedars of God.”
The Sea is the Mediterranean, and the River is the Euphrates.
The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.

chapters.title: For the music director, to the tune “Lilies.” A reminder. By Asaph. A psalm.

subheads.14: Look Down and Care for This Vine

verses.text:
Sing for joy to God, our strength.
Cheer for the God of Jacob.

Raise a song and beat the tambourine,
and play the pleasant lyre with the harp.

Sound the ram’s horn when the new moon comes,
and again at full moon, on our feast day.{b}

This is Israel’s rule,
an order given by the God of Jacob.

“I took the weight off his shoulder.
His hands were free of the basket.{e}

You called in trouble, and I saved you.
I replied from the thundercloud.
At the waters of Meribah{f} I put you to the test.
Selah

Hear me, my people, while I warn you.
Israel, how I wish you would pay attention!

Do not keep a foreign god among you.
Do not bow down to a god from another land.

I am Yahweh your God,
who brought you up out of Egypt.
Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.

“But my people refused to listen.
Israel wanted none of me.

So I left them to follow their own hard-headed ways,
and their own plans.

If only my people would hear me,
if only Israel would live by my ways,

I would quickly bring their enemies down
and turn my hand against their foes.

Those who hate Yahweh would shrink back in front of him,
and their punishment{g} would last forever.

But I would give you{h} the best wheat to eat,
and fill you with honey from the rock.”

notes.text: See the title of Psalm 8.
This was probably the Feast of Booths in the seventh month. See Leviticus 23:24 and 23:34.
Or “over.”
Or “I heard a language I did not know.”
This basket was for carrying clay or bricks. Compare Exodus 1:11–14.
Meribah means “quarreling.” Compare Exodus 17:1–7 and Numbers 20:1–13.
Hebrew “their time.”
Hebrew “him,” meaning Israel.

chapters.title: For the music director, on the gittith.{a} By Asaph.

verses.text:
God takes his place in the heavenly court.{a}
Among the gods he gives his decision.

“How long will you judge unfairly
and favor the wicked?
Selah

Defend the weak and children without fathers.
Stand up for the rights of the suffering and the broke.

Free the weak and the poor.
Pull them out of the hands of the wicked.”

They know nothing and understand nothing.
They stumble around in the dark.
The foundations of the earth are shaking.

“I said, ‘You are gods.
All of you are sons of the Most High.

But you will die as human beings die.
You will fall like any other ruler.’”

Rise, God, and judge the earth,
for every nation is your possession.

notes.text: Hebrew ‘adat-’el, “the assembly of God” or “of El.” The “gods” (elohim) in verses 1 and 6 are the heavenly beings who serve God and are held to account by him. Some think they are human rulers.

chapters.title: A psalm of Asaph.

verses.text:
God, do not stay quiet.
Do not hold back or stay still.

Look, your enemies are making a racket.
Those who hate you have lifted up their heads.

They make sly plans against your people.
They plot against those you hide away.

They say, “Come on, let us erase them as a nation,
so Israel’s name is never mentioned again.”

They are all of one mind in their plot.
They have formed an alliance against you:

the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites,
Moab and the Hagrites,

Gebal{a} and Ammon and Amalek,
Philistia with the people of Tyre.

Treat them as you treated Midian,
as you treated Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon Valley,{d}

who were destroyed at En-dor
and became fertilizer for the ground.

Make their leaders like Oreb and Zeeb,
and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,

who said, “Let us take over
the pastures that belong to God.”

My God, make them like a tumbleweed in a whirlwind,{e}
like chaff blown by the wind.

As fire burns through a forest,
as flames set the mountains ablaze,

so chase them with your windstorm
and frighten them with your hurricane.

Cover their faces with shame,
so they will look for your name, Yahweh.

Let them be shamed and afraid forever.
Let them be disgraced and die,

so they will know that you alone, whose name is Yahweh,
are the Most High over all the earth.

notes.text: This is probably Byblos on the Phoenician coast, or a region south of the Dead Sea.
Hebrew “arm.”
Moab and Ammon were Lot’s descendants. See Genesis 19:36–38.
Compare Judges 4–8.
Or “tumbleweed.” Hebrew galgal means “wheel.”

chapters.title: A song. A psalm of Asaph.

subheads.13: Let Them Know You Are the Most High

verses.text:
How lovely is the place where you live,
Yahweh of Armies!

My soul longs for the courts of Yahweh.
It even grows faint for them.
My heart and my body sing with joy
to the living God.

Even the sparrow has found a house,
and the swallow has built a nest for herself,
where she can lay her chicks,
near your altars, Yahweh of Armies,
my King and my God.

Happy are the ones who stay in your house.
They never stop praising you.
Selah

Those who find their strength in you are happy,
those who have set their hearts on the roads to Zion.{a}

They grow stronger as they walk,
and each one appears before God in Zion.

Yahweh, God of Armies, hear my prayer.
Listen, God of Jacob.
Selah

Look at our shield, God,{d}
and see the face of the king you chose.

A single day in your courtyards beats
a thousand days spent anywhere else.{e}
I would rather be a doorkeeper in my God’s house
than live in the tents of the wicked.

Yahweh God is a sun and a shield.
Yahweh gives favor and honor.
He keeps back nothing good
from people who live with integrity.

Yahweh of Armies,
happy is the one who trusts in you.

notes.text: Hebrew “the highways.” These are the pilgrim roads to Jerusalem.
Or “the valley of tears” or “of balsam trees.”
Or “pools,” with different vowels.
Or “God, our shield, look.” The shield is the king. Compare 89:18.
Hebrew “than a thousand.”

chapters.title: For the music director, on the gittith. By the sons of Korah. A psalm.

verses.text:
Yahweh, you were kind to your land.
You brought Jacob’s people back from captivity.{a}

You took away your people’s guilt.
You covered all their sin.
Selah

You put away all your fury.
You turned from your burning anger.

Bring us back again, God who saves us,
and end your anger toward us.

Will you be angry with us forever?
Will you keep your anger up for every generation?

Will you not bring us back to life,
so your people can celebrate in you?

Let us see your faithful love, Yahweh,
and give us your rescue.

I will listen to what God, Yahweh, says.
He will speak peace to his people, to his faithful ones,
as long as they do not return to foolish ways.

His rescue is near to those who fear him,
so glory can make its home in our land.

Faithful love and truth have met.
Goodness and peace have kissed.

Truth sprouts from the soil,
and goodness looks down from the sky.

Yes, Yahweh will give what is good,
and our land will give its harvest.

Goodness will walk in front of him
and make a road for his steps.{b}

notes.text: Or “restored the fortunes of Jacob.”
Or “and will put us on the road of his steps.”

chapters.title: For the music director. By the sons of Korah. A psalm.

verses.text:
Lean down and answer me, Yahweh.
I am poor and in need.

Be kind to me, Lord,
because I call to you all day.

Make your servant’s soul glad,
because I lift my soul to you, Lord.

You, Lord, are good and quick to forgive.
You are rich in faithful love for everyone who calls to you.

Hear my prayer, Yahweh.
Listen to my cries for mercy.

On my day of trouble I call you,
because you answer.

No god is like you, Lord,
and nothing compares to what you do.

Every nation you made will come
and kneel in front of you, Lord,
and they will honor your name.

You are great, and your deeds are amazing.
You alone are God.

Teach me your way, Yahweh,
so I can live by your truth.
Give me one heart that fears your name.

With all my heart I will thank you, Lord my God,
and I will honor your name forever.

So great is your faithful love for me!
You pulled me out from the deepest part of the grave.{b}

God, arrogant men have attacked me.
A gang of ruthless men is after my life,
and they give you no thought.

But you, Lord, are a God of tenderness and kindness.
You are slow to anger and overflowing with faithful love and truth.{c}

Turn toward me and show me pity.
Strengthen your servant,
and rescue the son of your maidservant.

Show me a sign of your favor,
so my haters see it and are ashamed,
because you, Yahweh, have helped and comforted me.

notes.text: Hebrew chasid, someone devoted to faithful love.
Hebrew Sheol, the place of the dead.
Compare Exodus 34:6.

chapters.title: A prayer of David.

subheads.1: I Am Poor and Need You
subheads.6: There Is No God Like You

verses.text: He built his city on the holy mountains.{a}

Yahweh loves the gates of Zion
more than any other home in Jacob.

Glorious things are told about you,
city of God.
Selah

“I will list Rahab{b} and Babylon
among those who know me.
Look, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush.
Someone says, ‘This one was born there.’”

Of Zion it will be said,
“This one and that one were born in her.”
The Most High himself will keep her safe.

Yahweh will count the peoples in his register:
“This one was born there.”
Selah

Both singers and dancers will sing,
“All my springs are in you.”

notes.text: The Hebrew of this short psalm is tightly packed and hard to read in places.
Rahab is a poetic name for Egypt. Compare 89:10 and Isaiah 30:7.

chapters.title: By the sons of Korah. A psalm. A song.

verses.text:
Yahweh, God who saves me,
I cry out to you by day, and in the night I am before you.

Let my prayer reach you.
Bend your ear to my cry.

My soul is stuffed with troubles,
and my life has come close to the grave.{c}

People count me among those who go down to the pit.
I am like a man whose strength is gone,

dropped among the dead,
like bodies lying in a grave,
whom you do not remember anymore,
because they are cut off from your care.

You have put me at the bottom of the pit,
in dark places, in the deep.

Your anger weighs down on me,
and you flatten me with all your waves.
Selah

My friends are gone, and you took them.
You made me disgusting to them.
I am locked in and cannot get out.

My eyes are worn out from pain.
Every day I call to you, Yahweh.
I hold my hands out to you.

Do you work wonders for the dead?
Do the ghosts{d} stand up and praise you?
Selah

Is your faithful love spoken of in the grave,
or your trustworthiness in Abaddon?{e}

Are your wonders known in the dark,
or your goodness in the land of forgetting?

But I am calling you, Yahweh, for help.
At dawn my prayer rises to you.

Yahweh, why do you turn me away?
Why do you hide your face from me?

Suffering and nearness to death have followed me since boyhood.
I bear your terrors, and I cannot go on.{f}

Your burning anger has swept over me.
Your terrors have wiped me out.

All day long they surround me like water.
They close in on me together.

Loved ones and friends are gone, and you took them.
The only close friend I have is the dark.{g}

notes.text: The meaning of this tune name is uncertain. It may mean “on sickness, for suffering.”
Compare 1 Kings 4:31, 1 Chronicles 2:6, and 1 Chronicles 15:19. This is the saddest of the cries to God, and it ends without a word of hope.
Hebrew Sheol, the place of the dead.
Hebrew rephaim, the dead in the world below.
Abaddon means “destruction.” It is a name for the place of the dead.
The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
Or “my companions are in the dark.”

chapters.title: A song. A psalm by the sons of Korah. For the music director, to the tune “Mahalath Leannoth.”{a} A maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.{b}

subheads.1: Yahweh, I Cry Day and Night
subheads.13: Why Do You Hide From Me?

verses.text:
Yahweh’s faithful love is my song forever.
My mouth will tell every generation how true you are.

I said, “Faithful love is built to last forever.
You set your trustworthiness firm in the heavens.”

“I made an agreement with the one I chose.
To my servant David I swore:

‘I will keep your family line safe forever
and build your throne for all generations.’”
Selah

The heavens praise your wonders, Yahweh,
and so does the gathering of the holy ones praise how true you are.

Who in the sky is equal to Yahweh?
Who among the heavenly beings{b} is like him?

In the circle of the holy ones, God is held in dread.
He is more awesome than all who stand around him.

You rule the raging sea.
When its waves rise up, you calm them.

You crushed Rahab{d} like a dead body.
Your powerful arm scattered your enemies.

The sky is yours, and so is the earth.
The world and all it holds were set up by you.

North and south you created.
Mount Tabor and Mount Hermon shout joyfully at the mention of your name.

Your arm is full of power.
Your hand is strong, and your right hand is raised high.

Justice and fairness hold up your throne.
Faithful love and truth walk in front of you.

Happy are the people who know how to shout your praise.
Yahweh, they live in the light of your face.

All day long they celebrate your name,
and your goodness lifts them up.

You are their glorious strength,
and by your favor our horn{e} is raised high.

Our shield is Yahweh’s,
and our king is the Holy One of Israel’s.

Long ago you spoke in a vision to your loyal people{f} and said,
“I have helped a warrior.
I have honored one chosen from the common people.

I have found David, my servant.
I have anointed him with my holy oil.

My hand will hold him steady,
and my arm will make him strong.

No enemy will trick him.
No evil man will bring him low.

I will beat down his foes before his eyes
and strike those who hate him.

My truth and my faithful love will be with him,
and through my name his horn will be raised high.

His left hand I will put on the sea,
his right on the rivers.

He will cry out to me, ‘Father!
You are my God, the rock who saves me.’

I will make him my oldest son,
the highest of the kings on earth.

My faithful love for him will never end,
and my agreement with him will never fail.

I will make his family line last for all time,
and his throne as long as the heavens last.

If his children leave my teaching
and do not live by my rules,

if they treat my laws as common
and do not obey my commands,

I will beat their sin out with a stick
and their guilt with whippings,

but my faithful love for him will never be taken away,{g}
and I will not be false to my word.

I will not break my agreement
or change what my lips have said.

I have made one promise by my holiness, once and for all:
I will never lie to David.

His family line will last forever,
and his throne will last like the sun in front of me.

It will stand firm forever like the moon,
the sky’s faithful witness.”
Selah
