But now you have thrown him away and turned from him.
You are full of anger against your chosen king.

You have canceled the agreement with your servant.
You have dragged his crown in the dirt.

You have broken down all his walls.
You have turned his forts to rubble.

Everyone who goes by robs him.
His neighbors laugh at him.

You raised the right hand of his foes.
You made all his enemies happy.

You even dulled the edge of his sword
and did not stand by him in battle.

You ended his glory
and threw his throne down to the ground.

You shortened his young years.
You covered him with shame.
Selah

How long, Yahweh? Will you hide for good?
Will your fury go on blazing?

Remember how short my life is.
For what a waste you made all people!

Lord, where is your old faithful love,
which you promised to David in your truth?

Remember, Lord, how your servants are insulted,
how I carry in my heart the insults of all these peoples,

with which your enemies mock you, Yahweh,
and mock every step of your chosen king.

Blessed be Yahweh forever!
Amen and Amen.{i}

notes.text: Compare 1 Kings 4:31. This psalm celebrates God’s agreement with David (2 Samuel 7:8–16), then cries out because it seems to have fallen apart.
Or “the sons of the gods,” Hebrew bene ‘elim.
Yah is the short form of the name Yahweh.
Rahab is a name for the sea monster of chaos. It is also used for Egypt. Compare 87:4 and Job 26:12.
A horn pictures strength.
Many Hebrew copies say “your loyal one.”
Some copies and ancient versions read “I will not remove.”
Hebrew Sheol, the place of the dead.
This blessing closes Book Three of the Psalms. Compare 41:13, 72:18–19, and 106:48.

chapters.title: A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.{a}

subheads.1: I Will Sing of Yahweh’s Faithful Love
subheads.38: But Now You Have Rejected Him

verses.text:
Lord, you have been our home{b}
through every generation.

Before mountains were formed,
before earth and world were birthed by you,
from forever to forever, you are God.

You turn people back to dust.{c}
You say, “Go back, children of Adam.”

You carry them off like a dream.
They are like new grass of the morning.

In the morning it blooms and grows.
By evening it is dried up and withered.

Your anger wears us out,
and your fury frightens us.

You put our sins out in front of you,
and our secret sins in the glow of your face.

All our days fade under your anger.
We end our years like a groan.

Seventy years are all we get,
or eighty if we are strong.{e}
Still, most of that time{f} is hard work and pain.
It passes quickly, and we fly away.

Who understands how strong your anger is,
or your rage, as great as the fear you deserve?

Teach us to count how many days we have,
so we may gain a wise heart.

Come back, Yahweh! How long will this go on?
Take pity on your servants.

Fill us each morning with your faithful love,
so we can sing and be glad all our days.

Make us as glad as the days you made us suffer,
and as many years as we have seen trouble.

Let your servants watch what you do,
and let their children see your glory.

May the kindness{g} of the Lord our God rest on us.
Make the work of our hands last.
Yes, let what our hands do endure.

notes.text: Book Four of the Psalms begins here and ends with the blessing at 106:48. This is the only psalm credited to Moses. Compare Deuteronomy 33:1.
Or “shelter.”
Hebrew “to crushed powder.” Compare Genesis 3:19.
Compare 2 Peter 3:8. A night watch was about four hours.
Hebrew “seventy years... eighty years.”
Or “their pride.”
Or “beauty.”

chapters.heading: Book Four (Psalms 90–106)
chapters.title: A prayer of Moses, the man of God.{a}

subheads.7: Teach Us to Count Our Days

verses.text:
Whoever lives in the Most High’s secret place
will rest in the shadow of Shaddai.{a}

I will tell Yahweh, “You are my shelter and my fortress,
my God, the one I trust.”

He will pull you free from the hunter’s net
and from the deadly sickness.

He will cover you with his feathers,
and under his wings you will find shelter.
His truth is your shield and your wall.

Do not fear the horrors of night,
or the arrow that flies at midday,

or the disease that creeps in the dark,
or the sickness that strikes at noon.

A thousand may drop beside you,
ten thousand at your right side,
but it will not come near you.

You will only watch with your own eyes
and see the wicked get what they earn.

You have made Yahweh your shelter,{b}
the Most High your home.

So no harm will find you,
and no disease will come near your tent.

He will command his angels about you,
to guard you in all you do.

They will hold you up with their hands,
so that you never hit your foot on a stone.{c}

You will step on lions and cobras.
Young lions and snakes you will trample.

“Because he holds on to me in love, I will rescue him.
I will lift him up high, because he knows my name.

He will call on me, and I will answer him.
I will be at his side in trouble.
I will free him and give him honor.

I will give him a long life,
and show him my rescue.”

notes.text: Hebrew Shaddai, often translated “the Almighty.” This psalm has no title. The Septuagint credits it to David.
Hebrew “You, Yahweh, are my shelter.” The second line says the Most High is the home.
Matthew 4:6 and Luke 4:10–11 quote verses 11–12.

verses.text:
It is good to thank Yahweh
and to sing to your name, Most High,

to tell of your faithful love in the morning
and your truth at night,

with the ten-string harp
and the soft sound of the lyre.

Yahweh, what you have done fills me with joy.
I sing for joy over the work of your hands.

How great your works are, Yahweh!
How deep your thoughts are!

A senseless person does not know this,
and a fool cannot understand it:

though the wicked sprout like grass
and every evildoer blooms,
they are headed for lasting ruin.
But you, Yahweh, are high above for all time.

Look, your enemies, Yahweh.
Look, your enemies will perish.
All evildoers will be scattered.

But you have lifted up my horn like the horn of a wild ox.
You have poured fresh oil over me.{a}

I have seen my enemies fall.
I have heard the sad end of the evildoers who attacked me.

Good people will flourish like a palm tree
and grow tall like a cedar of Lebanon.

Those planted in Yahweh’s house
will thrive in our God’s courtyards.

They still bear fruit when they are old.
They stay fresh and green,

showing that Yahweh is honest.
He is my rock, and in him there is no wrong.{b}

notes.text: The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
Some Hebrew copies spell this word differently.

chapters.title: A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.

subheads.10: The Good Grow Like Palm Trees

verses.text:
Yahweh is King.{a} He wears majesty like a robe.
Yahweh has put on strength like a belt.
Yes, the world is set firm and cannot be shaken.

Your throne has stood firm since long ago.
You have always been.

The floods have risen, Yahweh.
The floods have raised their voices.
The floods lift up their crashing.

Yahweh on high is mightier
than the thunder of great waters,
mightier than the surf of the sea.

Your laws stand completely firm.
Holiness suits your house,
Yahweh, for all time.

notes.text: Or “Yahweh has become King.” Psalms 93 and 95–99 celebrate Yahweh as King.

verses.text:
God of payback, Yahweh,
God of payback, shine out!

Stand up, judge of the earth.
Pay back the proud for what they have done.

How long, Yahweh, will the wicked
be allowed to cheer?

They spill out proud words.
All the evildoers brag.

They crush your people, Yahweh,
and make life hard for those who belong to you.

They murder widows and foreigners,
and they kill orphans.

They say, “Yah does not see.
Jacob’s God does not notice.”

Notice this, you senseless people.
You fools, when will you get wise?

Did the one who made ears not listen?
Did the one who shaped eyes not look?

Will the one who disciplines nations not hold them to account?
Will the one who teaches people not know?

Yahweh knows human thoughts
are only a puff of air.{a}

Happy is the person you correct, Yah,
the one you teach from your law,

giving him peace in evil days,
while a pit is dug for the wicked.

Yahweh will not throw out his people.
He will not walk away from his own.

Justice will come back to what is right,
and all who are honest in heart will follow it.

Who will rise up for me against evildoers?
Who will be on my side against those who do wrong?

If Yahweh had not helped me,
I would soon have been lying in the silent grave.

When I said, “My foot is slipping,”
your faithful love, Yahweh, held me up.

When worries pile up inside me,
your comfort cheers my soul.

Can a corrupt ruler join you,
one who makes trouble by law?

They gang up against the life of the good,
and declare the innocent guilty.

But Yahweh has become my high fortress,
and my God is the rock I run to.

He will turn their own wrong back on them
and destroy them for their evil.
Yahweh our God will destroy them.

notes.text: 1 Corinthians 3:20 quotes this verse.

subheads.8: Can the One Who Made the Ear Not Hear?
subheads.12: Happy Is the One You Teach

verses.text:
Come, let us sing with gladness to Yahweh.
Let us cheer for the rock who rescues us.

Let us walk into his presence giving thanks.
Let us raise songs of praise to him.

Yahweh is a great God,
and a great King above all gods.

The earth’s deepest places are in his hand,
and the highest hills are his.

The sea belongs to him, since he created it,
and his own hands shaped the dry land.

Come, let us bow low and worship.
Let us kneel before Yahweh, our maker.

He is our God,
and we belong to him, the sheep he feeds,
the flock in his care.
Today, if you hear his voice,

do not make your hearts hard, as they did at Meribah,{a}
or on the day at Massah{b} in the desert,

when your ancestors put me to the test
and tried me, though they had watched me work.

For forty years that generation made me sick.
I said, “Their hearts keep wandering,
and they have never learned my ways.”

So in my anger I swore,
“They will never enter my rest.”

notes.text: Meribah means “quarreling.”
Massah means “testing.” Compare Exodus 17:1–7 and Numbers 20:1–13. Hebrews 3:7–11 and 4:3–7 quote verses 7–11.

verses.text:
Sing a new song to Yahweh.{a}
Sing to Yahweh, everyone on earth.

Sing to Yahweh and bless his name.
Announce his rescue every day.

Tell about his glory among the nations,
and his wonders among all peoples.

Yahweh is great and deserves endless praise.
He is more to be feared than all gods.

The gods of the nations are all worthless idols,{b}
but Yahweh made the heavens.

Splendor and majesty are before him.
Strength and beauty fill his holy place.

Give to Yahweh, you families of the nations,
give to Yahweh glory and strength.

Give Yahweh the glory that his name deserves.
Bring an offering and enter his courtyards.

Bow to Yahweh as he shines in holiness.{c}
Tremble in front of him, all the earth.

Tell the nations, “Yahweh is King.
The world is set firm and cannot be shaken.
He will judge the peoples fairly.”

Let the skies be glad and the earth celebrate.
Let the ocean roar, with all that fills it.

Let the fields be happy, with all that is in them.
Then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy

before Yahweh, because he is on his way,
on his way to judge the earth.
He will judge the world with justice
and the peoples with truth.

notes.text: Most of this psalm is also in 1 Chronicles 16:23–33.
Hebrew ‘elilim, “nothings,” a play on the word ‘elohim, “gods.”
Or “in holy clothing.”

verses.text:
Yahweh is King! Let the earth celebrate.
Let the many islands be glad.

Clouds and deep darkness surround him.
Justice and fairness hold up his throne.

A fire marches ahead of him
and burns up his enemies on every side.

Flashes of his lightning light up the world.
The earth watches and shakes.

Mountains melt like wax in front of Yahweh,
in front of the Lord of all the earth.

The heavens announce that he is good,
and all the peoples see his glory.

Zion heard it and was glad.
The towns of Judah celebrate
because of your decisions, Yahweh.

You, Yahweh, are over all the earth, the Most High.
You are lifted far above all gods.

You who love Yahweh, hate evil.
He keeps safe the lives of those loyal to him
and saves them from the wicked.

Light has been planted{b} for those who do right,
and joy for those with honest hearts.

Celebrate in Yahweh, you who do right,
and give thanks to his holy name.{c}

notes.text: The Septuagint says “all his angels.” Compare Hebrews 1:6.
The Hebrew says “planted.” One Hebrew copy and the ancient versions say “Light rises.”
Hebrew “to the memory of his holiness.”

verses.text:
Sing Yahweh a new song,
because he has done wonders.
His strong right hand and holy arm
have won him the victory.

Yahweh has shown how he saves.
In front of the nations he has uncovered his justice.

He remembered his faithful love and truth
to the people of Israel.
The farthest corners of the earth have seen
how our God saves.

Shout out to Yahweh, all the earth.
Burst into joyful song and make music.

Make music to Yahweh on the lyre,
on the lyre, with a sweet melody.

With trumpets and the blast of the ram’s horn,
shout in front of the King, Yahweh.

Let the sea roar with everything in it,
the world, and all who make their home there.

Let the rivers clap their hands.
Let the mountains sing for joy together

in front of Yahweh, because he is coming to judge the earth.
He will judge the world with justice
and the peoples with fairness.

chapters.title: A psalm.

verses.text:
Yahweh is King. Let the nations tremble.
He sits above the winged guardians. Let the earth shake.

Yahweh is great in Zion.
He is high above all peoples.

Let them praise your great and awesome name.
He is holy!{a}

Lift up Yahweh our God
and bow at his footstool.
He is holy!

Moses and Aaron served as his priests,
and Samuel was one of those who called on his name.
When they called Yahweh, he replied.

He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud.
They kept his laws and the rule he gave them.

Yahweh our God, you answered them.
You were a God who forgave them,
but who also punished their wrongs.

Lift up Yahweh our God
and bow at his holy mountain,
because Yahweh our God is holy.

notes.text: The words “He is holy” come again in verses 5 and 9.
The Hebrew of this line is hard to read.

verses.text: Shout to Yahweh, everyone on earth.

Serve Yahweh with joy.
Come into his presence singing.

Go into his gates with thanks,
and into his courtyards with praise.
Thank him and bless his name.

Yahweh is good.
His faithful love lasts forever,
and his truth lasts through every generation.

notes.text: Or “for the thank offering.”
Some Hebrew copies say “and we are his.” The common Hebrew text says “and not we ourselves.”

chapters.title: A psalm for giving thanks.{a}

verses.text:
Faithful love and justice are what I will sing about.
I will make music to you, Yahweh.

I will think carefully about how to live a blameless life.
When will you come to me?
In my own home I will live
with an honest heart.

I will not set anything worthless
in front of my eyes.
I hate what people do when they stray.
They will not stick to me.

A twisted heart will stay far from me.
I will have nothing to do with evil.

Whoever puts down a neighbor in secret,
I will silence.{a}
Whoever has proud eyes and a puffed-up heart,
I will not put up with.

My eyes will look for the faithful in the land,
so they can live near me.
The one who walks a blameless path
will serve me.

No one who practices cheating
will live in my house.
No one who tells lies
will stand in front of me.

Every morning I will silence
the wicked in this land,
pulling up all evildoers
from the city of Yahweh.

notes.text: Some Hebrew copies spell this verb differently.

chapters.title: By David. A psalm.

verses.text:
Hear what I am praying, Yahweh.
Let my cry for help reach your ears.

Do not hide your face from me
on my day of trouble.
Lean down and listen.
When I call, answer me quickly.

My days drift off like smoke,
and my bones glow as hot as a furnace.

My heart is crushed and dried up like grass.
I even forget to eat.

From so much groaning,
my skin clings to my bones.

I am like an owl of the desert.{a}
I am like a little owl among the ruins.

I lie awake at night.
I am like a sparrow by itself on a rooftop.

All day my enemies insult me.
Those who are furious with me use my name in their curses.

I eat ashes like bread
and mix my drink with tears,

It is because of your anger and fury.
You lifted me up, and then you flung me away.

My days are like a long evening shadow.
I wither like grass.

But you, Yahweh, sit on your throne forever.
Your fame lasts through every generation.

You will rise up and take pity on Zion,
because it is time to be kind to her.
The set time has come.

Your servants love her stones
and feel sorry for her dust.

The nations will fear the name of Yahweh,
and all the kings of the earth will fear your glory.

Yahweh will rebuild Zion,
and his glory will be seen there.

He will pay attention to the prayer of the helpless
and will not look down on their plea.

Let this be written for a later generation,
so a people not yet born may praise Yah:

that from his holy height he looked down.
Yahweh looked from heaven to the earth,

to hear the groans of prisoners
and set free those sentenced to die,

so that people will announce Yahweh’s name in Zion
and his praise in Jerusalem,

once peoples have come together,
and kingdoms, to serve Yahweh.

He has broken my strength along the road.{b}
He has cut my days short.

I say, “My God, do not take me away
while my life is half done.
You live on through every generation.

In the beginning you laid the earth’s foundation,
and the heavens are made by your hands.{c}

They will wear away, but you will still be here.
They will all go threadbare like a coat.
You will swap them like clothes,
and they will be gone.

But you stay the same,
and your years will never end.

The children of your servants will live safely,
and their descendants will stand firm in front of you.”

notes.text: It is not certain which birds these are.
Some Hebrew copies say “my strength.” Others say “his strength.”
Hebrews 1:10–12 quotes verses 25–27.

chapters.title: A prayer of someone in trouble, when he is weak and pours out his complaint to Yahweh.

subheads.18: Write It for the Next Generation

verses.text:
Bless Yahweh, my soul.
Let all that is in me bless his holy name.

Bless Yahweh, my soul,
and remember all his gifts.

He forgives all your sins.
He heals all your diseases.

He buys your life back from the pit.
He puts on you a crown of faithful love and tenderness.

He fills your years{a} with good things,
so you become young again like an eagle.

Yahweh does what is right
and gives justice to all who are crushed.

He let Moses know his ways
and the people of Israel see his deeds.

Yahweh is tender and kind,
slow to anger and rich in faithful love.{b}

He will not accuse us forever,
and he will not stay angry for all time.

Our sins deserved more than he gave us,
and he did not repay us for our wrongs.

As high as the sky stands over the earth,
that is how great his faithful love is for those who fear him.

As far as sunrise is from sunset,
so far has he put our sins away from us.

As a father has pity on his children,
so Yahweh has pity on those who fear him.

He knows how we are made.
He remembers that we are dust.

A human life is like grass.
It blooms like a wildflower,

and then the wind blows over it, and it is gone.
Its place does not know it anymore.

for those who stay true to his agreement
and remember to obey his orders.

Yahweh has placed his throne in heaven,
and his kingdom rules over everything.

Bless Yahweh, you angels,
you mighty ones who do what he says,
who listen for the sound of his word.

Bless Yahweh, all his armies,
his servants who do what he wants.

Bless Yahweh, everything he has made,
in every place he rules.
Bless Yahweh, my soul.

notes.text: The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain. It is traditionally read “your mouth.”
Compare Exodus 34:6.

chapters.title: By David.

verses.text:
Bless Yahweh, my soul.
Yahweh my God, you are so great.
You are dressed in splendor and majesty.

You put on light like a robe.
You unroll the heavens like a tent cloth.

He builds his upstairs rooms on the waters.
He uses the clouds for a chariot.
He travels on the wind’s wings.

He makes the winds his messengers
and flames of fire his servants.{a}

The earth sits on foundations he laid,
so that it can never be shaken.

You covered it with the deep like a coat.
The waters stood above the mountains.

At your shout they ran away.
At the crash of your thunder they hurried off.

The mountains rose and the valleys sank{b}
to the place you had set for them.

You set a limit they cannot cross,
so they never again flood the earth.

He makes springs pour into the valleys,
and they run between the hills.

All the wild animals drink from them,
and the wild donkeys quench their thirst.

Birds nest beside them.
They sing among the branches.

From your upper rooms you water the mountains.
The earth is satisfied with what you have made.

You make grass grow for the cattle
and crops for people to farm,
so they can bring food out of the earth,

and wine to cheer the human heart,
oil to make faces shine,
and bread to give strength to the heart.

The trees of Yahweh drink all they want,
the cedars of Lebanon that he planted.

There the birds build their nests.
The stork makes her home in the juniper trees.

High mountains are home to wild goats.
The rocks are a hiding place for the rock badgers.{c}

He made the moon to mark the seasons.{d}
The sun knows when to set.

You bring darkness, and night falls,
when all the beasts of the forest creep out.

Young lions roar for their prey
and ask God for their food.

The sun rises, and they slink away
to lie down in their dens.

At that, people go off to their work
and stay at it until evening.

How many things you have made, Yahweh!
You made all of them with wisdom.
Your creatures fill the earth.

There is the sea, so big and wide,
filled with countless creatures,
living things both small and large.

Ships sail back and forth there,
and so does Leviathan, whom you made to play in it.{e}

Every one of them waits for you
to give them food at the right time.

You hand it out, and they pick it up.
You open your hand, and they are full of good things.

When you hide your face, they are terrified.
When you take away their breath, they die
and return to dust.

When you send out your Spirit,{f} they are created,
and you make the face of the ground new.

May Yahweh’s glory last forever.
May Yahweh enjoy all that he has made.

Yahweh looks at the earth, and it trembles.
He touches the mountains, and they smoke.

As long as I live, I will sing to Yahweh.
I will sing praise to my God while I have life.

May my thoughts please him.
I find my joy in Yahweh.

May sinners vanish from the earth,
and may the wicked be no more.
Bless Yahweh, my soul.
Hallelujah!{g}

notes.text: Or “he makes his angels winds.” Hebrews 1:7 quotes this.
Or “They went up the mountains and down into the valleys.”
Hebrew shephanim, a small rock-dwelling animal called a hyrax.
Or “the set festivals.”
Or “to play with.” Compare Job 41:5.
Or “your breath.”
Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” Yah is a short form of the name Yahweh. This is the first time the word appears in the Bible. It comes again many times in the Psalms.

verses.text:
Give thanks to Yahweh and call on his name.{a}
Let every nation hear about his deeds.

Sing to him and play music for him.
Speak of every wonder he has done.

Be proud of his holy name.
Let everyone who looks for Yahweh be glad.

Look to Yahweh and to his strength.
Seek his face all the time.

Remember the wonders he did,
his signs and the rulings he gave,

you children of Abraham, his servant,
you sons of Jacob, the people he picked.

He is Yahweh, our God.
His rulings reach the whole earth.

He never forgets his agreement.
He gave his word for a thousand generations.

It is the agreement he made with Abraham,
the promise he swore to Isaac.

He set it up for Jacob as a law,
for Israel as an agreement without end.

“To you,” he said, “I give Canaan,
and it will be your own share of land.”

They numbered only a few then,
just a small group living there as outsiders.

They roamed from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to the next.

Yahweh let nobody hurt them.
For their sake he warned kings,

“Do not touch the ones I have anointed.
Do not harm my prophets.”

He called a hunger down on the land
and cut off the whole supply of bread.{b}

Before them he sent a man,
Joseph, who was sold to be a slave.

They locked his feet in chains.
An iron ring was put on his neck.{c}

This went on until what he had said came true.
Yahweh’s word proved him right.

The king commanded that he be freed.
The ruler of nations let him out.

He put Joseph in charge of his palace
and over everything the king owned.

He could instruct the king’s leaders
and teach the older men to be wise.

Then Israel moved to Egypt.
Jacob camped as a foreigner in the land of Ham.{d}

God let his people have many children
and made them mightier than the people around them.

He let the Egyptians turn to hate his people
and make sly plans against his servants.

He sent Moses, his servant,
and Aaron, the man he had picked.

They did his signs among the Egyptians,
and amazing things in the land of Ham.{e}

He sent darkness, and the land went black.
Yet they kept fighting his words.{f}

He turned their water into blood,
and all their fish died.

Frogs crawled all over their land,
even into the king’s bedrooms.

He spoke, and clouds of flies came,
and biting gnats filled their country.

For rain he gave them hail,
and fire flashed across their country.

He smashed their grapevines and fig trees
and broke the trees in their country.

He spoke, and the locusts came,
young locusts too many to count.

They ate every plant in the land
and every crop that grew from the soil.

Then he struck down every oldest son in the land,
the first of all their strength.

He led Israel out with silver and gold,
and not one of his tribes fell behind.

Egypt was glad to see them go,
for the fear of Israel had come over them.

He spread a cloud above them like a roof
and sent a fire to light the dark.

When they begged, he brought them quail,
and gave them their fill of bread from heaven.

He split a rock, and water poured out.
It ran through the desert like a river.

He kept in mind the holy promise
he gave to his servant Abraham.

Then his people left with joy,
his chosen ones singing glad songs.

He handed over the lands of other nations to them,
and they took the riches others had worked for,

notes.text: This psalm’s verses 1–15 are also found in 1 Chronicles 16:8–22.
The Hebrew says “he broke every staff of bread,” meaning the food supply.
Hebrew nephesh, which can mean “soul” or “throat.” The Hebrew also says “his neck came into iron.”
Ham is a poetic name for Egypt. See Genesis 10:6.
Hebrew “They set among them the words of his signs.”
Some ancient copies leave out “not” and read, “they did not fight his words.” The Hebrew text is hard to read here.
Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” See the note on 104:35.

verses.text:
Who can list all that Yahweh has done,
or tell all the praise he deserves?

Happy are people who treat others fairly,
who do right every day.

Remember me, Yahweh, when you are kind to your people.
Come and save me,

Then I can see good things come to those you chose,
share the joy of your nation,
and brag along with the people who are yours.

We have sinned just as our parents did.
We have done wrong and acted wickedly.

In Egypt our parents
did not understand your wonders.
They forgot your many acts of faithful love
and turned against you at the sea, the Red Sea.{b}

Still, he saved them for his own name’s sake,
to show how powerful he is.

He ordered the Red Sea, and it dried up.
He led them through the deep as if on open ground.

He saved them from people who hated them
and took them out of their enemy’s hands.

The water closed over their enemies,
and none of them survived.

For a moment they trusted his words,
and they sang to praise him.

But soon they forgot what he had done.
They would not wait to hear his plan.

In the desert they let their hunger take over,
and they tested God in the wasteland.

He gave them just what they begged for,
but sent a sickness that made them waste away.

In the camp they became jealous of Moses
and of Aaron, whom Yahweh had set apart.

The ground opened and swallowed Dathan.
It closed over the followers of Abiram.

A fire broke out in their group.
Flames burned up those wicked men.

At Horeb they made a calf
and bowed down to a metal statue.

They gave up their Glory{c}
for a statue of a bull that eats grass.

They put God out of their minds,
though he had saved them
and done great things in Egypt,

amazing things in the land of Ham,
and awesome things at the Red Sea.

He said he would wipe them out.
But Moses, the man he had picked,
stood in the gap in front of him
and kept his anger from destroying them.

Then they looked down on the beautiful land.
They did not trust what he had promised.

They grumbled in their tents
and would not listen to Yahweh.

So he raised his hand and made a vow
to let them fall in the desert,

to make their children fall among the nations
and to scatter them across the lands.

They tied themselves to Baal of Peor
and ate food offered to dead idols.{d}

What they did stirred up his anger,
and a plague broke out among them.

Then Phinehas stepped up and acted,
and the plague stopped.

God counted this as a right act for him,
and people will remember it forever.

At the waters of Meribah they made him angry,
and Moses suffered because of them,

for they filled his spirit with bitterness,
and he spoke without thinking.

They did not wipe out the other peoples
as Yahweh had told them to.

They mixed with the nations
and picked up their ways.

They served idols,
and those idols became a trap for them.

They gave their sons
and daughters to evil spirits.

Innocent blood ran from their hands,
the blood of their sons and daughters.
They offered them to the idols of Canaan,
and the blood made the land unclean.

They made themselves unclean by what they did,
and they were unfaithful to God by their actions.

So Yahweh’s anger blazed against his people,
and he turned away in disgust from the ones who were his own.

He put them in the power of other nations,
and those who hated them ruled over them.

Their enemies pushed them down,
and they were made small under their power.

Again and again he saved them,
but they kept choosing their own way
and sank lower because of their sin.

Still, he saw how bad things were for them
and heard their cry for help.

He thought of his agreement with them
and changed his mind because of his great faithful love.{e}

He made all the people who held them
feel sorry for them.

Save us, Yahweh our God!
Bring us home from the nations,
so we may thank your holy name
and take pride in praising you.

Bless Yahweh, the God of Israel,
from the beginning to the end of time!
Let all the people say, “Amen!”
Hallelujah!{f}

notes.text: Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” See the note on 104:35. Verses 1 and 47–48 are also found in 1 Chronicles 16:34–36.
Hebrew Yam Suph, “Sea of Reeds.” It is also used in verses 9 and 22.
That is, God. An old scribal tradition says the first wording was “my glory.”
Or “to lifeless gods.” See Numbers 25:1–9.
The Hebrew copies’ margin has the plural “his many acts of faithful love.” The main text has the singular.
This verse ends Book Four of the Psalms. See 41:13, 72:18–19 and 89:52. Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!”

subheads.6: We Have Sinned Like Our Parents

verses.text:
Thank Yahweh, because he is good.
His faithful love lasts forever.{a}

Let those he has bought back say so,
the ones he took from the hand of the enemy

Some wandered through the desert on a dry, empty land.
They found no road leading to a town to live in.

Hungry and thirsty,
they grew weaker and weaker.

Then they cried to Yahweh in their trouble,
and he pulled them out of their distress.

He guided them along a straight path
to a town where they could settle.

Let them thank Yahweh for his faithful love{c}
and for the wonders he does for people.

He gives water to the thirsty
and fills the hungry with good food.

Some sat in deep darkness,
locked in iron chains.{d}

They had fought against what God said
and looked down on the advice of the Most High.

So he bent them low with heavy labor.
They stumbled, and there was no one to help.

Then they called to Yahweh in their trouble,
and he saved them from their misery.

He led them out of the darkness
and snapped their chains apart.

Let them thank Yahweh for his faithful love
and for the wonders he does for people.

He smashes doors of bronze
and cuts through iron bars.

Some were fools. They got sick from their sinful ways
and suffered because of their wrongs.

They could not stand the sight of food,
and they came close to the gates of death.

Then they cried to Yahweh in their trouble,
and he saved them from their misery.

At his command they were healed.
He rescued them from the grave.

Let them thank Yahweh for his faithful love
and for the wonders he does for people.

Let them bring thank offerings
and tell of his work with songs of joy.

Some took ships out to sea
and made their living on the great waters.

They saw what Yahweh can do,
his wonders in the deep.

He spoke, and a storm wind blew
and piled up the waves.

The ships went up to the sky and down to the deep.
The sailors lost their nerve in the danger.

They stumbled around like drunk men,
and they did not know what to do.

Then they called to Yahweh in their trouble,
and he led them out of their misery.

He calmed the storm to a whisper,
and the waves{e} grew still.

They were glad when it got quiet,
and he steered them to the port they wanted.

Let them thank Yahweh for his faithful love
and for the wonders he does for people.

Let them lift him high in the people’s meeting
and praise him where the leaders gather.

He changes rivers into desert
and flowing springs into dry ground.

He turns rich land into salty waste
because of the evil of the people who live there.

He turns a desert into ponds of water
and dry ground into springs.

He lets hungry people settle there,
and they build a town to live in.

They plant fields and vineyards
and gather a good harvest.

He blesses them, and they grow in number.
He does not let their herds shrink.

Then they get fewer and are pushed down
by cruelty, trouble and sadness.

He pours shame on their rulers
and makes them wander in a trackless desert.{f}

But he lifts the poor out of suffering
and makes their families grow like flocks.

Honest people see it and are glad,
and everyone who does wrong is silenced.

Whoever is wise should think about these things
and consider the faithful love of Yahweh.

notes.text: Book Five of the Psalms begins here and ends with Psalm 150. It includes the Songs of Ascents (120–134) and the Hallel psalms (113–118 and 146–150).
The Hebrew says “from the sea.” This likely means the south.
This chorus returns in verses 15, 21 and 31.
Or “in the shadow of death.” The same words are in verse 14.
Hebrew “their waves.”
Compare Job 12:21, 24.

verses.text:
My heart is steady, God.
I will sing and make music with all that I am.{b}

Wake up, harp and lyre!
I will wake the morning sun.

Among the nations, Yahweh, I will thank you.
Among the peoples I will sing to you.

Your faithful love is higher than the skies,
and your truth touches the clouds.

Be lifted above the heavens, God.
Let your glory fill the whole earth.

Use your right hand to save us and answer me,
so those you love will be rescued.

Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine.
Ephraim is my helmet.
Judah is my king’s staff.

Moab is my washing bowl.
I throw my sandal on Edom.
I shout in victory over Philistia.”

Who will bring me into the fortified city?
Who will lead me all the way to Edom?

God, have you pushed us away?
You no longer march out with our armies.

Help us fight our enemy,
because help from people is no good.

With God we will win,
and he will walk over our enemies.

notes.text: This psalm joins 57:7–11 (verses 1–5) and 60:5–12 (verses 6–13), with a few small changes.
Hebrew “even my glory.”
Or “in his temple.”

chapters.title: A song. A psalm of David.{a}

verses.text: God, you are the one I praise. Do not stay quiet.

Wicked, lying people
have spoken up against me.
Their tongues are full of lies about me.

Hateful words are all around me,
and they attack me without cause.

I love them, but they accuse me.
So I keep on praying.{a}

They pay me back with bad for good
and with hate for my love.

They say, “Put an evil man over him.
Let an accuser{b} stand at his right hand.

At his trial, may the verdict be guilty.
May even his prayer be held against him.

May his life be short.
May another man fill his post.{c}

May his children lose their father
and his wife be left a widow.

May his children beg as they roam,
driven from their wrecked homes in hunger.{d}

Let the man he owes take everything he has.
Let strangers carry off what he worked for.

Let no one show kindness to him.
Let no one feel sorry for his orphans.

Let his family line be cut off.
Let their names be erased in one more generation.

May Yahweh remember the wrongs of his father,
and never erase his mother’s sin.

Let Yahweh always keep them in view,
and let him wipe out any memory of them from the earth.

For he never once thought of being kind.
He hunted down the poor and the needy
and the brokenhearted, until they were dead.

He loved to curse, so let curses land on him.
He took no joy in blessing, so let blessing stay far away.

He wore cursing like a coat.
Let it soak into him like water
and into his bones like oil.

Let it wrap around him like a robe,
like the belt he wears every day.”

This is how Yahweh will pay my accusers,
those who say evil things about me.

But as for you, Yahweh my Lord,
do right by me for your name’s sake.
Your faithful love is good, so rescue me.

I am poor and in need,
and my heart is wounded inside me.

I am vanishing like the shade at dusk.
I am flicked away like a locust.

My knees wobble because I have gone without food.
My body has grown thin and bony.

People laugh at me.
When they see me, they shake their heads.

Help me, Yahweh my God!
Save me because of your faithful love.

May they know that your hand is behind this.
Yahweh, it is you who did it.

They may curse, but you will bless.
When they rise up, they will be shamed,
and your servant will rejoice.

Let those who accuse me be dressed in disgrace.
Let them wrap themselves in shame like a coat.

I will thank Yahweh loudly with my mouth.
Among the crowds I will sing his praise.

For he stands next to the poor
to save them from those who would judge them guilty.

notes.text: Hebrew “but I, prayer.”
Hebrew satan, “accuser” or “opponent.” Many readers take verses 6–19 as the words of the psalmist’s enemies against him, as if “they say” came before them.
Acts 1:20 quotes this verse.
The Hebrew has this reading. The Greek says, “let them be driven out of their ruins.”

chapters.title: For the music director. By David. A psalm.

verses.text:
From Zion Yahweh will reach out your mighty scepter.
“Rule among your enemies,” he says.

Your people will come freely
on the day you gather your army,
dressed in holy splendor.{b}
Like dew from the womb of the dawn,
your young men will come to you.

The Lord stands at your right hand.
When he is angry, kings will fall.

He will judge the nations
and pile up the dead.
He will crush the heads of rulers over wide lands.

He will drink from a brook by the road,
and then he will hold his head high.

notes.text: Hebrew neum YHWH ladoni. The first is Yahweh’s name. The second is adoni, “my lord,” a title of respect that is also used for kings.
Many Hebrew copies read this way. Others say “on the holy mountains.” This verse is hard to read in Hebrew.
Or “on account of Melchizedek.” See Genesis 14:18–20. Hebrews 5:6, 6:20 and 7:17, 21 quote this verse.

chapters.title: By David. A psalm.

subheads.5: The Lord Is at Your Right Side

verses.text:
Yahweh’s works are great.
All who enjoy them study them.

What he does is glorious and grand,
and his goodness never ends.

He has made sure his wonders are remembered.
Yahweh is kind and full of mercy.

He provides food for those who fear him.
He always remembers his agreement.

He showed his people the power of his deeds
by giving them the lands of other nations.

Everything his hands do is faithful and fair.
All his orders can be trusted.

They stand firm for ever and ever.
They are done with truth and with honesty.

He paid the price to free his people.
He set his agreement up to last forever.
His name is holy and awesome.

notes.text: Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” See the note on 104:35. After this opening, Psalms 111 and 112 are matching acrostic poems. Each line starts with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet.
See Proverbs 1:7 and 9:10.

verses.text:
His children will be strong on the earth.
Honest people’s families will be blessed.

His house is full of wealth and riches,
and his goodness stands forever.

Even in darkness a light shines for the honest.
They are kind, merciful and fair.

Good comes to those who give freely and lend,
and who run their business fairly.

Such a person will never be knocked down.
The good are remembered forever.

Bad news does not scare him.
His heart is firm because he trusts Yahweh.

His heart is steady, so he has no fear.
In the end he will look at his enemies and see them lose.

The wicked see this and are upset.
They grind their teeth and fade away.
What wicked people want comes to nothing.

notes.text: Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” This psalm is an acrostic like Psalm 111. It describes the good person with some of the same words used for God in Psalm 111.
2 Corinthians 9:9 quotes this.

subheads.1: Happy Are Those Who Respect Yahweh

verses.text:
May Yahweh’s name be blessed
now and forever.

From the place where the sun comes up to where it goes down,
praise Yahweh’s name.

Yahweh is above all the nations.
His glory is higher than the sky.

Who compares to Yahweh our God?
He sits on a throne up high,

yet he leans down to see
the sky and the earth.

He picks up the poor from the dirt
and lifts the needy from the trash heap.

He seats them with rulers,
with the rulers of his own people.

He gives the woman with no children a home
and makes her a happy mother.
Hallelujah!

notes.text: Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” See the note on 104:35. Psalms 113–118 are called the Egyptian Hallel and were sung at Passover.

verses.text:
When Israel left Egypt,
when Jacob’s family left a land with a strange language,

Judah became God’s holy place,
and Israel became the land he rules.

The sea saw it and fled.
The Jordan flowed backward.{a}

The mountains bounced like rams,
and the hills like lambs.

Sea, what made you flee?
Jordan, why did you flow backward?

Mountains, why did you leap like rams?
Hills, why like lambs?

Shake, earth, in front of the Lord,
in front of the God of Jacob,

who turns a rock into a pool of water
and hard stone into a spring.{b}

notes.text: See Exodus 14:21–22 and Joshua 3:14–17.
See Exodus 17:6 and Numbers 20:11.

verses.text:
Not for our sake, Yahweh, not for ours,
but for your name’s sake let there be glory,
because of your faithful love and your truth.

Why should other nations get to say,
“So where is their God?”

Our God is up in heaven.
Whatever pleases him, he does.

Their gods are crafted from silver and gold,
made by human hands.

Each has a mouth that does not speak,
and eyes that do not see.

Each has ears that do not hear,
and a nose that does not smell.

Their hands cannot feel,
their feet cannot walk,
and no sound comes from their throats.

The people who make them will become like them,
and so will everyone who trusts in them.{a}

Israel, trust in Yahweh!
He is their helper and their shield.

Family of Aaron, trust in Yahweh!
He is their helper and their shield.

All who respect Yahweh, trust in Yahweh!
He is their helper and their shield.

Yahweh remembers us, and he will bless us.
He will bless Israel’s family.
He will bless Aaron’s family.

He will bless all who respect Yahweh,
the young and the old.

May Yahweh make you grow in number,
you and your children.

May Yahweh bless you,
the one who made heaven and earth.

Heaven is Yahweh’s own,
but the earth he gave to people.

The dead cannot praise Yah,
and neither can anyone gone down to the silent place.

notes.text: Compare Psalm 135:15–18.
Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” See the note on 104:35.

verses.text:
I love Yahweh because he listens
to my voice and my cries for mercy.

He bent down to hear me,
so I will call on him as long as I live.

The ropes of death were tied around me.
The pain of the grave{a} came over me.
I met only trouble and sadness.

Then I called on Yahweh’s name:
“Yahweh, please save my life!”

Yahweh is kind and fair.
Our God is full of mercy.

Yahweh guards those who are simple.
I was weak, and he saved me.

Be at rest again, my soul,
for Yahweh has been very good to you.

You have kept me from dying,
dried my tears,
and stopped my feet from slipping.

I will walk with Yahweh
in the land of the living.

I kept believing, even when I said,{b}
“I am in terrible pain.”

In my panic I said,
“No one can be trusted.”

How can I repay Yahweh
for all he has given me?

I will raise the cup of rescue
and call on Yahweh’s name.

I will keep my promises to Yahweh
in front of all his people.

Yahweh values highly
the deaths of those who are loyal to him.

Yahweh, I am your servant.
I am your servant, born to your servant woman.
You have untied my chains.

I will bring you a thank offering
and call on Yahweh’s name.

I will keep my promises to Yahweh
in front of all his people,

in the yard of Yahweh’s house,
in the middle of Jerusalem.
Hallelujah!

notes.text: Hebrew Sheol, the place of the dead.
Or “I believed, so I said.” The Greek version reads, “I believed, so I spoke.”

verses.text:
Praise Yahweh, all you nations.
Give him honor, all you peoples.{a}

His faithful love for us is great,
and Yahweh’s truth lasts forever.
Hallelujah!

notes.text: Romans 15:11 quotes this verse. This is the shortest chapter in the Bible.

verses.text:
Thank Yahweh, because he is good.
His faithful love lasts forever.

Let Israel say,
“His faithful love lasts forever.”

Let the family of Aaron say,
“His faithful love lasts forever.”

Let those who respect Yahweh say,
“His faithful love lasts forever.”

In my trouble I called to Yah.
Yah answered and set me free in an open space.{a}

Yahweh stands with me. I have no fear.
How can mere humans harm me?{b}

Yahweh is with me as my helper.
I will look down on those who hate me.

It is better to run to Yahweh for safety
than to put trust in people.

It is better to run to Yahweh for safety
than to put trust in princes.

Every nation circled around me,
but in Yahweh’s name I cut them down.

They circled me, yes, they circled me,
but in Yahweh’s name I cut them down.

They swarmed like bees around me,
but they burned out like a fire in thorns.
In Yahweh’s name I cut them down.

They pushed hard at me so I would fall,{c}
but Yahweh came to help me.

Yah gives me strength, and he is my song.
He is the one who saves me.{d}

Shouts of joy and victory
ring out in the tents of good people.
“Yahweh’s right hand does mighty things.

Yahweh’s right hand is raised high.
Yahweh’s right hand does mighty things.”

I will not die. I will live,
and I will tell what Yah has done.

Yah punished me hard,
but he did not let me die.

Open the gates of goodness for me.
I will go in and thank Yah.

This is the gate of Yahweh.
Good people go in through it.

I thank you for answering me
and for becoming the one who saves me.

The stone the builders threw away
has become the main stone at the corner.{e}

Yahweh did this,
and it amazes us.

This is the day Yahweh made.
Let us celebrate and be glad in it.

Please, Yahweh, save us!{f}
Please, Yahweh, let us do well!

Blessed is the one who comes in Yahweh’s name.{g}
We bless you from Yahweh’s house.

Yahweh is God, and he has given us light.
Tie the festival sacrifice with ropes
up to the horns of the altar.

You are my God, and I give you thanks.
My God, I lift you high.

Thank Yahweh, because he is good.
His faithful love lasts forever.

notes.text: Or “he set me in a wide place.”
Hebrews 13:6 quotes this verse.
The Hebrew reads “You pushed me,” meaning the enemy. Some read “I was pushed.”
See Exodus 15:2 and Isaiah 12:2.
Jesus and the apostles quote this in Matthew 21:42, Acts 4:11 and 1 Peter 2:7.
Hebrew hoshiah na, which gives us the word “hosanna.”
The crowd shouted this to Jesus in Matthew 21:9.

verses.text:
Happy are those whose lives have no fault,{a}
who walk by Yahweh’s teaching.

Happy are those who hold on to his reminders
and look for him with all their hearts.

They do nothing wrong.
They stay on his paths.

You gave your orders
so that people would follow them closely.

I wish my life were steady
in doing what you say.

Then I would never be ashamed
when I look at all your commands.

With an honest heart I will praise you
as I learn your fair decisions.

I will do what you have said.
Please never leave me completely alone.

How can a young person keep life clean?
By living the way your word says.

With everything in me I have looked for you.
Keep me from straying off your commands.

I have stored your promise deep inside me,
to keep me from sinning against you.

You are blessed, Yahweh.
Teach me your rules.

I say out loud
every decision you have spoken.

I take as much joy in following your reminders
as in all the money in the world.

I will think over your orders
and keep my eyes on your ways.

Your rules are my delight.
I will never lose track of your word.

Treat your servant well,
so I can live and keep your word.

Take the cover off my eyes,
so I can see the wonders in your teaching.

I am just a guest on this earth.
Do not keep your commands secret from me.

I am worn out with longing
for your decisions at every hour.

You scold the proud,
the cursed ones who wander from your commands.

Take away their insults and scorn,
for I have held on to your reminders.

Even when rulers sit and plot against me,
your servant thinks about your rules.

Your reminders bring me joy.
They are my advisers.

I lie flat in the dust.
Make me live again, just as you said.

I laid out my life before you, and you replied.
Teach me your rules.

Help me understand what your orders mean,
so I can think about your wonderful works.

I am crying{b} with sadness.
Make me strong, as your word says.

Keep me far from the road of lies,
and kindly give me your teaching.

I have picked the road of loyalty.
I keep your decisions in front of me.

I hold tight to your reminders, Yahweh.
Do not let me end up ashamed.

I will run down the road of your commands,
for you give my heart room to grow.

Yahweh, show me the path of your rules,
and I will follow it to the very end.{c}

Give me understanding, and I will obey your teaching
and follow it with all my heart.

Lead me down the road of your commands,
because that is where I find joy.

Turn my heart to your reminders
and away from love of money.

Turn my eyes from looking at empty things.
Give me life on your path.{d}

Make good your promise to your servant,
the promise that leads people to respect you.

Take away the shame I am afraid of,
because your decisions are good.

Look how much I long for your orders.
Give me life through your goodness.

Yahweh, let your faithful love find me,
and your rescue, as you promised.

Then I can answer people who make fun of me,
because I trust your word.

Never take the true word completely from my mouth,
for I wait for your decisions.

I will obey your teaching without stopping,
forever and ever.

I will walk around free,
because I look for your orders.

I will tell kings about your reminders
and will not be ashamed.

I find joy in your commands,
and I love them.

I reach out to your commands, which I love,
and I think over your rules.

Remember what you promised your servant.
You gave me hope with it.

Here is what comforts me in my pain:
your promise keeps me alive.

Proud people sneer at me again and again,
but I do not leave your teaching.

I think about your decisions from long ago, Yahweh,
and they comfort me.

Anger burns in me at the wicked,
who walk away from your teaching.

Your rules have been my songs
wherever I have stayed as a traveler.

At night I remember your name, Yahweh,
and I follow your teaching.

This is what I have been given:
I get to keep your orders.

Yahweh, you are all I need.
I have vowed to obey your words.

I pleaded for your favor with everything in me.
Show me kindness, just as you promised.

I thought about the road I was on
and turned my feet back to your reminders.

I hurry and do not wait around
to obey your commands.

The wicked have wrapped me in ropes,
but I never forget your teaching.

At midnight I rise to thank you
for your fair decisions.

I am a friend to everyone who respects you,
to all who follow your orders.

Yahweh, the earth is full of your faithful love.
Teach me your rules.

You have done good to your servant,
Yahweh, just as you said.

Teach me good sense and knowledge,
for I trust your commands.

Before I suffered, I wandered off,
but now I obey what you said.

You are good, and goodness is what you do.
Teach me your rules.

Proud people smear me with lies,
but I keep your orders with all my heart.

Their hearts are dull and fat,
but I love your teaching.

It was good for me to suffer,
because it taught me your rules.

The teaching from your mouth is worth more to me
than thousands in silver and gold.

Your hands formed me and made me.
Give me insight, so I can learn your commands.

Those who respect you will see me and cheer,
since my hope is in your word.

Yahweh, I know your decisions are right,
and that you were true to me when you let me suffer.

Let your faithful love comfort me,
just as you promised your servant.

Let your mercy reach me so I can live,
because I love your teaching.

Let the proud be ashamed for twisting the truth to hurt me.
I will think about your orders.

May those who respect you come back to me,
those who know{e} your reminders.

Let my heart be fully loyal to your rules,
so that I am never ashamed.

I am fading as I wait for you to rescue me,
yet I hope in your word.

My eyes grow weary watching for your promise.
I ask, “When will you comfort me?”

I am like a leather bag dried out in smoke,
yet I have not forgotten your rules.

How many days does your servant have?
When will you judge the ones who hunt me?

Proud people have dug holes in my path.
They ignore your teaching.

All your commands can be trusted.
People attack me with lies. Help me!

They nearly wiped me off the earth,
but I did not drop your orders.

Give me life through your faithful love,
and I will obey the reminders from your mouth.

Yahweh, your word
is fixed in heaven forever.

Your faithfulness lasts through every age.
You planted the earth, and it stays put.

Everything stands today because of your decisions,
for all things serve you.

If your teaching had not been my joy,
I would have died in my suffering.

I will not ever forget your orders,
for they are how you gave me life.

I belong to you, so save me.
I have looked to your orders.

The wicked wait to destroy me,
but I focus on your reminders.

I have seen that everything perfect has an end,
but your command has no limit.

How I love your teaching!
I think about it all day long.

Your command makes me smarter than my enemies,
for it never leaves me.

I have more understanding than all my teachers,
since I think over your reminders.

I have more sense than old men,
because I obey your orders.

I keep my feet off every evil road,
so I can obey your word.

I have not turned from your decisions,
because you yourself have taught me.

How sweet your promises taste,
sweeter than honey on my tongue!

Your orders give me understanding,
so I hate every road of lies.

Your word is a lamp that shows my feet the way,
and a light for my path.

I have made a vow, and I will keep it:
to follow your fair decisions.

I am hurting badly.
Yahweh, give me life, as you promised.

Yahweh, accept the praise that I offer freely,
and teach me your decisions.

My life is always in danger,{f}
yet I never forget your teaching.

The wicked have hidden a snare for me,
but I have not drifted from your orders.

Your reminders are mine forever.
They make my heart glad.

I have set my heart on keeping your rules
forever, right to the end.

I hate half-hearted people.
Your teaching is what I love.

You are my hiding place and my shield.
My hope is in your word.

Leave me alone, you evildoers,
so I can follow my God’s commands.

Support me as you pledged, and I will live.
Do not let my hope fade into disgrace.

Hold me up, and I will be safe.
I will always study your rules.

You turn away everyone who wanders from your rules,
because their tricks get them nowhere.

You throw out the wicked of the earth like trash from a fire.
That is why I love your reminders.

My body shakes in fear of you.
I am afraid of your decisions.

I have acted with fairness and goodness.
Do not leave me to the people who hurt me.

Stand up for your servant’s good.
Do not let proud people crush me.

My eyes are tired from looking for your rescue
and for your true promise.

Treat your servant with your faithful love,
and teach me your rules.

I am your servant, so give me understanding,
and I will know your reminders.

It is time for you to act, Yahweh,
because people have broken your teaching.

That is why I love your commands
even more than gold, more than pure gold.

That is why I say all your orders are right in every way.{g}
I hate every road of lies.

Your reminders are wonderful,
so I obey them.

When your words open up, they bring light.
They make simple people wise.

My mouth hangs open, and I pant,
because I ache for your commands.

Turn my way and show kindness,
as you do for all who love your name.

Make my steps steady with your promise,
and do not let any sin be my boss.

Buy me back from people who push me around,
and I will obey your orders.

Smile on your servant,
and teach me your rules.

Streams of tears run from my eyes
because people do not follow your teaching.

You are right, Yahweh,
and your decisions are fair.

The reminders you gave are right
and completely trustworthy.

My passion has drained me,
since my enemies have forgotten what you say.

Your promise has been tested and proved,
and your servant loves it.

I am small and looked down on,
but I have not forgotten your orders.

Your goodness lasts forever,
and your teaching is true.

Trouble and pain have caught up with me,
but your commands make me happy.

Your reminders are right for all time.
Give me understanding, and I will live.

I cry out from the bottom of my heart. Answer me, Yahweh!
I will obey your rules.

I call to you, so save me,
and I will follow your reminders.

I wake before the sun is up and cry for help.
I wait for your words.{h}

I stay awake through the night hours
to think about your promise.

Hear my voice because of your faithful love.
Yahweh, give me life because of your justice.

Those with evil plans are coming close,
but they are far from your teaching.

Yet you are near, Yahweh,
and every command of yours is true.

Long ago I found in your reminders
that you built them to last forever.

See my trouble and rescue me,
since I have not forgotten your teaching.

Argue my case and buy me back.
Give me life, as you promised.

Rescue is far from the wicked,
because they do not look for your rules.

Your mercy is great, Yahweh.
Give me life by your decisions.

Many people chase me and fight me,
but I have not turned from your reminders.

I look at people who break faith, and I am sickened,
since they ignore your word.

See how I love your orders.
Yahweh, give me life because of your faithful love.

All your word added together is true,
and each of your fair decisions lasts forever.

Rulers hound me with no cause,
but my heart trembles at your words.{i}

I am glad over your promise
like someone who finds a huge pile of treasure.

I hate and cannot stand lies,
but I love your teaching.

Seven times a day I praise you
for your fair decisions.

Those who love your teaching have great peace,
and nothing trips them up.

I am waiting for your rescue, Yahweh,
and I do what you command.

I keep your reminders,
and I love them deeply.

I have kept your orders and your reminders,
because you see everything I do.

Let my cry reach you, Yahweh.
Help me understand, as your word says.

Let my plea come before you.
Save me, as you promised.

Praise will pour from my lips,
because you teach me your rules.

Let my tongue sing about your promise,
because every command you give is right.

Have your hand ready to help me,
since I have chosen your orders.

I long for you to save me, Yahweh,
and your teaching makes me happy.

Let me live and praise you,
and let your decisions help me.

I have wandered like a lost sheep. Come and find your servant,
because I have not forgotten your commands.

notes.text: Psalm 119 is an acrostic. Each set of eight verses starts with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet. In this book each section is named for its letter. The psalm uses eight main words for God’s word: teaching, reminders, orders, rules, commands, decisions, promise and word.
Hebrew “my soul drips.”
Or “I will keep it as my reward.”
Some copies read “in your word.”
Some Hebrew copies say “those who know.” Others say “and they will know.”
Hebrew “in my palm.” This means my life is in danger.
Some copies read “all your orders about everything I consider right.”
Hebrew has “your words.” Some copies say “your word.”
The Hebrew can mean “stands in awe” or “trembles at.”

subheads.41: Waw — Let Your Love Reach Me
subheads.49: Zayin — Your Promise Gives Me Hope
subheads.81: Kaph — I Am Worn Out Waiting
subheads.97: Mem — How I Love Your Teaching
