subheads.145: Qoph — I Cry Out at Dawn

verses.text:
In my trouble I called to Yahweh,
and he answered me.

Yahweh, save me from lying lips
and from tongues that cheat.

What will he do to you,
and what more will he add, you cheating tongue?

He will use a soldier’s sharp arrows
and burning coals from the broom bush.

How sad for me that I live as a stranger in Meshech,
and camp among the tents of Kedar!{b}

I have lived much too long
among people who hate peace.

Peace is what I want, yet when I talk,
they are ready for war.

notes.text: Hebrew shir hamma’aloth, “a song of ascents” or “steps.” The fifteen Songs of Ascents (Psalms 120–134) were probably sung by pilgrims as they went up to Jerusalem for the yearly festivals.
Meshech was far to the north, and Kedar was in the Arabian desert to the south. Together the two names mean living among foreign, hostile people.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem.{a}

subheads.3: Too Long Among Haters of Peace

verses.text:
I look up toward the mountains.
Who will come to help me?

My help is from Yahweh,
the maker of heaven and earth.

He will not let you slip.
The one who watches over you does not nap.

The one who watches over Israel
never naps and never sleeps.

Yahweh watches over you.
He stands beside you like shade at your right hand.

The sun will not hurt you in the day,
and the moon will not hurt you at night.

Yahweh will keep you safe from every harm.
He will protect your life.

Yahweh will protect you when you leave and when you come home,
now and forever.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem.

subheads.1: Where Does My Help Come From?

verses.text:
I was glad when people said to me,
“Let’s go to Yahweh’s house.”

We are here at last,
inside your gates, Jerusalem.

Jerusalem is a city built
with its houses packed close together.

Thrones for judging sit there,
the thrones of David’s family.

Pray for the peace of Jerusalem.{b}
“May everyone who loves you be safe.

May peace live inside your walls
and safety in your towers.”

For my family and my friends I say,
“May peace be with you.”

For the sake of the house of Yahweh our God,
I will work for your good.

notes.text: See Deuteronomy 16:16.
The name Jerusalem sounds like the Hebrew words for “city of peace.” The prayer plays on the sound of the name.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem. By David.

subheads.1: Let Us Go to Yahweh’s House

verses.text:
I lift my eyes to you,
the one who sits on a throne in heaven.

Servants watch their master’s hand.
A maid watches her mistress’s hand.
In the same way we watch Yahweh our God,
until he shows us mercy.

Show us mercy, Yahweh, show us mercy,
for we have had more than enough of being looked down on.

We have had far too much
of the sneers of comfortable people
and the scorn of the proud.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem.

verses.text:
“What if Yahweh had not stood with us?”
Let Israel say it.

“What if Yahweh had not stood with us
when enemies rose against us?

They would have gulped us down alive
in their blazing anger.

A flood would have swept us away.
A river would have poured over us.

Yes, raging water
would have gone over our heads.”

Praise Yahweh!
He kept their teeth from ripping us to pieces.

We got away like a bird
from a hunter’s trap.
The trap snapped,
and we flew free.

Our help is in the name of Yahweh,
who made heaven and earth.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem. By David.

subheads.1: If Yahweh Had Not Been on Our Side

verses.text:
Those who trust Yahweh are like Mount Zion.
It cannot be moved. It stays forever.

Mountains stand all around Jerusalem,
and Yahweh stands all around his people,
now and always.

The rule of the wicked will not remain
over the land given to good people.
Otherwise, good people might also turn to evil.

Yahweh, be good to those who are good,
to people with honest hearts.

But those who turn to crooked ways,
Yahweh will march off with the evildoers.
Peace be on Israel.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem.

verses.text:
When Yahweh brought Zion’s people home,{a}
it was like a dream.

Our mouths filled with laughter,
and our tongues with songs of joy.
People in other nations said,
“Yahweh has done great things for them.”

Yahweh did great things for us,
and we were glad.

Bring our people back,{b} Yahweh,
like streams in the Negev desert.{c}

People who plant seed with tears
will cut the crop with shouts of joy.

Whoever goes out crying,
carrying seed to plant,
will come home singing for joy,
carrying armfuls of grain.

notes.text: Or “When Yahweh turned the fortunes of Zion.” The Hebrew can mean bringing people back from exile or restoring good fortune.
Or “Restore our fortunes.”
The Negev is the dry land in southern Israel. Winter rains turn its dry stream beds into rushing water.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem.

verses.text:
If Yahweh does not build the house,
the builders work for nothing.
If Yahweh does not guard the city,
the guards stay up for nothing.

It is pointless to rise early
and go to bed late,
sweating for your daily bread,
when he gives rest to those he loves.{a}

Yahweh gives children as a gift,
a reward from him.

Sons born in a man’s younger years
are like arrows in a warrior’s hand.

How happy is the man
who has a quiver packed with them.
They will not lose face
when they argue with enemies at the city gate.

notes.text: Or “he gives to his loved one even while he sleeps.” The Hebrew can be read both ways.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem. By Solomon.

verses.text:
Happy is everyone who respects Yahweh
and lives by his ways.

You will enjoy the food your hands have grown.
You will be happy and well off.

Your wife in your home will be like a vine
loaded with grapes.
Your children around your table
will be like fresh olive shoots.

This is how a person is blessed
who respects Yahweh.

May Yahweh bless you from Zion,
and may you see Jerusalem do well
for as long as you live.

May you live to see your grandchildren.
Peace be on Israel.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem.

subheads.1: Happy Are Those Who Respect Yahweh

verses.text:
“Since I was young, they have attacked me again and again,”
let Israel say.

“Since I was young, they have attacked me again and again,
but they have never beaten me.

Farmers plowed on my back.
They cut long lines in it.”{a}

Yahweh does what is right.
He has cut me loose from the ropes of the wicked.

May all who hate Zion
be shamed and driven back.

May they be like grass on a roof,
which dries up before anyone can pull it,

so that no harvester can fill his hand with it,
and no one gathering grain can take any home.

May people walking by never say to them,
“Yahweh bless you.
We bless you in Yahweh’s name.”

notes.text: This describes the whip marks of slavery or hardship as if they were plowed rows on Israel’s back.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem.

verses.text: From the deep I call to you, Yahweh.

Lord, hear me.
Listen closely
to my cry for mercy.

If you, Yah, kept a list of wrongs,
Lord, who could face you?

But with you there is forgiveness,
so people will respect you.

I wait for Yahweh. All of me waits,
and I hope for his word.

I wait for the Lord
more than night guards wait for morning,
yes, more than night guards wait for morning.

Israel, hope in Yahweh.
With Yahweh there is faithful love,
and he has plenty of power to buy people back.

He will buy Israel back
from all its sins.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem.

verses.text:
Yahweh, my heart is not proud,
and I do not look down on others.
I do not chase big things
or things too wonderful for me.

Instead, I have made myself calm and quiet,
like a little child who has been nursed.
Like that child, I am at peace inside.

Israel, hope in Yahweh,
now and forever.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem. By David.

verses.text:
Yahweh, remember David
and all the hard times he went through.

He made a promise to Yahweh,
a vow to the Mighty One of Jacob.

“I will not walk into my home
or climb into my bed.

I will not let my eyes close in sleep
or let my eyelids rest,

until I find a place for Yahweh,
a home for the Mighty One of Jacob.”

We heard about the ark in Ephrathah,{a}
and found it in the fields of Jaar.{b}

“Let us go to where he lives.
Let us bow down at his footstool.”

Get up, Yahweh, and come to your resting place,
you and the ark that shows your power.

Let your priests be dressed in goodness,
and let your loyal people sing for joy.

For the sake of your servant David,
do not turn away your chosen king.{c}

Yahweh made David a true promise,
one he will not take back:
“A child of your own body
I will place on your throne.

If your sons keep my agreement
and the reminders I teach them,
their sons will also sit
on your throne forever.”

Yahweh has chosen Zion.
He wanted it as his home.

“This is where I will rest forever.
I will live here, since this is what I wanted.

I will fill her with plenty of food.
I will feed her poor until they are full.

I will dress her priests in rescue,
and her loyal people will sing loudly for joy.

Here I will make a strong king grow for David.
I have set a lamp for the one I anointed.

I will wrap his enemies in shame,
but his crown will shine on his head.”

notes.text: Ephrathah is the area around Bethlehem. Some think it also names a place near Kiriath Jearim.
Jaar is short for Kiriath Jearim, where the ark stayed for many years. See 1 Samuel 7:1–2.
Hebrew mashiach, “anointed one,” a person poured with oil to be king.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem.

verses.text:
How good and pleasant it is
when family members live together in peace.

It is like fine oil on a head
that runs down onto the beard,
onto Aaron’s beard,
and down onto the neck of his robe.

It is like Hermon’s morning dew
falling on the hills of Zion.
For that is where Yahweh ordered the blessing,
life that lasts forever.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem. By David.

verses.text:
Come and bless Yahweh,
all you servants of Yahweh,
who serve in Yahweh’s house at night.

Lift up your hands toward the holy place
and bless Yahweh.

May Yahweh bless you from Zion,
the one who made heaven and earth.

chapters.title: A song for the climb up to Jerusalem.

verses.text:
Hallelujah!
Praise Yahweh’s name.
Praise him, you servants of Yahweh,

you who stand in Yahweh’s house,
in the yards of our God’s house.

Praise Yah, because Yahweh is good.
Sing about his name, because it is lovely.

Yah chose Jacob to be his own,
and Israel to be his special treasure.

I know how great Yahweh is,
and that our Lord outranks every god.

Yahweh does anything he pleases
in the skies and on the earth,
in the oceans and all their depths.

Clouds rise at his command from the far ends of the earth.
He makes lightning flash for the storm
and pulls the wind from his storerooms.

He killed the oldest son in every Egyptian home,
and the firstborn of their animals.

In your land, Egypt, he showed signs and wonders
against Pharaoh and all his officials.

He defeated many nations
and put mighty kings to death:

Sihon, king of the Amorites,
Og, king of Bashan,
and every ruler of Canaan.

He turned their land over to Israel,
to belong to his people for good.

Yahweh, your name lasts forever.
Yahweh, you will be remembered in every generation.

Yahweh will take his people’s side
and take pity on his servants.{a}

The idols of the nations are only silver and gold,
the product of human craft.

They have mouths but say nothing.
They have eyes but see nothing.

They have ears, but they cannot hear.
There is no breath in their mouths.

Their makers will turn out just like them,
and so will everyone who counts on them.{b}

People of Israel, bless Yahweh.
Family of Aaron, bless Yahweh.

Family of Levi, bless Yahweh.
All who respect Yahweh, bless Yahweh.

Bless Yahweh from Zion,
he who lives in Jerusalem.
Hallelujah!

notes.text: Compare Deuteronomy 32:36.
Compare Psalm 115:4–8.

subheads.5: Our Lord Is Above All Gods

verses.text:
Thank Yahweh, because he is good.
His faithful love lasts forever.{a}

Thank the God over all gods.
His faithful love lasts forever.

Thank the Lord over all lords.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He alone does great wonders.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He made the heavens with understanding.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He spread the earth out over the waters.
His faithful love lasts forever.
He made the great lamps of the sky.
He set the sun over the day.
He set the moon and stars over the night.

He killed the oldest sons of Egypt.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He led Israel out of that land.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He did it with a strong hand and a stretched-out arm.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He cut the Red Sea in two.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He walked Israel through the middle of it.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He tossed Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea.
His faithful love lasts forever.
He guided his people across the wilderness.

He defeated great kings.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He killed powerful kings.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He beat Sihon, king of the Amorites.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He beat Og, king of Bashan.
His faithful love lasts forever.
He handed their land over as a gift.

He gave it to Israel, his servant.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He remembered us when we were down.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He pulled us away from our enemies.
His faithful love lasts forever.

He gives food to every living creature.
His faithful love lasts forever.

Thank the God of heaven.
His faithful love lasts forever.

notes.text: The refrain “His faithful love lasts forever” is repeated in every verse. It was probably sung by the people after each line the leader read.

verses.text:
Beside Babylon’s rivers
we sat and wept
as we remembered Zion.

We hung our harps
on the poplar trees{a} there.

The people who had taken us captive
asked us for songs.
Those who laughed at us demanded joyful music.
They said, “Give us a tune from Zion!”

How could we sing Yahweh’s song
on foreign ground?

If I ever forget you, Jerusalem,
may my right hand lose its skill.

May my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth
if I do not remember you,
if I do not rank Jerusalem
above my greatest joy.

Yahweh, hold the Edomites responsible
for the day Jerusalem fell.
They yelled, “Tear it down!
Tear it down to its foundations!”

Babylon, you are headed for ruin.
Happy is the one who pays you back
for the harm you did to us.

Blessed is the one who grabs your infants
and smashes them on the rocks.{b}

notes.text: Or “willow trees.”
This verse is a hard cry of anger from a people who had seen their own babies killed (compare 2 Kings 8:12 and Isaiah 13:16). It is a prayer for justice, not an order for us to follow.

verses.text:
I thank you with all my heart.
In front of the gods{a} I sing to you.

I bow toward your holy temple
and give thanks to your name
for your faithful love and truth,
because you raised your word even above your name.

On the day I called, you answered.
You gave me courage and made my spirit strong.

Every king on earth will thank you, Yahweh,
when they hear what you have said.

They will sing about Yahweh’s ways,
because Yahweh’s glory is great.

Yahweh is high above, yet he sees the humble.
The proud he knows only from far off.

Even if I walk through the middle of trouble,
you keep me alive.
You reach out your hand against my angry enemies,
and your right hand saves me.

Yahweh will finish what he started for me.
Yahweh, your faithful love lasts forever.
Do not give up on the work of your hands.

notes.text: Or “before the angels” or “before the false gods.” The Hebrew word is elohim.

chapters.title: By David.

subheads.1: I Thank You with All My Heart

verses.text: Yahweh, you have studied me, and you know me.

You know if I am sitting or standing.
From far off you understand what I am thinking.

You trace my travels and my times of rest.
You are familiar with all I do.

You know my words
before they even reach my tongue, Yahweh.

You are behind me and in front of me.
You have put your hand on me.

This kind of knowing is too wonderful for me.{a}
It is far above what I can grasp.

Where in the world could I hide from your Spirit?
Where could I flee from you?

If I rise to the skies, you are there.
If I make the grave my bed, you are present too.

If I fly off on the wings of the sunrise
and land at the far end of the sea,

even there your hand will guide me,
and your right hand will hold me.

If I say, “The dark will cover me,
and the light around me will turn to night,”

To you even the dark is not dark.
Night shines like day,
for dark and light are alike to you.

You made the deepest parts of me.{b}
You knit me together inside my mother.

I praise you, because I am made in an amazing and wonderful way.{c}
Your works are wonderful. I know that well.

You saw me while I was still unformed.
Every day of my life was written in your book
before even one day had come.

Your thoughts are so precious to me, God.
How many they are!

Were I to count them, there would be more than sand.
When I wake, you are still beside me.

God, how I wish you would put the wicked to death!
Violent people, stay away from me!

They speak against you with evil plans.
Your enemies misuse your name.{e}

Yahweh, how could I not hate those who hate you?
How could I not despise those who stand against you?

I hate them with total hatred.
They are my enemies too.

Search me, God, and know my heart.
Test me and know what worries me.

See if there is any hurtful way in me,
and lead me on the road that lasts forever.

notes.text: Or “Such knowledge is beyond me.”
Hebrew “kidneys.” The Hebrews saw the kidneys as the place of deep feelings.
Some copies read “You are to be feared, for I am wonderfully made.”
This is a poetic way to say the mother’s womb, as in Job 1:21.
The Hebrew here is hard to read. Some copies say “your cities.”

chapters.title: For the music director. By David. A psalm.

verses.text:
Rescue me, Yahweh, from wicked people.
Keep me safe from violent men,

who plan wicked things in their hearts
and stir up fights every day.

They sharpen their tongues like snakes.
Poison of vipers is under their lips. Selah{a}

Yahweh, keep me from the grip of the wicked.
Shield me from men of violence
who plot to trip me up.

Proud men have buried a trap for me, with cords.
They have stretched out a net along my path
and placed snares to catch me. Selah

I tell Yahweh, “You are my God.”
Hear my cry for mercy, Yahweh.

Yahweh my Lord, my mighty rescuer,
you shielded my head when the fight came.

Yahweh, do not give the wicked what they crave.
Do not let their scheme work,
or they will boast. Selah

As for those who surround me,
let the trouble their own lips made cover their heads.

Let slanderers find no place to stand on the earth.
Let disaster chase violent men
and knock them down.

I know{c} that Yahweh will defend those who suffer,
and he will see justice done for the poor.

Surely the good will thank your name,
and honest people will live near you.

notes.text: Hebrew Selah. See the note on 3:2.
Some copies read “Let burning coals fall on them.” Others say “let them be shaken down on them.”
Some Hebrew copies say “I know.” Others say “you know.”

chapters.title: For the music director. A psalm of David.

subheads.9: Let Their Own Words Fall on Them

verses.text:
Yahweh, I am calling to you. Come fast!
Hear my voice as I cry out to you.

Let my prayer rise to you like incense,
and my raised hands like the evening offering.

Put a guard on my mouth, Yahweh.
Watch the door of my lips.

Do not let my heart drift toward evil
or join in wicked acts
with people who do wrong.
Keep me from tasting their rich foods.

Let a good person strike me. That is kindness.
Let him correct me. It is like oil on my head,
and my head will not refuse it.
But my prayer stands against the evil they do.

Their rulers will be thrown down the side of a cliff,
and then people will hear that my words were kind.

Like wood that is split and chopped on the ground,
our bones lie scattered at the grave’s edge.{a}

But my eyes are fixed on you, Yahweh my Lord.
I run to you for safety. Do not let me die.

Keep me away from the trap they laid for me
and from the nets of evil people.

Let the wicked fall into their own nets,
while I walk safely past.

notes.text: Hebrew Sheol, the place of the dead. Verses 5–7 are hard to read in Hebrew, and readers differ on their meaning.

chapters.title: A psalm of David.

verses.text:
I cry out loud to Yahweh.
I beg Yahweh loudly for mercy.

I pour out my complaint to him.
I tell him what is wrong.

When my spirit grows weak,
you still know my way.
Along the road I travel
someone has hidden a trap.

Look at my right side and see.
No one pays attention to me.
I have nowhere to hide,
and nobody cares if I live.

I cry out to you, Yahweh.
I say, “You are my hiding place,
my share in the land of the living.”

Listen to my cry,
because I am very low.
Rescue me from those who hunt me down,
for they are too strong for me.

Free me from this prison,
and I will give thanks to your name.
The good will crowd around me
because you will treat me well.

notes.text: See 1 Samuel 22:1 or 24:3. A maskil is probably a song of teaching or skill. See the note on 32:1.

chapters.title: A maskil of David, when he was in the cave.{a} A prayer.

verses.text:
Yahweh, hear my prayer.
Pay attention to my pleas.
Reply to me because you are true and fair.

Do not put your servant on trial,
because no one alive is right in your eyes.

The enemy has chased me down.
He has pushed my life into the dust.
He makes me sit in the dark like those long dead.

So my spirit is weak inside me.
My heart is numb.

I remember the old days.
I think about everything you have done.
I think over the work of your hands.

I stretch out my hands to you.
I am as thirsty for you as dry ground. Selah

Hurry and answer me, Yahweh.
My strength is gone.
Do not turn away from me,
or I will be like the dead in the pit.

Let me hear about your faithful love at dawn,
for I trust you.
Show me which road to take,
for I lift my life up to you.

Yahweh, take me away from my enemies.
I hide myself in you.{a}

Teach me to do things your way,
because you are my God.
May your good Spirit guide me
over level ground.

For the honor of your name, Yahweh, let me live.
In your goodness, pull me out of this trouble.

In your faithful love, wipe out my enemies
and destroy all who are attacking me,
for I am your servant.

notes.text: Some copies read “I have hidden myself with you.” Others read “to you I have fled.”

chapters.title: A psalm of David.

verses.text:
Bless Yahweh, my rock,
who teaches my hands to fight
and my fingers to battle.

He is my faithful love{a} and my fort,
my high tower and my rescuer,
my shield, the one I run to.
He makes the nations{b} bow to me.

Yahweh, why do you even notice people?
Why do you give a thought to human beings?

A person is like a puff of breath.
His days are like a shadow passing by.

Yahweh, tip the heavens and come down.
Touch the mountains so they smoke.

Send lightning and scatter my enemies.
Shoot your arrows and make them run.

Their mouths speak lies,
and their right hands make false promises.

God, I will sing you a new song.
I will play for you on a harp with ten strings.

You give kings their wins.
You rescue your servant David
from the evil sword.

Pull me out and save me
from the hands of foreigners,
whose mouths tell lies,
and whose right hands swear false oaths.

May our sons be like young plants
that have grown tall while they are still in their youth.
May our daughters be like corner pillars
carved to decorate a palace.

May our barns overflow
with every kind of crop.
May our flocks grow by thousands,
by tens of thousands in our pastures.

Happy are the people who live like this.
Happy are the people whose God is Yahweh.

notes.text: Or “my loyal one.” Some copies read “my people” in verse 2.
Some Hebrew copies read “peoples.” Others read “my people.”
Or “may our cattle be well fed.” The Hebrew is not clear.

chapters.title: By David.

subheads.12: Happy Are the People Whose God Is Yahweh

verses.text:
I will lift you high, my God and King.
I will praise your name forever and ever.

Every day I will bless you
and praise your name always and beyond.

Yahweh is great and worthy of all praise.
His greatness is too deep for anyone to measure.

One generation will tell the next about your works.
They will tell of your mighty acts.

I will think about your glorious splendor
and about your wonderful works.{b}

People will tell of your awesome power,
and I will announce your greatness.

They will spread the story of your great goodness
and sing happily about your fairness.

Yahweh is kind and full of mercy.
He is slow to get angry and rich in faithful love.

Yahweh is good to everyone.
His mercy covers all he has made.

Everything you made will thank you, Yahweh,
and your loyal people will bless you.

They will describe the glory of your kingdom
and speak of your power,

so that all people will know his mighty acts
and the glorious splendor of his kingdom.

Your kingdom lasts through every age,
and your rule goes on through every generation.

Yahweh holds up all who are falling
and lifts up all who are bent over.

All eyes look to you,
and you feed them when it is time.
You open your hand
and give every living thing what it wants.

You open your hand
and give every living thing what it wants.

Yahweh is fair in everything he does
and loyal in all his works.

Yahweh is close to all who call to him,
to all who call to him honestly.

He gives those who respect him what they long for.
He hears their cry and saves them.

Yahweh watches over all who love him,
but he will destroy all the wicked.

My mouth will speak the praise of Yahweh.
May all that lives bless his holy name
for ever and ever.

notes.text: Psalm 145 is an acrostic. Each verse begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet. The line for the letter nun is missing in most Hebrew copies. Some old copies and the Greek and Syriac add it after verse 13: “Yahweh is faithful in all he says and loyal in all he does.”
Some copies read “I will tell of your wonderful works.”

chapters.title: A song of praise. By David.{a}

verses.text:
Hallelujah!{a}
My soul, praise Yahweh.

I will praise Yahweh all my life.
I will sing to my God while I still breathe.

Do not put your trust in princes,
in mere humans, who cannot save you.

When their breath leaves them, they return to the dust.
On that same day their plans are gone.

Happy are those whose helper is Jacob’s God,
and whose hope is in Yahweh their God,

who made heaven and earth,
the sea, and everything in them,
and who keeps his word forever.

He defends those who are wronged.
He feeds the hungry.
Yahweh frees prisoners.

Yahweh opens the eyes of the blind.
Yahweh lifts up those who are bent low.
Yahweh loves those who do right.

Yahweh watches over foreigners.
He takes care of orphans and widows,
but he turns the way of the wicked upside down.

Yahweh will be king forever.
Zion, your God will rule in every generation.
Hallelujah!

notes.text: Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” See the note on 104:35. Psalms 146–150 each begin and end with this call, and are called the final Hallel.

subheads.5: Happy Are Those Who Hope in Yahweh

verses.text:
Hallelujah!
How good it is to sing to our God.
It is pleasant, and praise is the right thing.

Yahweh is rebuilding Jerusalem.
He is gathering the people of Israel who were driven away.

He heals those with broken hearts
and wraps up their wounds.

He knows how many stars there are.
He calls each one by name.

Our Lord is great and has huge power.
No one can measure his understanding.

Yahweh lifts up the humble,
but he knocks the wicked to the ground.

Sing thanks to Yahweh.
Play on the harp for our God.

He fills the sky with clouds.
He prepares rain for the earth.
He grows grass on the hills.

He feeds the animals,
and the baby ravens when they cry out.

He is not impressed by the strength of horses
or by the legs of a runner.

Yahweh is pleased with those who respect him,
those who wait for his faithful love.

Praise Yahweh, Jerusalem.
Praise your God, Zion.

He has made the bars on your gates strong
and has blessed the children inside your walls.

He keeps your borders peaceful
and fills you with the best wheat.

He sends out his order to the earth,
and his word runs fast.

He spreads snow like a wool blanket
and scatters frost like ashes.

He throws down ice like crumbs of bread.
Who can stand against his cold?

He sends out his word, and the ice melts.
He lets his wind blow, and the waters run.

He gave his word{a} to Jacob,
his rules and decisions to Israel.

No other nation has been treated this way.
They do not know his decisions.
Hallelujah!

notes.text: Some copies read “his words.”

verses.text:
Hallelujah!
Praise Yahweh from the heavens.
Praise him from the heights.

Praise him, every one of his angels.
Praise him, every one of his armies.{a}

Praise him, sun and moon.
Praise him, all you shining stars.

Praise him, farthest heavens,
and you waters over the sky.

Let them praise Yahweh’s name,
for he gave the order and they were made.

He placed them there for good.
He set a boundary they cannot cross.

Praise Yahweh from the earth,
you sea monsters and all deep waters,

fire and hail, snow and fog,
and stormy winds that do what he says,

mountains and every hill,
fruit trees and every cedar,

wild animals and all farm animals,
crawling creatures and flying birds,

Kings of the earth and every nation,
princes and all earthly judges,

young men and young women,
old people and children together.

Let them praise Yahweh’s name,
for his name alone is lifted up.
His glory rises over earth and heaven.

He gave his people a mighty king.{b}
All his loyal ones have reason to praise,
the people of Israel who are close to him.
Hallelujah!

notes.text: Or “all his heavenly armies.” This means the angels.
Hebrew “he raised a horn.” A horn stands for strength.

verses.text:
Hallelujah!
Sing Yahweh a new song,
praise him where his loyal people meet.

Let Israel be glad in the one who made them.
Let the people of Zion cheer for their King.

Let them praise his name with dancing
and play music for him with tambourine and harp.

Yahweh enjoys his people.
He crowns the humble with rescue.

Let his loyal people rejoice and be glorious.
Let them sing for joy on their beds.

Let praise to God fill their mouths,
and a two-edged sword be in their hands,

to bring payback on the nations
and punishment on the peoples,

to tie up their kings with chains
and their leaders with iron cuffs,

to carry out the judgment already written.
This is an honor for all his loyal people.
Hallelujah!

subheads.4: Yahweh Takes Joy in His People

verses.text:
Praise him for his mighty acts.
Praise him for his great, great greatness.

Praise him with a loud ram’s horn.
Praise him with a lute and a harp.

Praise him with tambourine and dancing.
Praise him with strings and flute.

Praise him with crashing cymbals.
Praise him with loud, ringing cymbals.

Let everything that breathes praise Yah.
Hallelujah!{b}

notes.text: Hebrew raqia, the dome of the sky. See Genesis 1:6.
Hebrew hallelu-yah, “Praise Yah!” This final psalm ends Book Five and the whole book of Psalms with a great shout of praise.
